## Jameela

### 1. Summary

Jameela is a priestess of Undeath, Garth Larosse's most trusted subordinate, tall and elegant, capable and quick to learn. She helps lead the undead army in Cardinas and the desert, and dies fighting Taika when the priesthood collapses.

### 2. Facts

- **First impression**: a "tall, beautiful woman" with long legs, whose addition to Garth's group left him "almost sad to have given up his flesh"; "capable and intelligent, eager and quick to learn", the opposite of another priest he was forced to bring (Book 10, Ch88 L65).
- **Dress**: an elegant combat robe and heavy boots (Book 11, Ch24 L28).
- **Garth's feelings**: Garth feels a longing for her despite his unliving body but never acts on it, "not allowing himself such a lack of discipline" (Book 11, Ch24 L28).
- **Knowledge of Hero**: she says she has "never seen anyone who has drunk from the Cup of Heroes" and reads it as Hero's miracle at the brink of defeat (Book 10, Ch88 L70).
- **Before the god**: she and Garth drop to their knees when Undeath appears as a living man in black robes with empty sockets and a crimson spark (Book 10, Ch88 L76), and she bows to Undeath and then Garth (Book 10, Ch88 L97).
- **In battle**: she silences a skeleton's communication magic (Book 10, Ch91 L63), watches the divine giants clash (Book 10, Ch92 L46) and points out that crushing the undead at the wall will cost time to replenish (Book 10, Ch92 L51).
- **Perception**: she warns "He's not bluffing, High Priest... The world feels wrong, somehow. Like standing on a frozen lake as the ice starts to crack" (Book 10, Ch92 L84).
- **Intelligence work**: she extracts what she can about Asano from prisoners, who say his aura is like a gold-ranker's in strength and coverage (Book 11, Ch24 L43).
- **Negotiation with Boris**: in the desert she tells Boris "You are not in a position to negotiate" and "You're bluffing... You want Asano dead and he knows it" (Book 11, Ch26 L20, L26).
- **Spotting the enemy**: she is the first to point out two strange floating vehicles speeding across the desert (Book 11, Ch27 L69).
- **Death**: "One of the final priests to die was Jameela, Garth's most trusted subordinate. She refused to go down easy... her beauty destroyed by Taika's fists and her unwillingness to accept that her cause was lost" (Book 11, Ch32 L79).

### 3. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 10**: joins Garth's group; the siege of Cardinas (Book 10, Ch88-92).
- **Book 11**: the desert campaign and the fall of the priesthood (Book 11, Ch24-32).

### 4. Roleplay notes

Brisk, intelligent and unsentimental: she reads a battlefield and an opponent quickly and keeps her devotion practical.

- Says when the task is complete "the price is paid. Zithis Carrow Vayel will have fulfilled his debt to us" (Book 10, Ch15 L9).

### 5. Background

- One of the Council of Kings (Book 12, Ch33 L51-55).

- **Jason**: Jason says Muskar sees danger only for those he cares about, namely Jason himself (Book 13, Ch1003 L26).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Indulgent, vain and sharp when crossed. Cue: "the price is paid."

## Jason Asano

### 1. Summary

Jason Asano is the series' protagonist: an Australian from the coastal town of Casselton Beach who, at twenty-three, is pulled across the cosmos to Pallimustus by a failed summoning. He becomes an affliction specialist, a bronze-, silver- and gold-rank adventurer, a king of his own astral kingdom, and finally the administrator of the System that every essence user in the cosmos sees.

### 2. Appearance

- **On arrival**: he wakes bald and naked in a hedge maze (Book 1, Ch1 L8-10). Seeing himself later, he notes his Japanese facial features, inherited from his father, look even sharper than usual, his face is gaunt, and his bald head and absent eyebrows make him look "manic and unhinged" (Book 1, Ch8 L37). His skin is pale and taut.
- **Why**: his body ceased to exist in the deep astral; his soul, being magical, was given a new body in the way a summoned familiar is (Clive, Book 1, Ch69 L85-107).
- **Later**: his face changes with each rank. At gold his "strange, nebulous eyes" draw attention, though they return to the dark eyes he had at iron when he meets Zara (Book 12, Ch12 L20).
- **Clothing**: from Book 3 he buys a Vitesse-style wardrobe from the tailor Gilbert Bertinelli (Book 3, Ch2 L59-64).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Humour and references**: he jokes constantly and quotes films and television. He tells the Builder it and Knowledge "should get together and play Mario Kart" (Book 3, Ch57 L87); he compares a projected face to Emperor Palpatine (Book 9, Ch6 L17). He says "G'day" and "mate" (Book 1, Ch38 L55; Book 13, Ch1016 L21).
- **Self-deprecation**: "I'm only twenty-three but I've been pretty efficient about squandering my opportunities" (Book 1, Ch25 L43). He does not celebrate his birthday, which falls on 1 April: "It's not a celebratory time. I never liked my birthday anyway" (Book 5, Ch20 L25).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Essences**: Dark, Blood, Sin and the Doom confluence. His attributes are bound as Power (Blood), Speed (Dark), Spirit (Doom) and Recovery (the fourth essence) (Book 1, Ch99 L67-70).
- **Weapons**: a sword, Dread Salvation, an iron-rank growth item of legendary rarity made by Gary (Book 1, Ch56 L49-52), later reforged by Gary with his mentor Virid and with Jason's soul-bond guiding the work (Book 7, Ch2 L73-74), becoming the sword [Hegemon's Will] with the scabbard Hegemon's Dominion (Book 7, Ch54 L108-120); Virid's surname Martine is Book 6, Ch47 L270. Way of the Reaper martial arts (Book 1, Ch52 L7-11). The set Regalia of the Dark Hegemon includes the Amulet of the Dark Guardian (Book 6, Ch4 L29-36).
- **Abilities seen in the text**: Path of Shadows (a shadow-to-shadow teleport at iron, Book 1, Ch22 L120; at bronze a conjured shadow gate on a regional scale to a place already visited, Book 3, Ch29 L22-35; "a range of roughly two hundred kilometres" when he plans to reach Sydney from Casselton, Book 4, Ch1 L67), Midnight Eyes (awakened Book 1, Ch8 L35), Castigate (Book 1, Ch87 L85) and Verdict (Book 1, Ch99 L24), Punition (Book 1, Ch78 L54), Feast of Absolution (Book 1, Ch22 L84) and Gordon's Harbinger of Doom (Book 5, Ch31 L187).
- **Outworlder racial abilities** (Book 1, Ch1 L76-81): Interface, Quest System, Inventory, Map, Astral Affinity and Mysterious Stranger. Mysterious Stranger gives language adaptation, absorption of essences, awakening stones and skill books, and immunity to identification and tracking effects. Astral Affinity increases resistance to dimension effects and astral forces and increases the effect of dimension abilities and transcendent damage.
- **Familiars**: Shade, Colin and Gordon (see `Familiars/Shade.md`, `Familiars/Colin.md` and `Familiars/Gordon.md`, and the hub `Familiars.md`).
- **Titles**: Godless Prophet (Book 2, Ch65 L85), Spirit Warrior (Book 3, Ch21 L149), Indomitable (Book 4, Ch2 L22), Giant Slayer (Book 5, Ch29 L68-72), Reality Hegemon (Book 6, Ch15 L45), Keeper of the Cycle (Book 10, Ch83 L67-73).

### 5. Background

- **Home**: Casselton Beach on the Mid North Coast of New South Wales (Book 4, Ch3 L100). His father Ken is a landscape architect (Book 2, Ch11 L41); his mother Cheryl comes from a large family of mostly rural people (Book 2, Ch20 L18); his older sister Erika and her husband Ian live nearby with their daughter Emi; his brother Kaito and Kaito's wife Amy live next door to his parents' house (notes, Book 4). His uncles are Hiro, the black sheep with minor involvement in organised crime, and Shiro, the favourite (Book 4, Ch1 L66-67).
- **Before Pallimustus**: "a brief stint at university" studying political science (Book 1, Ch7 L26), then Melbourne "the last couple of years" (Book 1, Ch36 L87), seeing little of his family apart from his sister's household (Book 1, Ch52 says only that he had little contact with his family after they fell out), where he is "the cheapest childcare in town" (Book 1, Ch52 L27). He worked as an assistant manager at a retail bulk office supplier (Book 2, Ch14 L35).
- **Birthday**: 1 April (Book 5, Ch20 L24-26).
- **Arrival**: pulled from his bed in late November by Landemere Vane's failed summoning (Book 4, Ch3 L112).

### 6. Timeline of involvement (summary)

- **Books 1-3 (levels 0-1)**: arrives in Greenstone, joins the Adventure Society, forms the team that becomes Team Biscuit, gains Shade, Colin and Gordon, reaches bronze, and dies in the Builder's tower.
- **Books 4-6 (level 2)**: wakes in the old Casselton hospital in early June 2019, reveals magic to his family, rescues Farrah, ranks to silver after the Makassar events, claims transformation zones, is killed by Shako and leaves Earth in autumn 2021.
- **Books 7-9 (level 2)**: returns to Pallimustus as the great surge begins; the One Day War; becomes an astral king (Book 8, Ch65 L85-93); the Battle of Yaresh; takes in messengers.
- **Books 10-11 (level 3)**: the Cardinas expedition, the Death Pact, the Cup of Heroes, the transformation zone, and years inside his own soul fighting great astral beings.
- **Books 12-13 (level 3)**: a gold-rank "prime avatar of an astral nexus" (Book 12, Ch8 L100) who returns to Earth in 2038.

See the Master Timeline for dates.

### 7. Relationships

- **Mentors and early friends**: Rufus, Gary and Farrah; Rufus runs his field assessment (Book 1, Ch38 L45) and guides his first meditation (Book 1, Ch31 L120-133); Farrah trains his perception and aura projection with memory games and other exercises (Book 1, Ch40 L31, L50-52; Book 1, Ch41 L35).
- **Team Biscuit**: Humphrey, Sophie, Belinda, Clive and Neil.
- **Family**: Emi, Kaito (dies in Book 5), Amy, Erika.
- **Familiars**: Shade (a shadow, butler and driver), Colin (an apocalypse leech swarm) and Gordon (an Avatar of Doom); full entries in `Familiars/`.
- **Others**: Dawn, Zara, Anna Tilden, Boris, Knowledge, the Builder.

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

- **Level 2**: he has died four times by Book 6 (the Church of Death's certificate, Book 7, Ch17 L104; the card in Book 10, Ch38 L73); he is an astral king (Book 7, Ch17 L104-105).
- **Level 3**: his transformation into a prime avatar of an astral nexus (Book 12, Ch8 L100-104). Knowledge has been using him as a key part of her plan to invade Earth for half a millennium (Book 13, Ch1015 L78; the plan's origin, Ch1017 L14-15). At the end of Book 13 Umber's ritual is designed to bind his consciousness into the prime avatar, and Jason walks to the standing stones knowingly, promising Knowledge "the next time we meet, Goddess, will be the day you die" (Book 13, Ch1024 L153).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Dry, sarcastic and quick with modern references; polite to rank only when forced. Cue: "Do I have to pay a wizard to identify items?" (Book 1, Ch1 L108). See `../10_Roleplay_Support/Tone_and_Voice.md`.

- Keep the humour first and the substance second; pop-culture references and self-mockery are constant.
- He speaks at length when explaining, then plainly when serious.
- Leave out any claims about his inner moral life that the text does not show; the books show his actions and jokes.

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

## Jory Tillman

### 1. Summary

Jory Tillman is Greenstone's gentle alchemist and clinic-runner, Jason's first friend, and later Belinda's boyfriend. Passionate about making alchemy affordable, he becomes a Healer-backed teacher spreading his methods around the world.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in detail in the lines read; on a mission he puts away his coat and pulls out another one "covered in pockets" (Book 7, Ch4 L25).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Idealist**: "If I can make alchemical products affordable to everyone, not only can it help a huge number of people, but it will open up huge new markets" (Book 1, Ch35 L21).
- **Honest about himself**: technically an adventurer, he is "the first to admit he rarely went on adventures"; his "true calling was alchemy" (Book 1, Ch35 L10).
- **Gentle**: he tells Jason "You have a good day" to a guard and nurses patients with Healer priests (Book 1, Ch35 L57; Book 3, Ch2 L16).
- **Passionate teacher**: "He lit up when talking about his alchemy, and his passion for helping people was wildly appealing" (Book 11, Ch13 L61).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Alchemy**: he brews potions and elixirs from materials he gathers in towns and villages (Book 1, Ch35 L10) and runs an alchemy lab and medical clinic, the Broad Street Clinic (Book 1, Ch35 L63).
- **Miracle potion**: his facility produces the first batch of lesser miracle potions, a thank-you to Jason who funded it (Book 3, Ch16 L81).
- **In a fight**: floating clear orbs and materials from his pockets and belts in the Reaper trials (Book 2, Ch52 L72) and quick to throw enemies overboard on a skyship (Book 7, Ch4 L76).
- **Teaching**: in Book 11 he lectures a group of students on a stage in a hazy hall (Book 11, Ch68 L1403-1418).

### 5. Background

- Member of the Adventure Society and the Alchemist Association (Book 1, Ch36 L28).
- The Healer makes his clinic a sanctuary and the church backs him (Book 3, Ch16 L82); "The Church of the Healer gave him a mandate and funding to spread his methods around the world" (Book 5, Ch43 L94).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1-3**: he finds Jason, patches him up and offers a clinic (Book 1, Ch35); treats Sophie (Book 1, Ch104 L4); the Healer visit (Book 1, Ch95).
- **Book 5-6**: the Healer's mandate; Belinda contacts him through a water link (Book 6, Ch47 L843-844).
- **Book 7**: he is on the skyship to Vitesse with Gary and the team (Book 7, Ch3 L3) and is summoned away by the Church of the Healer (Book 7, Ch16 L6).
- **Book 11-13**: he teaches (Book 11, Ch68 L1411-1461) and joins the healers' discussions on Earth (Book 13, Ch953 L84).

### 7. Relationships

- **Belinda**: her boyfriend (Book 9, Ch21 L32), and the one who sees her cry in the classroom (Book 11, Ch68 L1461).
- **Jason**: first friend; "Jory is such a good friend to you" (Book 2, Ch1 L77).
- **Neil and the Healer's people**: they work together at the clinic (Book 3, Ch69 L859-860).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

The Healer's direct support is one reason the clinic is protected (Book 3, Ch16 L82).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Kind, enthusiastic and slightly flustered by combat; talk of alchemy makes him bright. Cue: "If I can make alchemical products affordable to everyone..."

## Kaito Asano

### 1. Summary

Kaito Asano is Jason's older brother, a year his senior, married to Amy, with two daughters, Hana and Jace. Easy-going and socially skilled, he is the "well-received original" Jason grew up in the shadow of. In Book 4 he reconnects with Jason, in Book 5 he flies a helicopter with Network defectors against the vampires, and he dies in Berlin.

### 2. Appearance

- Jason's face is more angular than his brother's; Kaito has a "signature easy-going smile" that Jason spent years learning to copy (Book 4, Ch25 L44).
- At a party he wears a pale suit and pastel shirt (Book 4, Ch26 L45).
- Jason's resemblance to him grows with each rank, until Jason stops begrudging it after Kaito's death (Book 13, Ch950 L33).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Socially adroit**: Jason says he never had "Kaito's skill for getting along" (Book 2, Ch11 L61).
- **The favourite**: their parents "got Kaito, so they were willing to put up with me" (Book 4, Ch7 L11).
- **Casual**: he greets the family meeting with "G'day... We're arrived for the mysterious family meeting" (Book 4, Ch27 L55).
- **Dry on pop culture**: his knowledge of classic pop culture "appeared to begin and end with Miami Vice" (Book 4, Ch26 L45).
- **Warm with his children**: he leads Hana by the hand and carries Jace (Book 4, Ch24 L101).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- After Jason's return he joins the Network-defector combat team with Asya and Greg (Book 5, Ch44 L17).
- He flies drones to sweep the ruins of a town (Book 5, Ch18 L83) and owns the helicopter Jason and Akari ride in (Book 5, Ch14 L37).

### 5. Background

- A year older than Jason; the "well-received original" at school, so Jason felt like "a disappointing rehash" (Book 2, Ch11 L65).
- He and Amy bought her parents' house next door to Jason's family (Book 4, Ch3 L133).
- He and Amy's relationship caused the fallout that left Jason dropping out of university; Jason did not want details (Book 4, Ch26 L47-50).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 4**: Jason sees his contact appear on the interface (Book 4, Ch3 L126) and sees the home he shares with Amy (Book 4, Ch3 L133); Erika and Kaito discuss Amy and Jason (Book 4, Ch24 L101-126); the family reunion (Book 4, Ch27 L55-70); the helicopter check with Erika (Book 4, Ch71 L62).
- **Book 5**: the strike team and helicopter crew (Book 5, Ch14 L37-49); dies in Berlin with Asya and Greg (Book 5, Ch51 L40); Jason at the funeral: "died for something that truly matters. To give his children a future" (Book 5, Ch52 L20).
- **Later**: Amy and the girls are Book 13 family (Book 13, Ch950 L29; Book 13, Ch1023 L33); his death is the grief behind Emi's uncle (Book 11, Ch68 L828).

### 7. Relationships

- **Jason**: brother; Jason says Kaito made his own choice to stand up for his world and that Amy knows it (Book 7, Ch1 L15).
- **Amy**: wife, with daughters Hana and Jace (Book 4, Ch24 L101; Book 13, Ch950 L29).
- **Erika**: sister who keeps the family together (Book 4, Ch71 L62).
- **Hiro**: his uncle, who spoke Japanese with his mother behind their father's back (Book 4, Ch34 L131).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

His death is why Amy's children grow up without a father "because he followed me" (Book 7, Ch1 L15).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Warm, teasing, effortless and brave without announcing it. Cue: "G'day... We're arrived for the mysterious family meeting."

## Kalif

### 1. Summary

Kalif is a member of Team Storm Shredder who has "bad blood" with Jason from their first meeting, and who ends up on his side in the war against the undead and messengers. He is blunt, sulky and loyal to his team leader Korinne.

### 2. Facts

- **Hot-headed**: Korinne tells her "still-angry team member" to let go of a quarrel, "You don't want to make an enemy of the next Amos Pensinata" (Book 7, Ch47 L59).
- **History with Jason**: he first met Jason "at a bad time", at the height of Jason's volatility (Book 9, Ch24 L50). They worked together on the underwater rescue under Korinne, after which Kalif "wanted nothing more to do with Asano" and was relieved he would leave Rimaros (Book 9, Ch24 L52-55). He then learned their team was going with him.
- **Agreeing to go**: "Of course we go. That doesn't mean we go blindly, and you know that Asano and I have bad blood" (Book 9, Ch24 L58). He eventually shakes Jason's hand (Book 9, Ch24 L64).
- **Team Storm Shredder**: he names the team to Jason (Book 9, Ch26 L69) and thinks being watched by Jason's guard dog is "unsettling. Makes it hard to relax" (Book 9, Ch26 L109).
- **Driving**: left behind to drive the team's new vehicle, he is "starting to get a handle on it" and has hit few other craft (Book 9, Ch29 L15).
- **Vitesse approach**: he sums up Humphrey's idea as "the Vitesse approach, but scaled up" (Book 9, Ch34 L93).
- **Complaints**: he grumbles that his team will work for two weeks while Jason is "knocking boots with the cute pink-haired woman" (Book 9, Ch42 L45).
- **Opinions on afflictions**: he says of area specialists, "No iron-rank monster is tough enough to make afflictions worthwhile" (Book 9, Ch53 L108).
- **Cardinas**: in the siege of Cardinas he asks "There's ten of us. How many undead are out there?" and "Shouldn't we have brought more people?" (Book 10, Ch90 L5-9). In Book 11 he commands silver-rankers with the cult and brighthearts (Book 11, Ch4 L21).
- **Wanting to rest**: after the surge he and others argue they should "loosen up and enjoy what we've earned" (Book 9, Ch28 L103-106).

### 3. Roleplay notes

Prickly, practical and honest about his dislikes; he follows orders without enjoying them and warms up slowly.

## Kasper Irios

### 1. Summary

Kasper Irios is a peak-bronze heir of House Irios whom Jason meets at a tailor's shop after the Zara marriage scandal. By Book 12 he is an adventurer on a team with Orin Pensinata.

### 2. Appearance

Not described beyond a House Irios crest on his arm (Book 7, Ch41 L26).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Shaken**: his movements are "oddly stumbling" and he freezes when he sees Jason (Book 7, Ch41 L3-10).
- **Eager to please**: shocked when Jason names himself the dead man (Book 7, Ch41 L11-12).
- **Nervous**: his friends pick up on his nervousness (Book 7, Ch41 L46).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- A peak-level bronze-ranker (Book 7, Ch41 L3), close to silver like his three young friends (Book 7, Ch41 L41).

### 5. Background

- Zara's intended match was "a member of the Irios family" (Book 7, Ch18 L70).
- Vesper engineered Jason's meeting with him for political reasons, and Jason's overture to the family was not taken up (Book 9, Ch14 L11; Book 9, Ch25 L79).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 7**: meets Jason at the tailor shop and walks the street with him (Book 7, Ch41 L3-46).
- **Book 12**: an adventurer now; Orin is the only one on his team to hit gold so far (Book 12, Ch12 L63).

### 7. Relationships

- **Jason**: unwilling companion (Book 7, Ch41 L26).
- **Orin Pensinata**: teammate (Book 12, Ch12 L63).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Shaken and eager to please; caught between his family's pride and Jason's reputation.

## Ken Asano

### 1. Summary

Ken Asano is Jason's father, a Japanese-born Australian landscape architect who embraces the Australian lifestyle with convert's zeal. He catches Jason in a huge hug when Jason returns, joins the Asano Village family, learns a skirmish confluence and by Book 13 is a regular companion on Jason's walks.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in detail in the lines read; he brushes his fingers over his son's scars (Book 4, Ch27 L109).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Convert's zeal**: "Proving there is no zealot like a convert, Ken was all about the Australian lifestyle, from pub rock to footy matches and weekend barbecues" (Book 1, Ch1 L88).
- **Warm and undemanding**: Jason finds "his father's warm and undemanding support was a balm" (Book 4, Ch72 L86).
- **Emotional**: he goes still, then "exploded forward" to hug Jason (Book 4, Ch27 L41).
- **Straightforward**: he asks whether Jason has gone "a little far" with his domain (Book 13, Ch1005 L83).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Has the skirmish confluence, which suits running battles; many powers trip up the enemy (Book 7, Ch31 L12).
- A landscape architect (Book 1, Ch17 L31).

### 5. Background

- Born in Japan, raised in Australia from a very young age (Book 1, Ch1 L88).
- The middle brother: Shiro was the favourite, Hiro the disappointment, "your father laid low in the middle" (Book 4, Ch7 L10).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 4**: the reunion (Book 4, Ch27 L41-44); plays with his granddaughters on the cloud house (Book 4, Ch45 L82); marches into the portal (Book 4, Ch33 L38).
- **Book 5**: guides Jason through the compound with Hiro and Emi (Book 5, Ch5 L59).
- **Book 7**: sits in the front row with the team and Gary (Book 7, Ch16 L42); his skirmish confluence helps hold off constructs round the skimmer (Book 7, Ch31 L12).
- **Book 13**: walks with Jason through a garden park (Book 13, Ch1005 L65-95).

### 7. Relationships

- **Jason**: son (Book 4, Ch27 L44).
- **Hiro and Shiro**: brothers (Book 4, Ch7 L10; Book 5, Ch34 L70).
- **Kaito**: his other son (Book 4, Ch45 L82).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Cheerfully practical, fond of barbecues and sport, quick to take Jason's side. Cue: holding on "like he would never let go."

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

## Killian Laurent

### 1. Summary

Killian Laurent is Cole Silva's right-hand man and the leader of Silva's bronze-rankers. He works with the Builder cult, uses a star seed, flees Greenstone with Silva's wealth and is later captured and chained by Jason's team.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in the lines read.

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Unctuous and without limits**: he ushers in guests (Book 3, Ch16 L43, L70; Book 9, Ch4 L11).
- **Merciless**: he argues that a man who can defy the star seed's power cannot be left alive (Book 3, Ch19 L78).
- **Exploitative**: in Book 8 he is described as dangerous for how he wormed into corners, exploiting and betraying those he works with (Book 8, Ch17 L8, L28).

- He uses a star seed for the cult (Book 3, Ch18 L130).

### 5. Background

- "Of the bronze rankers under Silva, Killian was the unquestionable leader" and he runs the secret site (Book 3, Ch17 L13-26).
- He had worked behind the scenes to plunder the Silva family while Jason distracted Silva (Book 9, Ch2 L85).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 2**: Silva calls for him (Book 2, Ch69 L12).
- **Book 3**: waits in Silva's lounge (Book 3, Ch16 L16-43); Jason's team hunts him for days (Book 3, Ch24 L3); he leaves the city on a ship loaded with Silva's holdings (Book 3, Ch25 L4).
- **Book 9**: Havi plans to deliver him but he captures Havi first; Jason's team takes and chains him in a ritual array (Book 9, Ch4 L11-39).

**Voice (condensed)**: Unctuous and without limits.

## Knowledge

### 1. Summary

Knowledge is the goddess of Knowledge. Jason meets her in Book 1 on arriving at her temple, and for twelve books she charms and manipulates him. In Book 13 he learns she has prepared for half a millennium to invade Earth and has used him as a key part of the plan.

### 2. Appearance and manner

In Book 1 a statue is replaced by a woman with colourful clothes and Mediterranean features, beautiful yet "detached and untouchable", not holding the statue's book (Book 1, Ch46 L16). She knows everything anyone in her world knows, including Jason, so she knows Mario Kart shortcuts (Book 1, Ch77 L10). A melodious voice behind Jason says "Such a shame. I was hoping to be your first" (Book 1, Ch45 L40).

### 3. Plan (spoilers)

The Book 13 briefing says she has been preparing to invade Earth for half a millennium and used Jason; that she promised the messengers' leader a chance to invade Pallimustus and claim Purity's relic; and that around a third of the priests and priestesses of Knowledge are her spies (Book 13, Ch1017 L14-20). She removes the divine essence of Gabrielle Pellin, a cube leaving Gabrielle's chest into her hand (Book 13, Ch1023 L139). Jason's last word to her: "The next time we meet, Goddess, will be the day you die" (Book 13, Ch1024 L153).

### 4. Relationships

Jason; Gabrielle Pellin; Purity and Disguise; the Church of Knowledge (one of the churches that contribute funding to the MRA, Book 12, Ch1 L58).

### 5. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Detached and untouchable in manner. Cue: "And you left. You have the same option here." (Book 1, Ch46 L15). See `../10_Roleplay_Support/Tone_and_Voice.md`.

Warm, detached and omniscient; she answers questions honestly in a way that serves her.

## Korinne Pescos

### 1. Summary

Korinne Pescos leads a Rimaros guild-elite team, later called Storm Shredder, that fights beside Jason in the surge, travels with him in Book 9 and joins the Cardinas campaign. In Book 11 she survives the Undeath siege dazed and morose after losing a friend.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in detail in the lines read; in Book 11 she has "dead eyes" until she finds Rosa (Book 11, Ch18 L29).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Efficient**: she relays orders swiftly, her efficiency "only enhanced by Jason's communication power" (Book 7, Ch48 L16).
- **Loyal**: "he's our asshole, and we don't turn on our own assholes" (Book 7, Ch50 L51).
- **Peacemaker**: "Let it go, Kalif... You don't want to make an enemy of the next Amos Pensinata" (Book 7, Ch47 L59).
- **Guarded then curious**: she visits Jason's cabin guarded about his methods and takes a slice of baked goods thoughtfully (Book 9, Ch25 L31, L89).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Leader of a silver-rank guild team of six; they were star performers, clearing enemies faster than the other teams, with two high-damage members and the rest built around them (Book 9, Ch34 L74).
- Her team "operated alone through most of the surge" (Book 9, Ch25 L31-63).
- She feels Jason's aura as "the cold anger of an icy hell" (Book 9, Ch39 L87).

### 5. Background

- Leader of Orin and Kalif's team, who coordinated the underwater complex rescue (Book 9, Ch24 L49-52).
- Her team eschewed the yacht for their own vehicle during travel (Book 9, Ch29 L14).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 7**: the mixed-force expedition (Book 7, Ch47 L54-59; Book 7, Ch48 L16; Book 7, Ch50 L51).
- **Book 8**: one of Shade's four intact bodies stays with her at the mining facility (Book 8, Ch42 L45).
- **Book 9**: asks Jason to train the team (Book 9, Ch25); travels in convoy (Book 9, Ch29 L14); Zara joins the team vehicle (Book 9, Ch41 L119).
- **Book 10**: "Storm Shredder's leader" at the breach (Book 10, Ch90 L51); in Jason's group meeting (Book 10, Ch9 L13).
- **Book 11**: stalked by a priest, finds Jetta dead and meets Rosa (Book 11, Ch6 L13-20; Book 11, Ch18 L29).

### 7. Relationships

- **Rosa, Orin, Kalif, Zara**: team members (Book 11, Ch32 L74; Book 7, Ch47 L59).
- **Jetta**: a friend, dead as a puppet (Book 11, Ch6 L19).
- **Jason**: she guesses he will lecture on Rimaros-style versus Vitesse-style adventuring (Book 9, Ch25 L58).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

In Book 11 she scrambles between rocks in a desert canyon while a priest taunts her (Book 11, Ch6 L13-16).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Brisk, proud of her team's training; she softens only when someone earns it. Cue: "He's our asshole."

## Landemere Vane

### 1. Summary

Landemere Vane is the Vane heir whose failed summoning pulls Jason to Pallimustus. He is the first person Jason meets and the first he kills, which leaves Jason shaken for weeks.

### 2. Appearance

His mother looks to be in her early thirties "no older than her son Landemere" (Book 1, Ch11 L65); no other description appears in the lines read.

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Ambitious and out of his depth**: Dougall says Landemere summoned "one of them entities from beyond the void" (Book 1, Ch9 L47-50).
- **Traditional family**: his mother says "this is my manor, my family, and we do things the traditional way" (Book 1, Ch9 L54).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Clive explains that Landemere's summoning went wrong, possibly because he reached beyond his ability or a dimensional event interfered (Book 7, Ch55 L64-79).
- He was holding more than a thousand coins when killed (Book 1, Ch13 L13).

### 5. Background

- His mother, who looks no older than her son, is among the cultists who greet Jason (Book 1, Ch11 L65).
- The Vane family treats the summoning as a family matter: "This is my manor, my family" (Book 1, Ch9 L54).
- Familiar: Jason's first encounter with a native creature was Vane's familiar, which tried to avenge him and fell victim to aging masonry (Book 5, Ch40 L81).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: the summoning in the Vane basement (Book 1, Ch9 L47-54); Jason reflects on the "very first person Jason met" and first killed (Book 1, Ch61 L41).
- **Book 2**: Clive regrets losing his notes (Book 2, Ch37 L67).
- **Book 4-7**: the first kill shakes Jason (Book 4, Ch2 L28); Clive's later explanation (Book 7, Ch55 L64).

### 7. Relationships

- **Cressida Vane**: his mother, who calls him "poor Landemere" (Book 1, Ch9 L54).
- **Jason**: accidental killer (Book 4, Ch2 L28).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Clive says random dimensional events connecting worlds are rare but more frequent because of the link between the worlds (Book 7, Ch55 L64).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Not heard on the page; remembered as ambitious and out of his depth.

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

## Liara Rimaros

### 1. Summary

Liara Rimaros is a gold-rank Adventure Society special-operations officer and a lesser member of the Rimaros royal house. She screens adventurers for Builder cultists in Book 7, leads the Book 8 expedition into the Builder's complex, handles Jason for the royal family and stays a brisk, protective ally.

### 2. Appearance

- Tall (her eldest daughter has "Liara's height") and gold-rank fast, flitting through streets unnoticed (Book 7, Ch17 L20; Book 8, Ch62 L39).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Brisk and official**: she is working without rest as the city fills with adventurers to be filtered for cultists (Book 7, Ch17 L3).
- **Wary of politics**: she "disdained" the politics she "could never seem to escape" (Book 9, Ch11 L53).
- **Self-critical but resolute**: after Gibson Amouz's capture she "allowed shame to flash over her expression before schooling it" (Book 8, Ch20 L3); she stands up to his father, "Get out of my office, Lord Amouz" (Book 8, Ch20 L57).
- **Protective**: "Don't even think about it", she tells Zareen of Jason (Book 8, Ch62 L59).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Rank**: a gold-ranker, leader of the Book 8 expedition with her former teammate Jana Costi as second (Book 8, Ch7 L4).
- **Investigator**: her search for the cult's portal users is a process of elimination through portal schedules, market tracking and field reports (Book 8, Ch20 L11).
- **Not for rescues**: she understands why she was told not to take part personally in the mining-complex rescue: "Her abilities were ill-suited to the task and her emotional investment would not be an asset" (Book 8, Ch40 L29).

### 5. Background

- **Royal branch**: "from one of the more remote branches of the royal family", not close enough to be called a princess, but entitled to a home on the royal sky island and to take part in the contests for the throne in her youth (Book 7, Ch17 L14).
- **Career**: "a long and prestigious career in Adventure Society special operations" (Book 7, Ch17 L15).
- **Marriage**: in her youth she married a local lordling, Baseph, "to secure royal influence"; they live largely separate lives but remain friends (Book 7, Ch17 L19-20). Baseph is born into House Amouz (Book 9, Ch5 L3).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 7**: she has been "working without rest" as adventurers are filtered for potential cultists (Book 7, Ch17 L3); Jason is told "Pelli and Liara Rimaros will be your contact points" (Book 7, Ch18 L95). She and Keel watch Jason and Farrah through a seeing stone (Book 7, Ch11 L65), and takes Jason to a private meeting room in the administration building (Book 7, Ch38 L91).
- **Book 8**: she leads the expedition on the Builder complex (Book 8, Ch7 L4), faces Lord Amouz (Book 8, Ch20 L14-57), re-collates her files (Book 8, Ch26 L15) and, assigned to handle Jason for the royal family, meets him with an agenda rather than gratitude (Book 8, Ch62 L30).
- **Book 9**: she tells Jason's group not to roam like a pack (Book 9, Ch14 L5), sits with him at the confrontation (Book 9, Ch16 L3) and goes to the cloud house (Book 9, Ch6 L73).

- **Book 12-13**: she visits Jason's island for a barbecue with her husband and family (Book 12, Ch56 L117); her daughter Zareen serves in the delegation to Earth (Book 13, Ch953 L51).

### 7. Relationships

- **Baseph and the children**: Baseph, Dara, Zareen and Joseph (Book 8, Ch62 L28-32); see Baseph_and_the_Rimaros_Children.md and Zareen_Rimaros.md.
- **Amouz family**: Cassin Amouz is her husband's family; she calls him "Uncle Cassin" when angry (Book 8, Ch20 L21).
- **Trenchant Moore**: stands beside her in the royal guard crisis (Book 7, Ch52 L71).
- **Jason**: she asks Farrah whether he knows about the Adventure Society liaison and says loyal, consistent people are to be treasured (Book 9, Ch6 L73-79).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Brisk, official and not unkind; she says what she needs and trusts competence. Cue: "Don't even think about it."

### 1. Summary

Lorelei Grantham is a researcher who becomes Vice-Dean and later Vice Chancellor of astral magic research, recruits Clive, covers for his escape from Rakesh and becomes his partner in Book 13. ### 7. Relationships

- **Clive**: partner (Book 13, Ch992 L122-124).

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

**Voice (condensed)**: Polite, administrative and quietly decisive.

## Lorenn

### 1. Summary

Lorenn is the last councilwoman of the brighthearts of Cardinas and, after Jason's intervention, the leader of her people. An ash-aspect brightheart who fought a war she could not win, she accepts surface allies she dislikes, hands her territories to Jason and leads her people into the new subterranean realm he builds.

### 2. Facts

- **Last of the council**: the brighthearts had a ruling council of nine, "three elected from the gold-rankers, three from the normal-rankers and three from the guilds"; only Lorenn remains, the others "having sacrificed everything to keep the rest of us alive" (Book 10, Ch72 L33). She is addressed as Councilwoman (Book 10, Ch72 L33).
- **Appearance**: an ash aspect, with "smoky greys" that she thinks far less appealing than the forge-glow of her fire-aspect friend Marla (Book 10, Ch65 L9).
- **War room**: she stands alone in the old council chamber, now a war room, before a live model of the city drawn from the natural array and mostly covered in the sickly green of the elemental messengers' tree (Book 10, Ch65 L4-8).
- **Marla**: Marla urges evacuating a number of people they can feed; Lorenn breaks down, then accepts the comfort (Book 10, Ch65 L16-24).
- **Beaufort**: she keeps the alliance with the Builder cult's commander despite loathing the cultists, "Our alliance stands" (Book 10, Ch65 L34). Later she tells the adventurers that accepting them "was not an easy choice" because "we are not warriors" (Book 10, Ch73 L35).
- **Suspicion of the surface**: she cannot bring herself to be happy at the prospect of more surface invaders (Book 10, Ch65 L38).
- **Meeting the adventurers**: she says "I am Lorenn... You, as I understand it, are Beaufort's enemies" and "So long as you can do something about the elemental messengers, I don't care what you are" (Book 10, Ch72 L44, L55).
- **Her people's story**: almost all the brighthearts died in three cycles of the messenger war, and the bodies rose; she says "We, so far as I know, are all the brighthearts that exist" (Book 10, Ch73 L45-47).
- **Accepting the loss of home**: "Losing the array is a blow our people may not recover from... if we are going to last as a people, we need to leave our home behind" (Book 10, Ch73 L57).
- **Jason's offer**: she doubts "a silver-ranker saving us all", and decides that "if we're choosing between no chance of survival and betting everything on a stranger, that's not a choice at all" (Book 10, Ch74 L25, L42). She asks what happens to the people in his soul realm if he dies (Book 10, Ch74 L57).
- **Crossing over**: she has never used a portal; she walks through with Jason as the soul realm forms chambers for her people, and fresh food appears (Book 10, Ch76 L62-75).
- **The new realm**: after her trip into it she tells Jason it is closer to the old array without its instability (Book 10, Ch77 L7).

### 3. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 10**: the war room; the alliance with Beaufort; the adventurers' arrival; the evacuation into Jason's soul realm (Book 10, Ch65-77).
- **Book 11**: she hands her territories to Jason, whose brand replaces hers; she objects to putting aside a weapon without discussion (Book 11, Ch16 L70, L77), joins the alliance council (Book 11, Ch17 L14, L39) and urges striking once the enemy messengers are destroyed (Book 11, Ch51 L61). She objects to a statue of the tree that "will loom over us, every day" (Book 11, Ch57 L17). She finds the new subterranean city "not the home she'd lost" but hopes it becomes home (Book 11, Ch62 L92-97).

### 4. Roleplay notes

Stoic, proud and exhausted; she hides grief behind formality and distrusts surface people. Her loyalty is to what is left of her people, and she bargains hard for their dignity.

---

## Lorus

### 1. Summary

Lorus is a fire-aspect brightheart who claims a territory in the unified battlefield and wants all the power. Ambitious, impatient and proud, he refuses to hand over his territory, is out-argued by Neil and Durrum, and loses his followers' support.

### 2. Facts

- **Fire aspect**: "Lorus, a fire-aspect brightheart whose messengers were likewise possessed of flame powers", each shrouded in steam as they evaporated the rain (Book 11, Ch10 L7).
- **Aggressive**: he pushes aggressively "in spite of casualties" while Durrum is more conservative (Book 11, Ch10 L8), and he has no intention of stopping his offensive against the cult (Book 11, Ch10 L12).
- **Betrayal charge**: Durrum shouts "Are you betraying us?" and "You're killing us" (Book 11, Ch10 L16-20).
- **Defiance of Neil**: the brighthearts around him yell that they would never let the undead go (Book 11, Ch10 L49), and Lorus grandstands once Neil has left the cage (Book 11, Ch11 L7).
- **His case**: "I will not hand over my power on their say-so. Those cultist abominations invaded our city. They were the beginning of the end for our entire people!" (Book 11, Ch11 L31).
- **Power grab**: "Then give the territories to me. Once everyone actually obeys, I will make us stronger as we go... Our messengers are stronger than theirs" (Book 11, Ch11 L53).
- **Neil's read**: Neil gambles that Lorus is "a volatile mix of ambition, impatience and pride, with an unearned sense of entitlement" (Book 11, Ch11 L67), and says his actions show he likes "having command of all these messengers" (Book 11, Ch11 L64).
- **Losing support**: Lorus looks around and finds even his followers will not meet his eyes, "their faces showing disgust, disdain or disappointment" (Book 11, Ch11 L71-73).
- **Last appeal**: "Durrum. Don't let this outsider lead you to disaster. Without enough messengers..." (Book 11, Ch11 L80). Durrum answers that he has never been content with what he has (Book 11, Ch11 L81).
- **Outcome**: Durrum accepts Lorus's territory (Book 11, Ch11 L86).

### 3. Roleplay notes

Loud and sure of himself, with grievances that are real and a need to be seen as the strong one. He fights bravely and bargains badly.

## Lucian Lamprey

### 1. Summary

Lucian Lamprey is the corrupt director of Greenstone's Magic Society branch, an elf with a fighter's physique "banished to Greenstone for previous improprieties". He treats the Fortress as his office, orchestrates Jason's kidnapping with Cole Silva, and is cut down by Danielle Geller and imprisoned.

### 2. Appearance

- An uncommonly muscular elf who "would not look out of place in the fighting pits himself", in expensive clothes (Book 1, Ch42 L26).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Smug and indulgent**: he arrives at his viewing room "with a contented sigh" (Book 1, Ch43 L47).
- **Handsy**: he strokes his fingers over a face in the viewing window (Book 1, Ch43 L69).
- **Quick to blame**: his fury threatens to erupt when pressed (Book 2, Ch38 L19).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Danielle outpaces him in a duel and cuts him (Book 3, Ch24 L23).
- His handling of a star seed for the Church of Purity comes under scrutiny (Book 3, Ch1 L107).

### 5. Background

- "Banished to Greenstone for previous improprieties"; he is not a member of the local elf community (Book 1, Ch42 L25-26).
- His deputy Pochard maintains the city campus so he can use the Fortress as his office (Book 1, Ch42 L30).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: the fighting pits viewing rooms (Book 1, Ch42-43; Book 1, Ch50 L104).
- **Book 2**: Clive's racks discussion (Book 2, Ch7 L62).
- **Book 3**: held in the prison tower (Book 3, Ch24 L48).
- **Book 9**: the kidnapping traced to him and Cole Silva (Book 9, Ch2 L84).

### 7. Relationships

- **Pochard Finn**: deputy and friend (Book 1, Ch50 L104).
- **Cole Silva**: co-conspirator (Book 9, Ch2 L84).
- **Danielle Geller**: opponent (Book 3, Ch24 L23).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Smug, indulgent and quick to blame. Cue: the contented sigh.

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- "A high-level agent of the Adventure Society's continental council, Marcus was a troubleshooter and enforcer" (Book 12, Ch15 L76).

- His arrival and the support he wins from figures such as Gormanston leave the aristocrats scattered (Book 10, Ch58 L58-61).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 10**: Yaresh arrival (Book 10, Ch47 L76-78); Bynes (Book 10, Ch48 L10); aristocrats scattered (Book 10, Ch58 L58-61); Cardinas planning (Book 10, Ch59 L12; Book 10, Ch60 L13-46).
- **Book 12**: dispatched to Yaresh again on hearing of Jason's return (Book 12, Ch15 L76).

### 7. Relationships

- **Gormanston Bynes**: opponent turned supporter (Book 10, Ch48 L10).
- **Jason**: ally (Book 10, Ch50 L51).

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Booming, cheerful and blunt. Cue: "I was warned that you might give me trouble."

## Marek Nior Vargas

### 1. Summary

Marek Nior Vargas is a gold-rank messenger commander who leads the breach force over Yaresh's entertainment district in Book 9. Held captive inside Jason's astral kingdom, he slowly questions the indoctrination every messenger undergoes and becomes the leader of the free messengers.

### 2. Appearance

Nine-foot messenger with wings (Book 9, Ch87 L31); he and Tera wear synthetic leather armour rather than the diaphanous clothes messengers favour (Book 10, Ch2 L18).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Arrogant, then honest**: confident in his superiority over "servant races" (Book 9, Ch87 L34), but he learns that "when pushed, even the least of sapient species would push back" (Book 9, Ch86 L17).
- **Respects craft**: he appreciates "a power used well over one that was mindlessly strong" (Book 9, Ch86 L22) and wants to face Humphrey in battle (Book 9, Ch89 L3).
- **Disaffected from the Voice**: he hates Jes Fin Kaal and avoids politics (Book 9, Ch96 L32).
- **Quietly longing for freedom**: freedom from astral kings "was what he had always hoped for and never believed possible" (Book 10, Ch2 L20).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Gold-rank commander (Book 9, Ch96 L32); he blocks a projectile with his wing without effort (Book 9, Ch87 L31).
- He spent far longer than Tera's lifetime working free of the conditioning every messenger goes through (Book 10, Ch2 L20).

### 5. Background

- Messengers' soul spaces are blank concrete utilitarian landscapes; Marek compares them with Jali's vibrant realm (Book 10, Ch55 L12).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 9**: leads the breach force (Book 9, Ch86 L16); worries as Humphrey plunges into the monster torrent (Book 9, Ch87 L35); Schaat sees him as a potential rival (Book 9, Ch96 L32); recognises Jason as Asano (Book 9, Ch97 L51); sits with Payan Nior Roel and pauses at Tera's fate (Book 9, Ch103 L56; Book 9, Ch104 L3).
- **Book 10**: waits in Jason's kingdom near the cocoon dome (Book 10, Ch1 L49); fears the leonid prisoner (Book 10, Ch1 L50); Jason says "Your kind are easy to hate" (Book 10, Ch27 L82); leads the messenger prisoners (Book 10, Ch42 L4).
- **Book 11**: involved in the Undeath siege (Book 11 mentions 46).

### 7. Relationships

- **Tera Jun Casta**: young messenger whose identity rests on the indoctrination; Marek sits beside her with concern (Book 10, Ch2 L20-21).
- **Jason**: his captor; Marek senses Jason looks "for reasons not to kill them" (Book 10, Ch4 L9).
- **Jes Fin Kaal**: he hates the Voice (Book 9, Ch96 L32).
- **Humphrey**: a respected enemy (Book 9, Ch89 L3).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

He notes that knowing messengers can survive without an astral king will be a revelation (Book 9, Ch103 L114).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Proud, dry and dutiful on the surface; adaptable, honest once his certainties break. Cue: "Freedom from astral kings was what he had always hoped for."

## Marie Finnegan

### 1. Summary

Marie Finnegan is the recently expelled director of the Zurich Network branch who ran a secret programme working with Elizabeth and Simon McKean. Controlling and secretive, she thinks she is running a tight operation; Jason takes her to talk and says he will hand her over to the Network afterwards.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in the lines read; she sips hot chocolate in a glass-walled chalet (Book 13, Ch964 L3).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Controlling and secretive**: she thinks she is running a tight operation (Book 13, Ch979 L64).
- **Professional**: she answers a call as "Finnegan" (Book 13, Ch964 L3-6).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- She uses earth-shaping powers to create a basin at a rocky shore (Book 13, Ch983 L113).
- She runs video conferencing with feeds from Pakistan and a grid system (Book 13, Ch964 L36).

### 5. Background

- The recently expelled director of the Zurich Network branch, fleeing with Elizabeth (Book 13, Ch973 L49).
- The leadership council kept the vampire programme contained at her insistence; her contacts with Elizabeth and McKean were critical (Book 13, Ch975 L24). Her backers called using Elizabeth the smart choice (Book 13, Ch975 L22).
- She worked directly with Elizabeth, "intimately" according to Remy (Book 13, Ch979 L72).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 13**: chalet introduction (Book 13, Ch964 L3-36); flees with Elizabeth (Book 13, Ch973 L49); council backing (Book 13, Ch975 L22-24); Remy's account (Book 13, Ch979 L64-72); storm shore (Book 13, Ch983 L113); Jason talks to her and says he will hand her to the Network (Book 13, Ch984 L34; Book 13, Ch985 L32-102).

### 7. Relationships

- **Elizabeth**: her vampire partner (Book 13, Ch979 L72).
- **Simon McKean**: contact (Book 13, Ch975 L24).
- **Jason**: interviews her at his estate, "this part is best done by me" (Book 13, Ch985 L32).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Her programme with Elizabeth and McKean was kept contained at her insistence (Book 13, Ch975 L24).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Controlling and secretive. Cue: answering a call as "Finnegan."

## Marla

- Leader of the brightheart military in Cardinas (Book 12, Ch11 L6).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 10**: Cardinas defence (Book 10, Ch65 L9-24; Book 10, Ch72-73; Book 10, Ch88-89).
- **Book 11**: the brightheart commander beside Beaufort of the Builder cult (Book 11, Ch4 L21; Book 11, Ch17 L80).
- **Book 12**: leader of the brightheart military (Book 12, Ch11 L6).

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

**Voice (condensed)**: Commanding and practical; she answers loss with order.

## Melody Jain

### 1. Summary

Melody Jain is Sophie's mother, who faked her death twenty years before Book 6 and then led the Order of Redeeming Light in the Storm Kingdom, brainwashed into fanaticism by the order's god. Jason's team captures her in Book 8; she is held, treated and slowly softens, ending as a loving mother in Book 13.

### 2. Appearance

- White hair and dark skin; she wears white leather armour stained and torn from shielding the fort (Book 7, Ch32 L7-8).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Fanatical and sharp**: "sharp, fanatical and brainwashed" when Jason met her (Book 13, Ch962 L56).
- **Clean habits**: she likes showers and is "ever at the ready" in her marred armour (Book 7, Ch32 L8).
- **Commanding**: she silences her second with a gesture (Book 8, Ch18 L8).
- **Softening later**: after therapy with her daughter she is "less hostile and manipulative" (Book 10, Ch36 L13).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- An essence user responsible for a fort holding out without supplies (Book 7, Ch32 L7).
- A sword fighter fast enough to dance with Jason's blade (Book 8, Ch34 L28).
- Shackled, she still runs and hides through a cloud-stuff palace (Book 8, Ch42 L5).

### 5. Background

- Faked her death twenty years before Book 6, using a wall panel in Marta Fries's house in Kurdansk (Book 6, Ch47 L510-513). Arabelle dates the story to "around a quarter of a century ago" (Book 9, Ch27 L24).
- The Order of Redeeming Light is a creation of the god Disguise masquerading as Purity; its Flames of Redemption are a modification of lesser vampirism (Book 10, Ch36 L14).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 7**: she leads the enclave, wanting a captive to lure her daughter to Rimaros (Book 7, Ch58 L38-46).
- **Book 8**: leads the local forces (Book 8, Ch18 L3-6); fights Jason (Book 8, Ch34 L28-84); escapes briefly and is recaptured (Book 8, Ch42 L5-7).
- **Book 9-10**: locked in the cloud palace while they seek a cure (Book 9, Ch19 L3); the mind-war of her fractured brainwashing (Book 10, Ch36 L13-14); Jason pins her with his aura (Book 10, Ch40 L22).
- **Book 13**: she gives Jason a motherly smile (Book 13, Ch962 L56).

### 7. Relationships

- **Sophie**: her daughter (Book 9, Ch19 L3; Book 10, Ch36 L13).
- **Arabelle**: helps look after her (Book 10, Ch42 L3).
- **Sendira**: her second (Book 8, Ch18 L8).
- **Jason**: his team holds her captive; by Book 13 she gives him a motherly smile (Book 13, Ch962 L56).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

The more she fights the brainwashing, the more the taint fights back (Book 10, Ch36 L14).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Controlled and sincere; early on zealot-bright, later warm. Cue: the motherly smile.

## General Michael Mills

### 1. Summary

General Michael Mills of the United States Army is the operational commander of the EDJI's largest military action to date, the war against the vampires in Book 13. A career soldier who rebuilt infantry doctrine for the magical age, he is trusted to handle Jason, and is chosen as spokesperson for the EDJI member states.

### 2. Facts

- **Past posting**: he was stationed at Saint-Étienne "two decades and several ranks ago", before the Asano Clan took over (Book 13, Ch1001 L3).
- **Seen the horrors**: he has seen "with his own eyes the power of the vampire lords and the land of horrors they had made" and believes the stories of Asano reclaiming his territory (Book 13, Ch1001 L4).
- **The EDJI**: he had never thought it would happen and was there for the negotiations when China and Russia demanded more influence; the US almost derailed it over the spelling of "defense" (Book 13, Ch1001 L6). He does not approve of the troops calling it "edgy" (Book 13, Ch1001 L7).
- **Doctrine**: he commanded the Infantry Reimplementation Program, redefining infantry doctrine as augmented soldiers with magitech weapons returned infantry to the forefront (Book 13, Ch1001 L91-94).
- **Command**: with his doctrine knowledge and experience fighting vampires, he is placed "in operational command of the EDJI's largest military action to date" (Book 13, Ch1001 L96).
- **Observations of the base**: he is met by a saluting EDJI lieutenant in a US Army-marked uniform (Book 13, Ch1001 L97); the tarmac holds augmented infantry and Cabal contingents (Book 13, Ch1001 L98), and he finds a "wild amount of diversity" in Asano Clan territory (Book 13, Ch1001 L99).
- **Hopes and fears**: he hopes the unity will outlast the common enemy, and worries what awaits when the threat is dealt with (Book 13, Ch1001 L101).
- **Politics**: he has no Network origins and has navigated Network and anti-Network factions his whole career (Book 13, Ch1001 L119).
- **Meeting Jason**: he has met Jason several times, mostly in passing at political events (Book 13, Ch1001 L91). In a meeting with Yumi he says "It was always my intention to pit you against McKean" (Book 13, Ch1002 L42).
- **Candour**: "Mr Asano, it's been many years since you first came back to Earth. Yes, a lot of people made less than ideal choices in those days" (Book 13, Ch1002 L49). He asks why Jason has spent a decade forging humanity's military into a single sword rather than going home (Book 13, Ch1002 L55), and why he has not told anyone about the specific threat (Book 13, Ch1002 L65).
- **Spokesperson**: he is chosen as the spokesperson for the EDJI member states, "known as someone who could handle Jason without triggering some meeting-ending debacle" (Book 13, Ch1020 L91), and enters in an informal EDJI service dress uniform with a briefcase (Book 13, Ch1020 L85).

### 3. Roleplay notes

Courteous, dry and watchful: a soldier who prefers a plan to a speech, and honest enough to name his worries to the man who frightens him.

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

## Miriam Vance

### 1. Summary

The gold-rank leader of Team Moon's Edge and Tactical Commander of the Cardinas expedition, who shares overall command with Jason.

### 2. Facts

- Introduced as "the leader of Team Moon's Edge, Miriam Vance" (Book 10, Ch59 L17). Moon's Edge is a team of six women, all gold rank, raised and supervised by Allayeth from early in their careers (Book 10, Ch51 L43; Book 10, Ch59 L4).
- She is the expedition's Tactical Commander and tells Jason no when he wants to add his butterflies to a messy flying battle (Book 10, Ch61 L45; Book 10, Ch69 L19). Her gold-rank senses read Jason's emotions through his aura (Book 10, Ch68 L10).
- She notices how Allayeth acts around Jason (Book 10, Ch64 L22), questions him about astral kings and the goddess (Book 10, Ch65 L60; Book 10, Ch67 L64), and argues with him over command (Book 10, Ch76 L3). Death addresses her by name (Book 10, Ch85 L38).
- She runs the withdrawal through the citadel tunnels as overall commander (Book 10, Ch82 L58) and sets the defensive perimeter (Book 10, Ch80 L33).
- In Book 11 she is the zone's co-commander with Jason (Book 11, Ch19 L56; Book 11, Ch49 L79), directs Moon's Edge to destroy the tree crystals (Book 11, Ch51 L64; Book 11, Ch52 L10) and protects the non-combatants in Ramona's invisibility sphere when Amos Pensinata goes into the orb (Book 11, Ch53 L25; Book 11, Ch55 L3).
- Her team "was the most powerful force on the battlefield other than the cloud buildings and the two divine entities" (Book 11, Ch32 L75).
- Jason introduces her to Gordon, his avatar of doom (Book 11, Ch33 L20). A different Miriam, Miriam Coyle, heads a magitech weapons institute in Book 13 (Book 13, Ch995 L14).

### 3. Timeline of involvement

- Book 10: leads Moon's Edge on the Cardinas expedition (Book 10, Ch59-85).
- Book 11: co-commands the zone (Book 11, Ch19-57).

### 4. Roleplay notes

Disciplined, direct and unwilling to take chaos on trust; she argues with Jason as an equal.

---

## Mr North (Noreth)

### 1. Summary

Mr North is the true leader of the Engineers of Ascension, first among its four Cardinals, and the Network founder's former familiar Noreth. A very old rune spider turned man, he spends centuries on Earth bargaining, scheming and experimenting, ends by disabling the Grid and by leaving Jason a vault of his research, and dies in Book 6 killing Gerling to avenge his friend.

### 2. Appearance

- A grinning man who meets Jason "grinning like a snake who found a nest full of baby mice" (Book 5, Ch40 L68). When he drops the act he is stern, adjusting his tie and cuffs, "the grinning, languid man Jason had met was nowhere to be seen" (Book 5, Ch41 L103).
- He is a gold-ranker, not an essence user, and "a bonded familiar, but your bond has been severed" (Book 5, Ch40 L74-78). Jason tells Anna that "He was a magic spider. A familiar of the man you know as the network founder" (Book 13, Ch987 L16).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Amused and mocking**: "You're a smart man, Mr Asano. More or less" (Book 5, Ch40 L72); he calls Jason "a parade of delights" (Book 5, Ch41 L33).
- **Controlled**: "He had long ago schooled himself out of dangerous curiosity and exploitable impatience" (Book 5, Ch8 L24).
- **Ruthless about outcomes**: with the Grid down for months he says "A wide-scale collapse of civic and social infrastructure does not obviate our objectives" and "So long as we rule" (Book 5, Ch8 L58-60).
- **A manipulator of principles**: "Be wary of your principles, Mr Asano. I might use them to be assured that you enter that astral space" (Book 6, Ch25 L117).
- **Paranoid and lonely**: Barbou thinks he is "older and more powerful than anyone realises", not human, and "lonely" (Book 6, Ch30 L56-58).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Webs**: he draws ritual circles in webbing that contain auras, sound, scent and magic (Book 6, Ch38 L71). He buries himself in a cocoon before the nuclear solar rockets, and digs out afterwards (Book 6, Ch46 L112-113).
- **Magitech without theory**: he developed magitech "with almost no knowledge of magical theory, drastically low ambient magic, and essentially zero technology", and was too paranoid to trust capable scientists; Audrey Blaine "was a buffer between North's ambitions and his paranoia" (Book 13, Ch987 L22-24).

### 5. Background

- **A rune spider**: "I was a rune spider, originally" (Book 5, Ch40 L79). The Network founder was his essence user; "My essence user was blinded by faith... giving up power and prestige to lift up a bunch of savages", and the bond broke before the founder died (Book 5, Ch40 L84).
- **Betrayal**: Noreth sold out the founder to the early magic societies (Book 8, Ch50 L52; Book 13, Ch1017 L24).
- **Centuries on Earth**: Boris supplied him with spirit coins to survive as a gold-ranker but North never trusted him; had he trusted him, "North's core research might not have been such a mess" (Book 13, Ch987 L28).
- **The EOA**: his organisation is named for his project of engineering people without essences; its leader "secretly being some kind of spider" (Book 13, Ch1001 L92).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 5**: the Cardinal's meetings and the shutdown plan (Book 5, Ch3 L5-12; Book 5, Ch8 L14-67). He takes Barbou from Mrs West's circle (Book 5, Ch32 L8; Book 5, Ch40 L86). He meets Jason in the Builder's door space, tells him to absorb the door and says "It's about time you showed up" (Book 5, Ch40 L66; Book 5, Ch41 L24-26).
- **Book 6**: he stays near Jason through the transformation zone work (Book 6, Ch35 L6; Book 6, Ch38 L3). He insists Jason will go into the astral space "whether I give you Barbou or not" (Book 6, Ch25 L107-113) and later dies killing Gerling (Book 6, Ch46 L112-127).
- **Later books**: his vault of EOA secrets goes to Jason (Book 7, Ch48 L36; Book 11, Ch36 L14) and the clan uses his research (Book 13, Ch987 L14).

### 7. Relationships

- **Jason**: sometimes ally, sometimes enemy; Jason "never trusted" him but believed his intentions were good (Book 8, Ch1 L57).
- **Barbou**: he calls him a quality subordinate and takes him after the Lyon plans fail (Book 5, Ch40 L86).
- **Audrey Blaine**: his own cardinal Mrs South, whom the cardinals murder for refusing the plan (Book 5, Ch8 L62-67; Book 13, Ch987 L12).
- **Gerling**: "You took my friend", he says, and kills him at the cost of his own life (Book 6, Ch46 L117-125).
- **Boris**: they knew each other, but "North's paranoia prevented them from working together" (Book 13, Ch987 L27-28).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

His identity as the Network founder's familiar is revealed to Jason in Book 5 (Book 5, Ch40 L78-86) and to everyone else in Book 13 (Book 13, Ch1017 L39). Noreth's failure was not seeing that Asano was an ally (Book 13, Ch954 L12).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Dry, old and amused; he treats everyone as a long game, flatters and needles in the same breath, and drops the grin when the stakes are real. Cue: "You're a smart man, Mr Asano. More or less."

## Neil Davone

### 1. Summary

Neil Davone is an elf of Greenstone's Island families, a healer who grows from the Mercers' hanger-on into the heart of Jason's team. He is a priest of the Healer, and by 2038 he uses his growth magic to reclaim deserts.

### 2. Appearance

Muscular (Sophie and Belinda comment on his "muscular body", Book 2, Ch71 L14), though the notes describe him as "chubby for an elf" (Book 2, Ch71 L14).

### 3. Personality and voice

He grew up in the Mercer family's orbit: he started spending time at the Mercer compound as a boy because Thadwick needed friends his own age and the Davone and Kettering families had close ties to the Mercers (Book 2, Ch27 L41-43). At thirteen he had a crush on Cassandra Mercer, four years older (Book 2, Ch27 L41-48). He makes a stand in the Temple of the Healer (Book 1, Ch94 L3-7), and after being rejected by the Mercers' circle the guards treat him as "just another iron-ranker" (Book 2, Ch27 L59). He is uncertain about joining Jason's team (Book 2, Ch27 L46) and shows a nervous expression when pressed (Book 2, Ch27 L112).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Essences**: Shield, Growth and Renewal, producing the Prosperity confluence (Jason's notebook, Book 2, Ch28 L44): short-lived shields that intercept attacks, healing and cleansing.
- **Abilities**: size-growth power (Book 2, Ch30 L52-54) and Armour of Renewal, which reduces damage taken and gives healing over time (Book 2, Ch64 L55); the Reaper's Redoubt (wiki).
- **Summon**: a chrysalis golem "like an ogre carved out of diamond" with runes appearing on its facets as it is hit (Book 3, Ch4 L29-32).
- **Late**: his Growth, Renewal and Prosperity essences find fertile ground in desert reclamation in Australia and North Africa (Book 13, Ch997 L37-38).

### 5. Background

An elf of the Davone family, whose household is on the Island and holds tea lands in the Mistrun valley (Book 2, Ch23 L17, where a maid serves the family's blend). He was initially Thadwick Mercer's lackey and team mate (Book 1, Ch110 L40; Book 2, Ch75 L67); after the disastrous expedition Thadwick disbanded the team without notice and the two were glad to be free of being known as Thadwick's flunkeys (Book 2, Ch27 L57), and Neil then joined Jason's team (Book 11, Ch6 L63). Cassandra Mercer is not his ex: as a youth he admired Thadwick's older sister (Book 2, Ch27 L43), and he was angry that she chose Jason (Book 11, Ch6 L60). She was Jason's girlfriend and ended it (Book 2, Ch13 L19).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: stands in the Temple of the Healer; joins Rufus, Gary and Jory at the clinic reopening.
- **Books 2-3**: joins Jason's team; the chrysalis golem and shields.
- **Book 11**: a defender-healer in the transformation zone with Dustin Kettering (Book 11, Ch8 L23-24).
- **Book 12**: in the Mirror Kingdom with Nik (Book 12, Ch12 L75), portalled in with Team Shining Scabbard led by Sigrid Freyn, with whom Neil had been training (Book 12, Ch15 L8).
- **Book 13**: reclaiming deserts.

### 7. Relationships

Jory Tillman, Dustin Kettering (friend, tank), the Mercer family, Cassandra Mercer, Nik, the Church of the Healer.

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

His fall from the Mercers' favour is level 1.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Tentative before committing. Cue: Asano's visit left Neil uncertain, since the only real attraction to joining the team was Humphrey Geller (Book 2, Ch27 L46). See `../10_Roleplay_Support/Tone_and_Voice.md`.

Calm and humane; the healer who patches everyone up.

## Nigel Thornton

### 1. Summary

Nigel Thornton leads a nine-person mercenary unit that began as a Network tactical team. He is the first gold-ranker outside the United States to get there without cores, and in 2038 he works as a gold-ranker for hire, infiltrating vampire strongholds and clearing blood farms alongside the Asano clan.

### 2. Appearance

- In the camp he wears black fatigues under magical tactical armour, carrying no firearms, only a thigh-mounted magic knife (Book 4, Ch39 L65).
- By Book 12 he holds a gold-rank pistol with a magical silencer, a gift from a grateful client (Book 12, Ch4 L23).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Disciplined**: "We can't match up to your gear... But we have training and discipline" (Book 4, Ch41 L96).
- **Direct and proud of results**: "We've taken out four category threes just today" (Book 4, Ch41 L92).
- **Bitter at the blood farms**: "How many farms were left running while the Asanos were hiding in their magic hole?" (Book 12, Ch10 L60).
- **Careful**: he spends more time hiding than moving in the city and freezes when a vampire sniffs the cellar (Book 12, Ch4 L23-28).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- First gold-ranker outside the US without cores; "the US had non-core training programs long before Farrah Hurin arrived" (Book 12, Ch3 L3).
- The rest of his team are silver-rank core users (Book 12, Ch3 L4).

### 5. Background

- His team is the same nine-person unit it was almost two decades earlier, when it belonged to the Network's secret paramilitary wing (Book 12, Ch3 L5).
- When the Network schismed, they left, sickened by infighting and the Australian government, and became mercenaries (Book 12, Ch3 L6).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 4**: Keith brings Nigel to the grandmother's visit (Book 4, Ch36 L74); his team sweeps a camp perimeter (Book 4, Ch40 L61); Jason shows him his party voice chat (Book 4, Ch40 L22) and tells him the Network's methods are reaching their limits (Book 4, Ch41 L89-97).
- **Book 5**: he is Gladys's bodyguard when Jason's rage flares (Book 5, Ch43 L14).
- **Book 12**: hides in a vampire city (Book 12, Ch4 L23-48); moves blood farm victims with the clan (Book 12, Ch10 L59).
- **Book 13**: infiltrates Multan, Pakistan (Book 13, Ch1007 L16); his teams bring vampires back when clearing farms (Book 13, Ch979 L22).

### 7. Relationships

- **Jason**: Jason's tutor on how teams will fail against stronger monsters (Book 4, Ch41 L97).
- **Rufus**: rides back with him from the blood farms (Book 12, Ch10 L59).
- **Gladys**: he is her bodyguard (Book 5, Ch43 L14).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Steady, weary and loyal to his team; professional, short on speeches. Cue: "We have training and discipline."

## Nik Asano

### 1. Summary

Nik is a four-foot humanoid rabbit in a top hat and tuxedo whom Jason brought into being, unplanned, when his soul realm became a transformation zone (Book 11, Ch61 L16). He curses constantly, is bleeped on the page (Book 11, Ch8 L102), and calls Jason "Dad" (Book 12, Ch39 L15). He is the control key to the zone's network (Book 11, Ch46 L32), trains at the Geller estate (Book 11, Ch68 L1034-1038), reaches gold rank (Book 13, Ch998 L4) and acts as a team's coordinator and overwatch through drones and mapping powers (Book 13, Ch966 L71).

### 2. Facts

**Origin and name**
- Nik first appears to Neil and Dustin in the soul realm as a "four-foot humanoid rabbit in a top hat and tuxedo", with swearing bleeped and a "bleeper" he does not recall being installed (Book 11, Ch8 L102-106).
- Jason names him in a forest: "Nik. NIK, no C", from "Lehenik", a word from the language of Jason's birth world meaning "first" or "firstly", and the name Jason would give a people of which Nik is the first instance (Book 11, Ch23 L42). Jason declines to name him after Kai and offers him the Asano surname if he wants it (Book 11, Ch23 L38).
- The transformation zone created him, with the Healer's gift erasing any flaws; Jason "unconsciously brought" him into being (Book 11, Ch61 L16).
- He says he is "six months old" and that most of what he knows is "random nonsense put in my head" (Book 11, Ch50 L15).
- He is "the key" to the network of control nodes Jason made while changing the zone, and the node's lock is broken (Book 11, Ch46 L30-33).

**Book 11: in the zone**
- He and one of Shade's bodies bring Jason's friends into the soul realm as "plan B" and lead them to the objective (Book 11, Ch36 L40-45; Book 11, Ch38 L3). He calls Boris "Two-Piece Feed" (Book 11, Ch36 L40-42).
- He attacks by making wind sounds with his mouth, and a small cloud appears (Book 11, Ch38 L33). He he runs the weather machine across the unified territory from a platform of control panels (Book 11, Ch50 L10-25).
- His head can pass through a portal while his body stays hundreds of kilometres away (Book 11, Ch53 L56). He learns a board game from Neil and suggests planting the tree in Jason's soul realm (Book 11, Ch57 L26-41).
- He is part of Jason's "core group of friends" in the tree city (Book 11, Ch67 L19).

**Training (Book 11 to Book 12)**
- After the zone, being normal rank among gods left him feeling "vulnerable and weak", and he trains at the Geller estate in Greenstone (Book 11, Ch68 L1034-1036).
- His combination is from Earth: the technology essence Jason brought, with Myriad and Vast, producing the Network confluence (Book 11, Ch68 L1037). Danielle Geller's introduction gets him into the family's most elite training programme, building a support set as the "central hub of a team" (Book 11, Ch68 L1038). He is bronze when he leaves Greenstone (Book 11, Ch68 L1039).
- He calls Neil "Uncle Neil" (Book 11, Ch68 L1082, L1104).

**Book 12: reunion**
- Neil and Nik are portalled in from the Mirror Kingdom with Team Shining Scabbard, led by Sigrid Freyn (Book 12, Ch15 L8).
- Jason estimates that Nik was "five, maybe" when he left (Book 12, Ch15 L45-47).
- Nik tells Jason: "Dad, you created me out of thin air like you were starting your own bible, sent me to violence boarding school and then vanished for a decade and a half" (Book 12, Ch39 L15). Jason promises to do better, warns him that Emi will hug him all week, and Nik asks him for a hug (Book 12, Ch39 L30-35).
- He travels on Jason's cloud ship (Book 12, Ch39 L3) and in Vitesse, where he points out the flowering towers (Book 12, Ch43 L46-50). At the sky port battle he offers to get the arriving groups "in line", saying he is used to jumping in with groups that do not know him (Book 12, Ch53 L92).
- His System ability: a raid group invitation notes that "the powers of [Nik Asano] interface with you" (Book 12, Ch54 L33-34).

**Book 13: Earth**
- He is nervous about meeting the Asano family, wishes Jason had come back (Book 13, Ch951 L4-11), and wants to find a team on Earth (Book 13, Ch951 L7).
- His mapping powers are more precise than Jason's tactical map, and he can relay powers and devices remotely (Book 13, Ch966 L71). He acts as overwatch through an earpiece (Book 13, Ch996 L5-9) and through a drone over briefings and the field (Book 13, Ch1007 L48; Book 13, Ch1011 L63).
- He tells Michael that Jason "created me" and complains he has not been given a girlfriend, saying he might be the last of his kind (Book 13, Ch1003 L67-72).
- He reaches gold rank, with a celebration party (Book 13, Ch997 L11, L23; Book 13, Ch998 L4). Sophie will teach him, Jason and Emi to use wingsuits (Book 13, Ch996 L181).
- After Jason destroys McKean's astral space, Nik takes over McKean's broadcast and keeps it going (Book 13, Ch1015 L48).

### 3. Roleplay notes

- **Voice (condensed)**: blunt and profane, with bleeped swearing and a love of pop-culture references such as Superman and Lois Lane (Book 11, Ch8 L102; Book 13, Ch1003 L72); fond of "Dad" and wary about being treated as a toy (Book 12, Ch39 L31).
- **What drives him**: wanting power that is his own rather than borrowed (Book 11, Ch68 L1036), and wanting Jason to stay (Book 13, Ch951 L11).
- **How he works in a group**: a support set built around being the hub of a team, with mapping and relays (Book 11, Ch68 L1038; Book 13, Ch966 L71).
- **Do not give him**: a canonical homeland, a mate or other rabbit-folk. The books leave the Lehenik as an intention, not a people (Book 11, Ch23 L42).

## Noriko Asano

### 1. Summary

Noriko Asano is the strongest member of the old Asano clan and its patriarch's mother, who takes control from her son and opposes Jason's family. By Book 12 she is matriarch of the old clan, hosting Jota Withers. Stern, brusque and proud, she measures people by strength.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in the lines read; she presides with eight elders at a low table (Book 5, Ch36 L3).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Contemptuous of honour**: "You sound like your new white friend, Asano" (Book 5, Ch36 L89).
- **Strength-first**: she argues there is only shame in weakness and "only the strongest shall rise" (Book 5, Ch36 L11-16).
- **Calculating**: she tells the others not to inform Mei and Akari, so they act as a mask for the clan's own plans (Book 5, Ch36 L32).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- The strongest member of the old Asano clan (Book 5, Ch36 L3).

### 5. Background

- She wrests control of the clan from her son, the former head Shiro, whose closest family settle in Asano Village (Book 5, Ch52 L68).
- She explains the government seized land from the "upstart clan" and gave it to the "true Asano clan" (Book 12, Ch63 L30).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 5**: seizes the clan and confronts Jason; Jason says "My Asano family and your Asano clan henceforth have no connections, Noriko" (Book 5, Ch36-37, Ch52; Book 5, Ch37 L92).
- **Book 12**: hosts the pirate admiral Jota Withers with daily visits and servants (Book 12, Ch63 L19).

### 7. Relationships

- **Shiro**: son she displaces (Book 5, Ch52 L68).
- **Jason**: opponent (Book 5, Ch37 L92).
- **Jota Withers**: guest (Book 12, Ch63 L19).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Book 12 calls her matriarch of the Asano clan while Yumi is also called matriarch; the two descriptions are not reconciled (open question; Book 12, Ch63 L19).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Stern, brusque and proud; treats compromise as weakness. Cue: "only the strongest shall rise."
