## Phoebe Geller

### 1. Summary

Phoebe Geller is a distant Geller cousin of Humphrey's, Rick Geller's sister, and a pugilist on Rick's team. Blunt and curious, she asks what everyone is thinking and sits in on Sophie's training.

### 2. Appearance

- Darker skin and much lighter hair than Humphrey, from a distant branch family; light-brown pixie-cut hair (Book 1, Ch66 L4; Book 2, Ch24 L27).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Dry**: "I suspect your mother's hand will be firmly pressed down on the scale" (Book 1, Ch66 L30).
- **Relaxed**: she settles happily in a chair sipping her second glass while watching Sophie (Book 2, Ch24 L72).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- A pugilist, "a more damage-oriented version of Sophie"; she launches off Stash's palm to strike multiple enemies (Book 10, Ch70 L42).
- Iron rank in Book 1 and with the Adventure Society for over half a year (Book 1, Ch66 L3).

### 5. Background

- Distant cousin of Humphrey; the two share a last name but barely any ethnicity (Book 1, Ch66 L4).
- Rick's sister, on his team but absent for family issues at one point (Book 9, Ch1 L83; Book 9, Ch104 L54).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: meets Humphrey on his return from a contract (Book 1, Ch66 L3); present when Rick and Humphrey arrive (Book 1, Ch110 L51).
- **Book 2**: watches Sophie's practice (Book 2, Ch24 L72).
- **Book 9**: back on Rick's team (Book 9, Ch104 L54).
- **Book 10**: fights beside Dustin with Stash's help (Book 10, Ch70 L42-44).

### 7. Relationships

- **Rick**: brother (Book 1, Ch110 L51).
- **Humphrey**: cousin (Book 1, Ch66 L3).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Blunt and curious; she asks what everyone is thinking. Cue: the dry aside about the mother's thumb on the scale.

## Pochard Finn

### 1. Summary

Pochard Finn is Lucian Lamprey's long-time deputy director in Greenstone, an elf and local who does the actual work while Lamprey enjoys the title. He is practical, discreet and understands the value of discretion.

### 2. Appearance

An elf and a local (Book 1, Ch42 L30).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Discreet**: "a man who understood the value of discretion" (Book 11, Ch68 L1167).
- **Protective of his boss**: he steps up when fury crosses Lamprey's face (Book 2, Ch38 L19).
- **Judges Humphrey fairly**: he remembers the Geller son as "polite, forthright and a little lacking in confidence" (Book 11, Ch68 L1174).

- He keeps the city campus running while frequently travelling to the Fortress (Book 1, Ch42 L30).
- He arranges the lifelike water-link to Gabriel Remore (Book 1, Ch49 L27).

### 5. Background

- Long-time deputy who did the real work during Lamprey's famously corrupt tenure (Book 11, Ch68 L1167).
- His son Cassowary is Lamprey's dogsbody and go-between (Book 1, Ch43 L47; Book 1, Ch50 L104).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: explains the Fortress office arrangement (Book 1, Ch42 L30); watches Clive (Book 1, Ch42 L40).
- **Book 2**: Emir and Finn contain Lamprey's outburst (Book 2, Ch38 L19).
- **Book 11**: at his desk when Humphrey arrives (Book 11, Ch68 L1167-1175).

### 7. Relationships

- **Lucian Lamprey**: friend and employer (Book 1, Ch50 L104).
- **Cassowary Finn**: son (Book 1, Ch43 L47).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Practical and discreet; the one who keeps the books. Cue: stepping forward as Lamprey's fury rises.

## Raythe

### 1. Summary

Raythe is the prime vessel of the Keeper of Moments, a peak diamond-ranker from beyond Pallimustus who steps in on Jason's behalf in Yaresh and stays after the great beings leave.

### 2. Appearance

- An elf with dark brown skin and light brown hair flecked with green (Book 13, Ch991 L3).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Direct**: "I am Raythe, and I have told you as much of my intentions as you need to know. Leave or die" (Book 9, Ch97 L80).
- **Calm and amused**: "You shall see me again when it is done. Not too soon, as you have earned your rest" (Book 12, Ch2 L9).
- **Reluctant when needed**: she tells Jason with a straight face that the World-Phoenix will crawl into his soul, with reluctance in her expression (Book 11, Ch65 L97).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Prime vessel of the Keeper of Moments (Book 11, Ch64 L9); with Velius she leads the descent of peak diamond-rankers into the shaft (Book 11, Ch61 L8).
- Boris says the Keeper of Moments polices time manipulation harshly (Book 11, Ch63 L98).
- She tells Jason only the nameless will stand with the World-Phoenix against him (Book 11, Ch65 L55).

### 5. Background

- After the great beings leave, she alone remains; time there is synchronised with Jason's universe (Book 12, Ch1 L5-11).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 9**: in Yaresh she tells a challenger to "Leave or die" (Book 9, Ch97 L80).
- **Book 11**: asks if the Reaper did not tell Velius why they came (Book 11, Ch22 L12); the descent (Book 11, Ch61 L8-11); revealed as the Keeper's vessel (Book 11, Ch64 L9).
- **Book 12**: remains with Jason (Book 12, Ch1 L5-11; Book 12, Ch2 L9).
- **Book 13**: walks beside Jason through the empty tree city of Arbour (Book 13, Ch991 L3-42).

### 7. Relationships

- **Velius**: fellow peak diamond-ranker (Book 11, Ch61 L8).
- **Jason**: ally and counsel (Book 11, Ch65 L55).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Calm, precise and amused; she says little more than the situation requires. Cue: "Leave or die."

## Remy

### 1. Summary

Remy is a portal specialist whose range is limited. In Book 4 he and Sebastian work for Adrien Barbou, hop across Australia with a rescued agent in Kakadu and kill her; in Book 5 he helps in Makassar; in Book 13 he is Marie Finnegan's portal man, caught between Jason and the vampire queen Elizabeth.

### 2. Facts

- **Kakadu**: he and Sebastian have taken Miranda (Ellis) out of Australia; her complaint that "Twelve hundred kilometres is the best you can do? And you have to wait an hour between portals?" draws "Let's see your portal power" (Book 4, Ch49 L3-4). They are in Kakadu National Park, which Remy is scornful of her not recognising (Book 4, Ch49 L7).
- **Range**: he says no essence user can portal sixteen thousand kilometres, and that the Chinese reportedly have someone near category four who can do a few thousand at a time (Book 4, Ch49 L9-10). He notes the rule that "You cannot portal where you have never been" (Book 4, Ch49 L84).
- **Barbou's men**: Miranda calls Remy a failure of "the great portal master Barbou promised" (Book 4, Ch49 L11). After a glance, Sebastian kills her with metal hummingbirds and a kick; Remy says "A personality like that is practically a suicide note" (Book 4, Ch49 L16-18). He reports to Adrien by phone (Book 4, Ch49 L19-26).
- **Book 5**: "Hi, I'm Remy. You two came in pretty hot", and he takes Jason and a companion through a portal to a command post near Paotere Harbour (Book 5, Ch26 L39-44).
- **Book 13: Finnegan's portal man**: he opens a portal "About time... If any gold-rankers turned up, I was just going to bail", is careful around "that guy", and follows Marie, Gerling and the blood orb through it (Book 13, Ch973 L73-82).
- **Hurt by Jason's field**: a teleport attempt leaves him "doubled over, coughing" in Book 13, after which the portal flickers like an old TV (Book 13, Ch975 L102). He recovers on a bus roof (Book 13, Ch975 L113; Book 13, Ch977 L48).
- **Old job**: he did a job for the Lyon branch "back when Asano had just returned to Earth the first time" and explains how a silver-rank was sent to kidnap Jason; Sebastian kicked her off a rock in Kakadu (Book 13, Ch977 L96-111).
- **Interrogated**: Jason reads a spike of panic in his aura when asked who he is protecting and tells him "Give me a name, Remy" (Book 13, Ch977 L118-125).
- **Finnegan and Elizabeth**: Jason learns from Remy that Marie has been working "intimately" with Elizabeth, the vampire queen increasingly on the outs with her subjects (Book 13, Ch979 L72).
- **Last scenes**: Remy scrambles through a portal with Elizabeth and Marie (Book 13, Ch984 L73) and wonders "What is this place?" at Elizabeth's refuge (Book 13, Ch985 L9). Elizabeth apologises for jabbing at his weakness (Book 13, Ch985 L18).

### 3. Roleplay notes

Dry, wary and mercenary: he is brave only as far as the exit and talks when cornered.

## Rick Geller

### 1. Summary

Rick Geller is a Geller cousin and team leader, a big swordsman who is the main rival of Jason's team in Greenstone. He loses his teammate Jonah Geller to a star seed, takes Dustin Kettering on, and becomes a friend and ally of Jason in Rimaros and the later wars.

### 2. Appearance

- "Like his sister, his skin was dark brown, his hair light brown. His build was more like Humphrey, tall and broad-shouldered" (Book 1, Ch66 L58).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Earnest and wide-eyed**: the 'standard Rick' expression is wide-eyed, as Jason thinks of it (Book 9, Ch1 L111).
- **Respectful of rank**: he realises he is speaking to a gold-rank princess and his head dips as if yanked by a string (Book 9, Ch1 L59).
- **Loyal to his team**: he does not like having his team split (Book 9, Ch1 L83), and watches over Jonah in the rescue (Book 2, Ch17 L10).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- A huge sword wielded "like a baton", with an essence ability that "temporarily ramped up his speed and power" (Book 1, Ch67 L99).
- Rank: iron-rank in Book 1 (Book 1, Ch66 L17), a spear-wielder by Book 10 whose team smashes messengers with Stash's help (Book 10, Ch70 L38).
- Hunt style: put an enemy in front of him and nothing at iron rank survives (Book 1, Ch66 L17).

### 5. Background

- Brother of Phoebe Geller; his team includes Jonah, Henry, the Adeah twins and later Dustin Kettering (Book 1, Ch110 L51; Book 2, Ch29 L8; Book 9, Ch104 L54).
- His girlfriend is Hannah Adeah, who slaps the back of his head in Book 10 (Book 10, Ch13 L26).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1-3**: the mirage-arena match with Jason (Book 1, Ch66-67), the survivors of the expedition (Book 1, Ch110 L51), Jonah's death (Book 2, Ch17 L10), the team contest (Book 2, Ch29 L69).
- **Book 7**: he and his team arrive in Rimaros, taken to the throne room by Vesper (Book 7, Ch59 L65-72) and present a recording (Book 7, Ch59 L122).
- **Book 9-11**: he meets Jason in Rimaros (Book 9, Ch1 L59-111), flies over Yaresh after the battle (Book 10, Ch1 L57), fights in Cardinas (Book 10, Ch70 L38) and brings groups to Jason's territory with Sophie (Book 11, Ch21 L104).

### 7. Relationships

- **Dustin**: Rick's team replaced Jonah's role with Dustin, who "was a friend of Neil's" (Book 7, Ch59 L65).
- **Humphrey**: a close match in style (Book 2, Ch30 L51).
- **Jonah**: the teammate he fails to save (Book 2, Ch17 L10).
- **Phoebe**: his sister, on his team (Book 9, Ch104 L54).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

None in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Earnest, a bit overawed by Jason and fiercely loyal to his team. Cue: the wide-eyed 'standard Rick' stare.

## Roland Remore

### 1. Summary

Roland Remore is Rufus's grandfather, a diamond-rank sword master, archchancellor of Remore Academy in Vitesse and leader of Burning Violet. He rarely appears but his presence is felt, and he arrives with the diamond-rankers at the end of Book 13.

### 2. Appearance

- "A well-preserved forty, a tenth of the reality": tall, strong and handsome, with a round bush of dark curly hair (Book 3, Ch69 L588).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Weighty and remote**: his presence on the Academy campus is always felt and draws all eyes (Book 3, Ch69 L587).
- **Proud of the guild**: Gabriel says "He's always treated the guild like it's his own little fiefdom" (Book 12, Ch45 L56).
- **Famous**: Rufus often repeats his advice (Book 3, Ch20 L25).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Diamond-rank sword master (Book 3, Ch20 L25); his aura surges out in Book 13 (Book 13, Ch1024 L35).
- He personally brought a boy from the countryside to the academy, rumoured (Book 3, Ch69 L588).

### 5. Background

- Archchancellor of Remore Academy; the guild Burning Violet became more associated with the Academy after he became guild leader (Book 6, Ch47 L125).
- Rufus's grandfather; Gabriel's father (Book 12, Ch45 L56).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 3**: introduced via Rufus's advice and the Academy (Book 3, Ch20 L25; Book 3, Ch69 L587-588).
- **Book 7**: Farrah has met him (Book 7, Ch46 L78).
- **Book 9**: Jason asks about him (Book 9, Ch18 L70).
- **Book 12**: Humphrey says Roland was looking forward to meeting Jason (Book 12, Ch45 L97).
- **Book 13**: emerges from the dimensional vessel and meets Jason's aura (Book 13, Ch1024 L14, L35).

### 7. Relationships

- **Rufus**: grandson, who repeats his advice (Book 3, Ch20 L25).
- **Gabriel**: his son (Book 12, Ch45 L56).
- **Humphrey**: friend of Rufus who knows his reputation (Book 12, Ch45 L97).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Measured, aphoristic and rarely seen; scenes with him should feel weighty. Cue: aura rising across a room.

## Rosa Liselos

### 1. Summary

Rosa Liselos is the scout of Korinne's Team Storm Shredder, with the best perception on the team. Practical and comfort-loving, she backs Kalif in wanting rest, spots Jason's skulking admirer, and guides her wounded team back through enemy lines in Book 11. By Book 12 she has retired and works for the Adventure Society.

### 2. Facts

- **Introduced as a rival**: a Rimaros adventurer addresses her as "Rosa Liselos, isn't it? What do you say, Liselos? Can you do better than Asano's shadows?" (Book 7, Ch47 L73).
- **Role**: "Rosa Liselos, the scout from Korinne's team" (Book 9, Ch26 L110); "the team scout, she had the best perception amongst them" (Book 9, Ch53 L118).
- **Comfort**: she says she "can definitely live with it" if working for Jason means cloud beds and giant dinner spreads (Book 9, Ch26 L110), and joins Kalif in telling Korinne the monster surge is over: "This is a can for storing food, not adventurers" (Book 9, Ch28 L106-110; Book 9, Ch29 L8).
- **Insight**: she names the difference "between adventuring approaches in Rimaros and Vitesse" (Book 9, Ch34 L86).
- **Gossip**: she bets Jason "doesn't go for those stuffy society dances" (Book 9, Ch42 L52).
- **Candour about Zara**: she tells a princess to get over a man who is not keen on her (Book 9, Ch53 L114) and senses him "skulking around" (Book 9, Ch53 L118).
- **Surprise**: she asks "How did you get so close? You didn't use to be this good" of someone who has improved (Book 9, Ch54 L8).
- **Book 11**: the team scout guides the wounded team back to friendly lines "through the enemy throng" to the healers (Book 11, Ch32 L74).
- **Book 12**: "Rosa retired. She works for the Adventure Society now" (Book 12, Ch12 L61).

### 3. Roleplay notes

Sensible and a little sardonic: she notices things before anyone, wants a bed and a hot meal, and would rather say what she thinks than keep a mask.

## Rufus Remore

### 1. Summary

Rufus Remore is a bald, dark-skinned swordsman from Vitesse, grandson of the diamond-ranker Roland Remore. He is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, runs Jason's field assessment, and remains his friend for the rest of the series.

### 2. Appearance

Dark skin, a bald head and "stupidly handsome"; when Jason first sees him, grimy from his ordeal, he looks like an action hero heading into act three (Book 1, Ch11 L49). His voice is "like dark chocolate" (Book 1, Ch11 L51). He is "tall and lean" (Book 7, Ch9 L6) and a "tall, leanly muscular adventurer" (Book 9, Ch3 L59); no height in numbers is given.

### 3. Personality and voice

- He is calm under pressure: when Anisa demands that Jason be burned as tainted, he answers "I did [know]" and refuses her any say (Book 1, Ch30 L88-93).
- He feels responsible as the leader of his group: Farrah tells Jason "Rufus is in charge, so he blames himself" for their capture, and says the pressure on him from his family is enormous (Book 1, Ch30 L57-60).
- After Farrah's death he is driven by obsession, which strains his relationships (Book 3, Ch33 L11-12).
- The family joke, repeated by Arabelle and Rufus in Book 10, is "my family runs a school" (Book 10, Ch21 L19-21).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Swordsmanship**: an elegant scimitar of golden light with red-gold inscriptions that he conjures in his hand (Book 1, Ch16 L31-36); silver and golden swords (Book 1, Ch16 L31-36).
- **Other powers**: boots that let him walk on water (Book 1, Ch16 L38) and a "speed of light" power that makes the world "seem to freeze in time" for "two seconds of accelerated time" (Book 1, Ch108 L99; Book 1, Ch109 L23).
- **Kingdom of Eclipse**: a sun-and-moon power invoked by incantation ("Darkness and light, sun and moon; be mine to awaken and move at my command...", Book 2, Ch76 L71).
- **Rank**: bronze at the start of the series (Book 1, Ch15 L92: "We're bronze-rank adventurers"), and in Book 11 he is the most powerful combatant on Earth below gold rank (Book 11, Ch68 L1514); the chapters read do not state that he reaches gold.
- **Teaching**: he teaches Jason footwork, balance and combat (notes, Book 1) and later teaches the Asano clan (Book 13, Ch1001 L8).

### 5. Background

Son of Gabriel and Arabelle Remore (Book 2, Ch33 L6); grandson of Roland Remore (Humphrey calls Roland "the grandfather who means so much to his friend", Book 12, Ch45 L97); his older brother Gwydion is a priest of Hero (notes, Book 11); Rufus's uncle is clergy of Hero (Book 1, Ch48 L92-96). Rufus was "really late fighting his first monster" but did it "by nineteen" (Book 11, Ch68 L918).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: captured with Gary and Farrah by the Vane blood cult; frees them with Jason; runs Jason's field assessment; present when Farrah dies.
- **Books 2-3**: uses his Kingdom of Eclipse power in the strike on the Builder cult camp (Book 2, Ch76 L71).
- **Book 7**: reunites with Jason in Rimaros.
- **Book 11**: travels to Earth with Taika and Boris, arriving at the standing stones and meeting Yumi Asano (Book 11, Ch68 L470-473; Yumi is from the notes).
- **Book 13**: by 2038 he teaches the Asano clan; he introduces Hassan Dukhtar, whom he is dating (Book 13, Ch1016 L23-27).

### 7. Relationships

Jason (closest friend), Gary and Farrah (childhood friends), Roland, Arabelle, Gabriel and Gwydion (family), Humphrey Geller, Taika Williams, Hassan Dukhtar. The books only imply a relationship with Vincent Trenslow, so it is not recorded here (project decision).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

His journey to Earth and role teaching the clan (Book 11 onward) are level 3.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Courteous and formal, quick to apologise for discourtesy. Cue: his apology to Priestess Pellin (Book 7, Ch9 L18). See `../10_Roleplay_Support/Tone_and_Voice.md`.

Speak calmly and courteously; refuse unreasonable demands without raising your voice; make quiet jokes about the family school.

## Sendira

### 1. Summary

Sendira is Melody Jain's second in command in the Order of Redeeming Light's local enclave: a silver-rank zealot and the person Melody trusts most. She commands the Purity forces on the island in Book 8, carries the aura beacon and the clockwork kings, and holds the order's discipline together while suspecting others.

### 2. Facts

- **Rank in the order**: Melody leads the enclave and Sendira, her second, reports on what the scouts have found (Book 7, Ch58 L38). The overall leadership is the same silver rank as the individual cell leaders, so there is "a constant tension" (Book 8, Ch9 L17).
- **Reliability**: she is "ever-reliable"; like another cell leader, Kelleigh, she is not ambitious, which places her as Melody's second (Book 8, Ch33 L16).
- **Doctrine**: she tells the converted, "Only Purity is worthy of our devotion, not his servants... We are all unworthy, seeking to cleanse the taint that lingers within us" (Book 8, Ch9 L21), and "Distraction and frivolity taint pure dedication of purpose" (Book 8, Ch9 L14).
- **Command on the island**: she is "the commander of the Purity forces on the island", separating from most of her group to take a smaller team underground (Book 8, Ch13 L3).
- **Control of subordinates**: she wants Fila and Ramona "under her thumb instead of causing trouble for Melody's plans" (Book 8, Ch13 L6). She snaps at Ramona that "What Melody wants with the target is no concern of yours. Your place is to obey, not criticise in ignorance" (Book 8, Ch13 L54).
- **The beacon**: when the grab team seizes Melody's daughter, "Sendira couldn't activate the beacon fast enough" (Book 8, Ch13 L51). She launches a flare that scatters motes of light (Book 8, Ch14 L59), and the beacon's pervasive aura drenches the island until it is cut off, at which she shows "an expression of uncertainty" (Book 8, Ch14 L70-72).
- **Clockwork kings**: when the Builder cult delivered the first clockwork king, it came with a control device; she explains that the order purified both (Book 8, Ch14 L67). She orders the kings through a portal after taking out a silver pyramid (Book 8, Ch16 L85-92).
- **Doubt among her people**: Jaime says "Sendira is using us as decoys" (Book 8, Ch16 L29).
- **Assessment**: "The likelihood of their having realised our objective is high" (Book 8, Ch16 L82).
- **At the leaders' meeting**: she stands next to Melody as hostile cell leaders glare (Book 8, Ch17 L55); angry at a remark, she is silenced by Melody's gesture (Book 8, Ch18 L8). Melody asks whether she has been telling people they were going after Melody's daughter (Book 8, Ch18 L80).
- **Search**: she crouches with the others to feel faint vibrations through the floor (Book 8, Ch33 L22).

### 3. Roleplay notes

Rigid, loyal and humourless: she speaks in doctrine, obeys Melody absolutely and treats questions as faults. When her plan fails she falls quiet rather than doubting.

## Shako

### 1. Summary

Shako is a diamond-rank servant of the Builder who kills Jason in Book 6, apparently possessed by the Builder at the moment he does it. Later he is taken by the Sundered Throne, and the Builder replaces him with Erigo Fin Desca.

### 2. Appearance

- Pale, freckled skin, wild red hair and eyes so green they almost glow (Book 3, Ch69 L193).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Impatient and proud**: he sighs at his petitioners despite not needing breath for centuries (Book 3, Ch69 L196).
- **Contemptuous**: he sneers when Jason tries to push back (Book 6, Ch17 L68).
- **Struck still when overridden**: when the Builder speaks through him he goes stiff (Book 8, Ch54 L13).
- **Told he has no authority of his own**: "You don't have any authority, do you, Shako?" (Book 8, Ch52 L56).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Diamond-rank: his aura crushes Jason's aura and lifts him into his grip (Book 6, Ch17 L62).
- Can enter through a window opened by the transformation event as long as he leaves before it closes (Book 6, Ch17 L43).
- Moves faster than Jason can think; a tablet throws him back with a sonic boom (Book 8, Ch52 L59-60).

### 5. Background

- A servant of the Builder (Book 6, Ch17 L41); in Book 3 he is seen in an imperial throne room with an empress (Book 3, Ch69 L207-213).
- Dawn warns that killing Jason violated the compact between the Builder, the Reaper and the World-Phoenix (Book 6, Ch18 L79).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 3**: the imperial palace scene and the Reaper's district (Book 3, Ch69 L193-236).
- **Book 6**: introduces himself and kills Jason (Book 6, Ch17 L41-62); Dawn confronts him (Book 6, Ch18 L4, L27, L79-84); Jason wonders whether he was sent to "lose control" (Book 6, Ch19 L5).
- **Book 8**: tablet incident and Dawn-Builder switch (Book 8, Ch52 L56-60; Book 8, Ch54 L13); catatonic afterwards (Book 8, Ch54 L115).
- **Book 10-11**: Erigo replaces him (Book 10, Ch15 L5); Jason mentions him (Book 11, Ch64 L65).

### 7. Relationships

- **Dawn**: confronts him (Book 6, Ch18 L4).
- **Jason**: killer and later subject of questions (Book 8, Ch55 L99).
- **The Builder**: his master (Book 6, Ch17 L41).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

The Church of Death's certification counts Jason's deaths; Shako's killing is the fourth (Book 7, Ch17 L104).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Impatient and proud, believing he is in control; when overridden he stiffens. Cue: "I am Shako. I am a servant of the Builder."

- **Neil**: sparring partner (Book 12, Ch20 L9).
- **Hastor**: father (Book 3, Ch5 L57-58).

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

## Simon McKean

### 1. Summary

Simon McKean is the former head of the Earth researchers in the Network's grid workgroup. By Book 13 he works with the vampires from a research complex beneath a French castle, preparing for a decade to fight Jason, and is Jason's final earthly adversary.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in the lines read.

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Obsessed with the fight**: Boris warns Jason that McKean "has spent the last decade preparing for this fight. To him, battling you is not a means but an end in itself" (Book 13, Ch1000 L104).
- **Cunning**: he baited the coalition into the fight, and no one knows why (Book 13, Ch1003 L9).
- **Controlled**: he watches Jason and two familiars move through his tunnels from a monitoring room (Book 13, Ch1010 L3).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Expert in the grid: "about as expert in it as anyone but you" (Book 13, Ch1003 L47) and understands it better than anyone other than Farrah (Book 13, Ch1006 L15).
- Created vampire-magitech abominations by mixing modern magitech with blood magic (Book 13, Ch1006 L60).
- Modified a vine to revive the undead and bound souls of vampires and minions to it (Book 13, Ch1008 L20-27).
- He took Gerling from the vampire queen and used him as an agent (Book 13, Ch1008 L33).

### 5. Background

- Head of the Earth researchers, ranked only behind Farrah in the workgroup (Book 13, Ch970 L38).
- He and Farrah repaired the grid together after the Engineers of Ascension sabotaged it (Book 13, Ch1003 L31).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 13**: Farrah describes him (Book 13, Ch970 L38); Boris's warning (Book 13, Ch1000 L104); Michael and Jason plan the strike (Book 13, Ch1002 L40-42; Book 13, Ch1003 L4-92); Jason will "confront McKean tomorrow" (Book 13, Ch1005 L104); the castle was a Network operations centre (Book 13, Ch1006 L15); the vine (Book 13, Ch1008 L5-33); his broadcast breaks up at the collapse (Book 13, Ch1014 L75).

### 7. Relationships

- **Farrah**: the only one in Jason's circle who knows him personally (Book 13, Ch1003 L31).
- **The vampires**: he is already working with them (Book 13, Ch1003 L86).
- **Gerling**: his agent (Book 13, Ch1008 L33).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Jason says McKean is "just a warm-up compared to what comes next" (Book 13, Ch1005 L121).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Theory-obsessed and patient; he treats the fight as his life's work. Cue: battling Jason "is an end in itself."

---

## Sophie Wexler

### 1. Summary

Sophie Wexler is a celestine fighter known as the Nightingale in the Greenstone fighting pits. She is a thief and debt-slave when Jason meets her, has her indenture taken over by Jason in Book 2, and becomes the team's fastest fighter and, later, Humphrey's fiancée.

### 2. Appearance

Chocolate skin, shining silver hair and sharp eyes that exactly match the hair, "the matching metallics a giveaway trait of the celestine race"; normally shoulder length, tied back in a simple, practical ponytail (Book 1, Ch43 L18).

### 3. Personality and voice

Suspicious of kindness at first: "Are you trying to tell me that Jory is such a good friend to you that you'd go this far over some girl he likes?" (Book 2, Ch1 L77-80). She fights through pain without complaint; in Book 2, one-armed and struggling to her knees, she waves off the lesser miracle potion Jason offers (Book 2, Ch45 L69-72). Her laugh is "free" (Book 9, Ch48 L12).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Essences**: Swift, Balance and Wind, producing the Mystic confluence: Clive answers "Mystic" when Rufus asks what that combination produces (Book 2, Ch5 L82-87). Before Jason's help she had only the Swift essence and its single ability for more than half a dozen years (Book 2, Ch5 L37-41).
- **Abilities**: Eternal Moment, a massive acceleration power in which "time seemed to freeze" as she produced wind blades (Book 3, Ch49 L15); Between the Raindrops (from the Awakening Stone of the Rain; notes, Book 2); Mirage Step and Wind Blade (Book 2, Ch8 L170-173; Ch7 L129); unarmed Way of the Reaper strikes.
- **Racial gifts** (celestine): Mana Integrity evolves into Mana Wellspring (Book 2, Ch61 L146), Astral Affinity into Boundary Breaker, which removes the damage reduction from rank disparity (Book 3, Ch68 L14-15), and Celestial Swiftness into Princess of the Firmament (Book 8, Ch22 L37-38).
- **Late**: in Book 13 she has spent several years purging whole cities of disease with her wind and aura (Book 13, Ch997 L28-31).

### 5. Background

Born in Kurdansk, in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil (Book 6, Ch47 L390, Emir). Her father's failed expedition left her with a huge debt at sixteen or seventeen, and she worked as a pit fighter; Cole Silva, whose father her father had worked for, wanted her (Book 1, Ch51 L26; Book 1, Ch50 L92). Her mother is Melody Jain (Book 9, Ch19 L3-6), who faked her death some twenty years earlier (Book 6, Ch47 L510-513).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: caught as a thief, sentenced to indenture; fights in the pits as the Nightingale.
- **Book 2**: Jason takes her indenture; she joins the Adventure Society.
- **Books 3-6**: key fighter; the team's accelerator.
- **Book 7**: Jason learns that her mother leads the Order of Redeeming Light in Rimaros (Book 7, Ch58 L38-46).
- **Book 11**: Humphrey calls her his fiancée (Book 11, Ch68 L1177).
- **Book 13**: travels the world for years purging epidemics.

### 7. Relationships

Humphrey (fiancé), Belinda (oldest friend), Jason (the man who took her indenture), Melody Jain (mother), Danielle Geller.

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Her mother's identity and fate are levels 2-3.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Wary of kindness and silent about pain. Cues: she asks why Jason would do so much for them (Book 2, Ch1 L77-80); she grimaces silently through the pain of a broken arm (Book 2, Ch45 L69-72). See `../10_Roleplay_Support/Tone_and_Voice.md`.

Quick and sharp; she distrusts kindness at first and stays in the fight through pain.

---

## Soramir (Soramir Rimaros)

### 1. Summary

Soramir Rimaros is the founder of the Rimaros royal house, a diamond-rank ruler with a palindromic name, who guides Jason through the Builder crisis. His connection to Jason is why Jason is protected from political accusations.

### 2. Appearance

- Emerald hair and eyes at a party, then natural royal blue (Book 7, Ch18 L49).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Calming and formal**: his aura spreads calm that oppresses the agitated Farrah and Liara (Book 7, Ch46 L86).
- **Plain-spoken about debts**: "It is undeniable that we have dragged Jason Asano into events he never asked for" (Book 7, Ch46 L98).
- **Deference from others**: even the Storm King defers to the founder in the private lounge (Book 9, Ch14 L4).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Diamond-rank ruler (Book 13, Ch1024 L14).
- He tells Jason that the Hierophant may intervene in the world a single time (Book 7, Ch60 L27).

### 5. Background

- Palindromic first and last names "were assigned in adulthood rather than at birth and denoted important members of a given family" (Book 7, Ch18 L41-42).
- Sits with the Storm King and core royal family members in an elevated lounge (Book 9, Ch14 L4).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 7**: meets Jason (Book 7, Ch18 L41-49); the balcony meeting with Liara and Trenchant (Book 7, Ch46 L74-98); leads Dawn away (Book 7, Ch52 L71); the Builder's fortress emerges (Book 7, Ch65 L6).
- **Book 9**: with the royal family at the confrontation (Book 9, Ch14 L4); he steps in when Jason soul-attacks a man in front of the king (Book 9, Ch23 L11).
- **Book 10**: his connection to Jason keeps the Adventure Society from accusing him (Book 10, Ch2 L58).
- **Book 13**: not among the diamond-rankers who emerge from the dimensional vessel (Book 13, Ch1024 L14).

### 7. Relationships

- **Liara**: royal officer and relative (Book 7, Ch46 L74).
- **Jason**: protector and uneasy debtor (Book 7, Ch46 L98).
- **Dawn**: he leads her away from the crowd (Book 7, Ch52 L71).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

His connection to a diamond-ranker Jason knows deferentially is not explained in the lines read (Book 7, Ch56 L6).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Dignified, plain-spoken and used to getting his way, but aware of what it costs others. Cue: "My family is used to getting our way."

---

## Taika (Taika Williams)

### 1. Summary

Taika is a huge Māori man who works for Hiro Asano, befriends Jason on his return to Earth and becomes one of the Asano clan's core fighters. He rockets up the ranks, takes the garuda confluence and a golden bird form, and travels to Earth with Rufus and Boris in Book 11.

### 2. Appearance

- "The mountainous Māori", comparable in size to a leonid or a draconian (Book 4, Ch17 L42), with tattoos that stand out against his skin when it turns emerald to resist damage (Book 9, Ch93 L27).
- A "massive frame" that does not buckle a reinforced chair when he drops into it (Book 11, Ch52 L29).
- In bird form he is a giant golden bird (Book 10, Ch21 L34).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Easy and cheerful**: "Taika, by the way. Like the director, but I don't make films" (Book 4, Ch4 L27); "the numbers for letters thing is a bit naff, though, right? It's not 2004" (Book 4, Ch16 L44).
- **Companionable**: he sits behind a plastic drum kit while Jason and Emi play a rhythm game (Book 4, Ch44 L3). He tells Jason "I don't normally like watching people's holiday videos, but they were pretty sweet" (Book 7, Ch37 L25).
- **Sharp-eyed**: his "narrowed eyes lingered on Boris" before he got to work (Book 11, Ch68 L580).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Rank: he races up through the proto-spaces and monster waves, "especially with being human as an accelerating factor" (Book 9, Ch33 L14). At the end of the surge his aura is "so close to breaking through to silver that it was like an egg starting to hatch" (Book 9, Ch71 L43, per the Power Sets file).
- A mobility brawler: Farrah teaches him to fight "like Taika", adapting to his new abilities, and his performance helps convince the Network to grant him a place (Book 4, Ch65 L30).
- Garuda confluence and bird form: see Taika_Power_Set.md (Book 9, Ch93; Book 10, Ch21).

### 5. Background

- He is "Taika Williams" (Book 7, Ch44 L61), employed by Hiro in Sydney (Book 4, Ch5 L40) and knows the ropes of the Asano family business.
- When offered the renewal essence and immortal confluence Jason picked out, he chose a different combination after discussion (Book 4, Ch65 L22).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 4**: he phones to say a man claiming to be Hiro's nephew is looking for him (Book 4, Ch4 L17) and drives Jason to a code-locked building, telling him the code so he can come and go (Book 4, Ch5 L40).
- **Book 7**: he and Travis stay with the Gellers in dormitories for young trainees, preferential treatment for being Jason's friends (Book 7, Ch44 L61).
- **Book 9**: his rank-up (Book 9, Ch92 L3), his fight with the messenger Fal (Book 9, Ch93) and his meeting with Haliastur (Book 9, Ch78 L11).
- **Book 10-11**: he flies after Jason and Farrah as a golden bird, meditates atop Onslow's shell and goes to Earth with Rufus and Boris (Book 10, Ch21 L34; Book 10, Ch22 L67; Book 11, Ch68 L305).
- **Book 12**: he and Boris's group go to meet Shiro and the bodyguards (Book 12, Ch59 L35), and his bird form carries a saucer (Book 12, Ch62 L4-9).

### 7. Relationships

- **Hiro Asano**: his boss, who rides in silence with him in Book 4 (Book 4, Ch13 L80).
- **Rufus**: both could benefit from each other's knowledge (Book 9, Ch6 L41); they travel together (Book 11, Ch68 L618).
- **Jason**: "boss" (Book 4, Ch16 L44).
- **Emi**: sits behind a drum kit as she and Jason play a rhythm game (Book 4, Ch44 L3).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

None in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Large, good-humoured and loyal; a complaint about his mother's opinions on French food is his signature (Book 6, Ch47 L155). Cue: "Taika, by the way. Like the director, but I don't make films."

---

## Tera Jun Casta

### 1. Summary

Tera Jun Casta is a branded messenger who challenges Jason to a duel in Yaresh, is knocked out when Jason strips her seal and later works through the destruction of her sense of self. She ends as a member of the freed messenger community living with the Asano clan.

### 2. Appearance

She and Marek wear simple leather armour of magical synthetic instead of the diaphanous clothing messengers favour (Book 10, Ch2 L18).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Zealous**: "I am Tera Jun Casta... I will be the one to kill you" (Book 9, Ch100 L19).
- **Rigid and devout**: a "zealous follower of the messenger orthodoxy before her forced liberation" (Book 11, Ch67 L12).
- **Duellist by temperament**: she chooses weapons that instil the most fear (Book 9, Ch100 L69).
- **Guarded**: she listens to Jason's story "without comment or expression, but her aura was a calamity of emotions" (Book 13, Ch973 L85).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- She fights comfortably with her abilities suppressed, in an orthodox style (Book 9, Ch100 L49).
- Her seal keeps her at silver rank; Jason removes it by working inside her soul (Book 9, Ch102 L54-67).
- A messenger unable to advance beyond silver is a loose addition to the raid forces (Book 10, Ch1 L17).

### 5. Background

- Her soul is branded and she was raised on lies and exploited her entire life (Book 10, Ch42 L7).
- Her old friend from "their days of enslavement" is Jali Corrik Fen (Book 13, Ch973 L85).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 9**: duel with Jason in a ruined tavern and dormitory (Book 9, Ch100 L49-72; Book 9, Ch101 L12-23); stripped of her seal (Book 9, Ch102 L54-67).
- **Book 10**: Marek sits with her (Book 10, Ch2 L20); the astral king punishes the emotions she held back (Book 10, Ch52 L67).
- **Book 11-13**: Jali's only friend (Book 11, Ch68 L2480); at the kitchen table with Jason, Boris and Jali (Book 13, Ch973 L85).

### 7. Relationships

- **Jali Corrik Fen**: old friend (Book 11, Ch68 L2480).
- **Marek Nior Vargas**: her commander (Book 10, Ch1 L17).
- **Jason**: freed her against her will (Book 11, Ch67 L12).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Inflicting soul torture on her was the only way Jason could win the death match she forced on him (Book 11, Ch67 L12).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Rigid, devout and furious at being freed; stoic on the surface. Cue: "I will be the one to kill you."

---

## Thadwick Mercer

### 1. Summary

Thadwick Mercer is the arrogant heir of House Mercer, who torments his two "offsiders" Neil and Dustin, feuds with Jason, takes a Builder star seed and becomes a vessel for the Builder. The Builder's vessel is later "the worst vessel I ever possessed"; Thadwick himself ends as an energy vampire in Book 9 and returns in Book 13.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in detail in the lines read; his gear includes a blade with a ruby and onyx hilt and a spiked grip in Book 13 (Book 13, Ch1022 L62).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Arrogant and cruel**: "a fool whose arrogance and incompetence only escalated over time" (Book 11, Ch6 L57) and "the worst" (Book 4, Ch68 L185).
- **Fixated on Jason**: "Thadwick was always fixated on me. I think he might have had a sister complex" (Book 9, Ch26 L59), after Jason dated his sister Cassandra (Book 4, Ch68 L177).
- **Leashed**: a rival greets him, "I see your mother let you out, so long as you wore your leash" (Book 2, Ch41 L80).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Lightning, wind, potent and storm essences (Book 1, Ch110 L20; see Essence_Catalogue.md).
- He fights from behind his protectors: Dustin used his powers to protect while Neil healed him, and Thadwick "had been blasting powers" (Book 1, Ch110 L17).
- After the star seed he becomes a vessel for the Builder (Book 3, Ch46 L61; Book 11, Ch68 L160) and later "some weird vampire" (Book 9, Ch26 L57-58).

### 5. Background

- **Family**: his father Beaufort Mercer is the Duke of Greenstone's brother; his mother Thalia is an adventurer (Book 1, Ch77 L47; Book 2, Ch59 L4).
- **Companions by obligation**: Dustin, like Neil, was "forced to train and work with Thadwick through the obligation of his family to the Mercers" (Book 11, Ch6 L57, L61).
- **Sister**: Cassandra Mercer is four years older than Neil and the object of his youthful affection (Book 2, Ch27 L43).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: his entourage at the Mercer gatherings (Book 1, Ch77 L46-57); the expedition (Book 1, Ch110 L17).
- **Book 2**: he faces Timos and wipes the sneer off his face (Book 2, Ch41 L80-89); he is missing and hunted (Book 2, Ch59 L4-36).
- **Book 3**: he enters a hole to receive power (Book 3, Ch46 L61) and is in the cult's care when Jason appears as a shadow (Book 3, Ch57 L15).
- **Book 9**: an energy vampire who took the sword (Book 9, Ch26 L57-58); in Book 10 "the vampire once known as Thadwick" speaks (Book 10, Ch34 L118).
- **Book 13**: he carries the relic blade and meets Thalia in a warehouse (Book 13, Ch1022 L62-67).

### 7. Relationships

- **Neil and Dustin**: his offsiders, "both stuck under Thadwick due to their families" (Book 1, Ch77 L46).
- **Thalia and Beaufort**: parents, one adamant about training, the other guilty (Book 1, Ch53 L54; Book 11, Ch6 L59).
- **Cassandra**: his sister, who dated Jason (Book 4, Ch68 L177).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

He was possessed by the Builder at one point (Book 11, Ch68 L160-186), and is the subject of Umber's later plans (Book 13, Ch1024 L118-125).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Petty, loud and entitled, given to threats that lean on his family name. Cue: a sneer and a leash joke from someone else.

---

## Thalia Mercer

### 1. Summary

Thalia Mercer is the matriarch of the Mercer family, a silver-rank explosive adventurer and friend and teammate of Danielle Geller. She wants better training for her son Thadwick, fusses over him after the Builder-cult crisis, and by Book 13 watches her estranged daughter Cassandra from the shadows.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in detail in the lines read.

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Welcoming with an edge**: "You must be the young man people are getting so curious about" (Book 1, Ch53 L47-49).
- **Wry and diplomatic**: "I daresay you're right. So, you're willing to leave Thadwick to my family?" (Book 1, Ch97 L108).
- **Unhappy about her husband's decision**: she tried to convince him Thadwick needed more training (Book 1, Ch53 L54).
- **Motherly under pressure**: she fusses over Thadwick as he is carried through a portal (Book 1, Ch111 L42).
- **Sentimental about her daughter**: she hasn't seen Cassandra "in years" and watches her from behind a tree (Book 13, Ch999 L3).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Silver rank with might, potent, swift and onslaught essences: "in terms of pure explosive power she was a match for any adventurer alive" (Book 2, Ch59 L83).
- She blasted Thadwick's door "to splinters with a special attack" (Book 2, Ch59 L84).
- Her Onslaught essence informs her inclinations as well as her power set (Book 13, Ch999 L3).

### 5. Background

- Friend and teammate of Danielle Geller (Book 2, Ch59 L83).
- Present at the estate when Danielle witnesses Jonah Geller's gruesome end (Book 2, Ch21 L19).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: introduced by Danielle; boards the Geller carriage (Book 1, Ch53 L45-62); settles Thadwick's future (Book 1, Ch97 L108; Book 1, Ch111 L42).
- **Book 2**: with Danielle, Emir, Arella and the archbishop (Book 2, Ch21 L19); the black parlour and the corpse puppets (Book 2, Ch59 L22, L82-84).
- **Book 13**: watches Cassandra (Book 13, Ch999 L3); Thadwick leaves the bunker without a word of goodbye (Book 13, Ch1022 L67).

### 7. Relationships

- **Thadwick**: son (Book 1, Ch111 L42).
- **Cassandra**: daughter she hasn't seen in years (Book 13, Ch999 L3).
- **Danielle Geller**: friend and teammate (Book 2, Ch59 L83).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Her Book 13 watching of Cassandra from a tree implies the estrangement (Book 13, Ch999 L3).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Composed, watchful and wry; fiercely protective of her son. Cue: "I tried to convince my husband."

## Timos

### 1. Summary

Timos is a Builder cultist embedded in Greenstone for years who regrets going along with Thadwick's self-recruitment, kills Frank, and stands with Zato in the Vane estate ritual. He is careful, patient and horrified by amateurs.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in the lines read; he wears dismissive sneers until Thadwick wipes one off (Book 2, Ch41 L89).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Regretful**: he "quickly came to regret" Thadwick's aggressive self-recruitment (Book 2, Ch59 L87).
- **Cautious**: every mistake "threatened to snowball into disaster" (Book 2, Ch59 L89).
- **Compartmentalising**: he facilitated the cult's insertions and ran operatives in compartmentalised groups (Book 3, Ch34 L10).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- He kills Frank with a conjured spear (Book 2, Ch59 L106-110).
- He takes part in a ritual with Zato and Dougall (Book 3, Ch51 L85).

### 5. Background

- "Timos had been operating in Greenstone for years" (Book 2, Ch59 L87).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 2**: Thadwick presses him about flashes of memory (Book 2, Ch41 L88-89); the Frank murder (Book 2, Ch59 L87-110).
- **Book 3**: led with Thadwick across the Vane estate by Zato (Book 3, Ch46 L55); the ritual (Book 3, Ch51 L85); Zato notes the marks on his neck (Book 3, Ch41 L73).

### 7. Relationships

- **Zato**: his leader (Book 3, Ch46 L55).
- **Thadwick**: an inconvenient recruit (Book 2, Ch59 L87).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Careful, patient and horrified by amateurs. Cue: a dismissive sneer.

## Travis Noble

### 1. Summary

Travis Noble is a young Californian magitech weapons engineer who becomes Jason's outworlder weapons researcher on Pallimustus, marries the Knowledge priestess Gabrielle Pellin and, by Book 13, leads weapon development against the vampires. Earnest, happy and quick to adapt, he is the person who builds Earth's new arsenal.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in detail in the lines read; "goofy grin" when he watches his wife eat (Book 13, Ch1016 L74).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Overworked and decent**: "Travis Noble was twenty-one years old and a category two magitech weapons engineer from California. He was also having a very bad month" (Book 6, Ch28 L36).
- **Clear-sighted on Network faults**: "The Network has kidnapped Mr Asano twice, along with killing his friend, his girlfriend and his brother" (Book 6, Ch29 L52).
- **A researcher by temperament**: "an enthusiastic researcher whose expertise bled into" other fields (Book 10, Ch8 L6).
- **Devoted husband**: he is happy and worried watching his wife eat (Book 13, Ch1016 L74).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Magitech weapons engineer**: a specialist in large-scale weaponry (Book 10, Ch8 L6). His dimensional space is a holographic cabinet with a sliding door, from which he pulls an oversized high-tech revolver (Book 6, Ch28 L65).
- **Cross-world builder**: he works with Clive, Gary and Gabrielle on the tools and artifice side of magitech (Book 7, Ch60 L96).
- **Constructs**: he waves a rod and a mannequin-like construct walks out (Book 10, Ch30 L13).
- **Sky link**: his sky link service carries calls by Book 12 (Book 12, Ch53 L32).

### 5. Background

- Category-two Network engineer who becomes head of the Special Munition Stockpile Division when his supervisor goes AWOL, with a team of people who all hate him (Book 6, Ch28 L36-37).
- An outworlder from Earth to Pallimustus (Book 10, Ch8 L6).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 6**: Germany, Network base (Book 6, Ch28-29); he stays in France when Jason leaves (Book 6, Ch47 L155).
- **Book 7**: Greenstone and Rimaros; Jason takes him to the Church of Knowledge (Book 7, Ch56 L71); the battle seen from the cloud house (Book 7, Ch65 L44).
- **Book 9-10**: he joins Jason's circle (Book 9, Ch38 L21) and works on weapons for the siege (Book 10, Ch30).
- **Book 12-13**: he and Farrah own the island (Book 12, Ch56 L10); by Book 13 he is the lead researcher for the Joint Magitech Weapons Research Institute (Book 13, Ch995 L14).

### 7. Relationships

- **Gabrielle Pellin**: his wife, a priestess of Knowledge (Book 13, Ch1016 L74; Book 8, Ch6 L6).
- **Taika**: close friend (Book 7, Ch44 L61).
- **Clive and Gary**: collaborators (Book 7, Ch60 L96).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

His negotiations with the Church of Knowledge over what Earth magitech he may bring to Pallimustus are part of Knowledge's plan (Book 9, Ch13 L85).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Enthusiastic, technical and polite; a worrier who gets his best work done in a crisis. Cue: his goofy grin at his wife.

## Trenchant Moore

### 1. Summary

Trenchant Moore is a gold-rank human sword specialist of the Sapphire Crown royal guard who escorts Jason's group in Rimaros. Watchful and reserved, he reads places and people for danger.

### 2. Appearance

- A human in a guild of mostly celestines: pale-skinned and dark-haired, lean and angular with icy blue eyes (Book 7, Ch21 L13-14).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Reserved**: he drops to one knee before the royals (Book 7, Ch46 L74).
- **Cautious about politics**: he warns that Vesper's world is political (Book 7, Ch58 L53).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Gold rank sword specialist who has served as a guard on and off for decades (Book 7, Ch21 L13-18).
- He boards ships checking society contracts (Book 7, Ch22 L93).

### 5. Background

- The royal family does not shield the Sapphire Crown from surge quotas (Book 7, Ch21 L15-18).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 7**: summoned to a low-key palace meeting where Vesper Rimaros lets him keep his sword (Book 7, Ch21 L21-25); escorts Jason's group to the cloud house (Book 7, Ch53 L102); Jason tells him to hear his debrief (Book 7, Ch35 L72); stands with Liara when Zara confronts them (Book 7, Ch46 L81).

### 7. Relationships

- **Liara**: stands beside her (Book 7, Ch46 L81).
- **Vesper Rimaros**: the royal who gives him leave to keep his sword (Book 7, Ch21 L21-25).

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

**Voice (condensed)**: Watchful and reserved; reads places and people for danger. Cue: dropping to one knee.

## Umber

### 1. Summary

Umber is Shade's brother, an astral being of the Reaper's kind who trapped Shade in an astral space for centuries and, in Book 13, serves Knowledge's plan against Jason. Sensuous, opportunistic and bitter, he plays games when Shade's power is limited by a vessel.

### 2. Appearance

- Appears as a mass of shadow with smoky orange eyes (Book 13, Ch1024 L100-104).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Resentful of change**: fixated on the idea that changing from the original state means falling from grace; he hates Shade for embracing it (Book 13, Ch981 L62-64).
- **Opportunistic and bitter**: he plays games when Shade's power is limited by a vessel (Book 8, Ch55 L86).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- He built the bridge anchor ritual to bind Jason's consciousness into the prime avatar (Book 13, Ch1024 L118-127); a word from Jason makes him reel (Book 13, Ch1024 L138).

### 5. Background

- Shade says Umber told him he had Shade trapped in an astral space for centuries "to teach you a lesson about duty" (Book 8, Ch55 L85-86).
- Umber persuaded Shade's summoner to trap him (Book 13, Ch1024 L118; Book 11, Ch62 L36).
- Astral beings are things of spirit with defined natures: Colin an avatar of hunger, Gordon a herald of annihilation, Shade "a shepherd of death" (Book 13, Ch981 L37).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 8**: Shade recounts his imprisonment (Book 8, Ch55 L85-86).
- **Book 13**: Shade explains the siblings (Book 13, Ch981 L37-64); marshalling yard (Book 13, Ch1024 L100-138).

### 7. Relationships

- **Shade**: brother and enemy (Book 13, Ch981 L62-64).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

He serves Knowledge's plan against Jason (Book 13, Ch1024 L118-127).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Sensuous, opportunistic and bitter.

## Valdis Volaire

### 1. Summary

A swordmaster prince of the Kingdom of Mirrors whom Clive meets in the City of Fallen Echoes; he is cheerful, reckless and a rival and friend to Jason's team.

### 2. Facts

- Introduces himself as "Valdis" and praises Clive's reputation (Book 2, Ch48 L77); the system names him Valdis Volaire (Book 2, Ch51 L56).
- A prince of the small but influential Kingdom of Mirrors, whose borders have not changed in eight centuries (Book 2, Ch51 L8); his father, the Mirror King, is eight hundred years old and the kingdom is "thick with princes and princesses" (Book 2, Ch55 L63; Book 12, Ch15 L9).
- A reckless enthusiast who leads his three teammates up a tower in search of treasure (Book 2, Ch51 L9-10); he has a light-step power, a slow-fall power and a wall run (Book 2, Ch51 L17, L28, L32).
- He chooses the path of courage in the trial and is the first to step forward (Book 2, Ch51 L42; Book 2, Ch57 L63).
- A sword master, mobile striker and the stronger team's leader (Book 3, Ch4 L3, L7); his team is a highly efficient cohort trained since before they had essences (Book 3, Ch3 L80).
- His father collects him from Jason's ship, to Valdis's embarrassment (Book 3, Ch5 L42-50); he portals in for Jason's memorial (Book 3, Ch69 L895).
- By Book 12 he is Sigrid's husband (Book 12, Ch15 L8), assembles an arena event in under two days (Book 12, Ch16 L11), and fights Jason in a mirage chamber using Mind's Eye to sense the space around him (Book 12, Ch17 L55-73).

### 3. Timeline of involvement

- Book 2: Clive's team-mate in the City of Fallen Echoes; party and trials (Book 2, Ch48-61).
- Book 3: friendly rival team; mock battles (Book 3, Ch4; Book 5, Ch64 L24).
- Book 12: Mirror Kingdom arena duel with Jason (Book 12, Ch15-17).

### 4. Roleplay notes

Boisterous, flirtatious and fond of a good story ("the virile verve of ten men", Book 2, Ch61 L74); he loves duelling famous warriors for the push, not the win (Book 12, Ch17 L56).

## Velius

### 1. Summary

Velius is a tall celestine diamond-ranker, the prime vessel of the Reaper. Warm and wry in person, chilling when the Reaper speaks through him.

### 2. Appearance

- "A tall celestine, with dark skin and a bushy mound of curly, silver hair that matched his eyes" (Book 3, Ch69 L238).
- When the Reaper speaks, his eyes become black orbs and his voice turns cold and bleak (Book 11, Ch64 L51).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Warm**: Shako greets him warmly in the dome chamber (Book 3, Ch69 L233-237) and he waves Shako into a lounge chair (Book 3, Ch69 L242).
- **Rueful about descendants**: he says he made the mistake of getting his descendants out of trouble again and again until he washed his hands of them (Book 3, Ch69 L245).
- **Earnest in work**: Rufus finds him "earnest and diligent" in a role normally handled by the church of Fertility (Book 11, Ch68 L778).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Prime vessel of the Reaper (Book 11, Ch64 L9).
- With Raythe he leads the descent of peak diamond-rankers into the shaft (Book 11, Ch61 L8).

### 5. Background

- Someone who has known Velius a very long time calls him "an old friend" (Book 6, Ch35 L50).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 3**: the dome chamber (Book 3, Ch69 L233-251).
- **Book 11**: says the Builder is done with Pallimustus (Book 11, Ch22 L11); the descent (Book 11, Ch61 L8); the Reaper speaks through him (Book 11, Ch64 L51); asks for a meeting in the clan maternity ward (Book 11, Ch68 L947).

### 7. Relationships

- **Shako**: friendly rival (Book 3, Ch69 L233-237).
- **Raythe**: fellow peak diamond-ranker (Book 11, Ch61 L8).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

When he and Shako change, the Reaper speaks through Velius and the voice becomes cold (Book 3, Ch69 L250-251).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Warm and wry; chilling when the Reaper speaks through him. Cue: eyes turning to black orbs.

## Vesta Carmis Zell

### 1. Summary

Vesta Carmis Zell is the astral king who rules the messenger forces around Yaresh and keeps her servants capped with seals. Cold, curious and acquisitive, she treats the lives of her servants as experiments.

### 2. Appearance

Not described in the lines read.

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Cold and curious**: she watches servant race armies battle to the death, resurrecting them and bestowing abilities "to keep things interesting" (Book 9, Ch102 L65).
- **Soul engineer**: known for her fascination with soul engineering (Book 10, Ch1 L53).
- **Separate goals**: she chose a separate goal from the rest of the group and is young (Book 10, Ch15 L30-43).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- She feels one of her seals vanish when Jason removes it from Tera (Book 9, Ch102 L66-67).
- Jason says Vesta used Tera, keeping her at silver rank (Book 10, Ch2 L40).

### 5. Background

- "The astral king who rules the local messenger forces" and a known practitioner of soul engineering (Book 9, Ch78 L82).
- Marek served her until recently (Book 10, Ch1 L53).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 9**: introduced (Book 9, Ch78 L82); the seal incident (Book 9, Ch102 L65-67).
- **Book 10**: Jason removes her brand from Tera (Book 10, Ch2 L19); at the Council of Kings her prime avatar scolds Jamis (Book 10, Ch15 L8).
- **Book 11**: Boris says she hired messengers with elemental powers and would never accept a member of the Unorthodoxy, and has no idea he is one (Book 11, Ch24 L85-86).

### 7. Relationships

- **Marek, Tera**: servants (Book 10, Ch1 L53; Book 10, Ch2 L19).
- **Jamis Fran Muskar**: fellow king (Book 10, Ch15 L8).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Boris is of the Unorthodoxy and she does not know it (Book 11, Ch24 L85-86).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Cold, curious and acquisitive.

## Vincent Baudrillard

### 1. Summary

Vincent Baudrillard is a French swordsman from Saint-Étienne whom Rufus picked out young, now an upper-silver adventurer and Emi's love interest in 2038. Anxious and earnest around Emi, he is flustered by Jason's attention and by her teasing.

### 2. Appearance

- Increasingly dishevelled hair that "only further set off his rakish good looks" (Book 13, Ch971 L3).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Anxious**: pacing around a rooftop garden while Emi eats a sandwich and teases him (Book 13, Ch971 L3-28).
- **Driven**: his drive is more valuable than his talent; the Remore teaching method gives the most time to those with motivation (Book 13, Ch971 L51-52).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Swordsman, close to gold: his aura is in the upper reaches of silver (Book 13, Ch971 L55).
- Rufus picked him out early for his swordsmanship and self-motivation (Book 13, Ch971 L52).

### 5. Background

- Member of the Baudrillard family; Chloe Baudrillard, an epidemiologist Jason befriended, is of the same family (Book 11, Ch68 L633).
- Jason has watched him grow from a boy to a man through the domain (Book 13, Ch971 L50).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 13**: the Saint-Étienne rooftop scene (Book 13, Ch971 L3-56).

### 7. Relationships

- **Emi**: love interest; Jason's interest is as a match for her, and rank matters for the ageing question (Book 13, Ch971 L56).
- **Rufus**: his mentor (Book 13, Ch971 L52).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Open question: his exact relationship to Chloe Baudrillard (the text names the family, not the relation).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Anxious and earnest around Emi; flustered by Jason and her teasing.

## Vincent Trenslow

### 1. Summary

Vincent Trenslow is an Adventure Society official in Greenstone with a magnificent moustache, who runs Jason's field assessment and speaks to him with strict professionalism. By Book 12 he is a drooping senior official preparing for a shipload of gold-rankers.

### 2. Appearance

- A moustache that "extended past either side of his head" (Book 1, Ch54 L29); in Book 12 "everything about Vincent Trenslow was drooping except for his immaculate moustache" (Book 12, Ch28 L3).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Professional**: Rufus notes his manner "had been nothing but professional" (Book 1, Ch44 L23).
- **Barking**: "Mercer, if I see you try to use an ability on a fellow candidate again, you will fail on the spot" (Book 1, Ch54 L30).
- **Disdainful of favouritism**: he shows "a hint of disdain around the eyes" at Guy's division of the group (Book 1, Ch54 L41).
- **Unhappy official**: he explains an administrative error "unhappily" (Book 1, Ch44 L24).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- He uses a silver-grey recording crystal during assessments (Book 1, Ch54 L50-52).
- He identifies thirteen ratlings that would run to their burrows (Book 1, Ch54 L59).

### 5. Background

- Rufus worked closely with him during the last field assessment and called him "exactly what I expect from a Society official" (Book 1, Ch54 L32-33).
- He extends the director's apologies and says she is "new to the role" (Book 1, Ch44 L28).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 1**: explains the assessment procedure (Book 1, Ch44 L24-28; Book 1, Ch54 L35-60); hands Jason his badge and explains stars (Book 1, Ch62 L61-93).
- **Book 2-3**: drinks with Rufus on the houseboat (Book 3, Ch1 L115); at the marina group (Book 3, Ch22 L3); on the terrace with Rufus (Book 2, Ch28 L13).
- **Book 12**: managing requests from nobility before the gold-rankers arrive (Book 12, Ch28 L3).

### 7. Relationships

- **Rufus**: worked together on the assessment (Book 1, Ch54 L32).
- **Elspeth Arella**: his director (Book 1, Ch44 L28).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Strict and fair; he does not flatter. Cue: "You will fail on the spot."

## Yumi Asano

### 1. Summary

Yumi Asano is Jason's paternal grandmother and the matriarch of the Asano clan. She came to magic late in life and her flesh-shaping powers restored her youth, so she looks no older than Jason. Authoritative, affectionate and unimpressed by his status, she pushes him to formalise the clan.

### 2. Appearance

- Her flesh-warping powers restored her youth, giving her a mid-twenties appearance (Book 11, Ch68 L565); in Book 13 she looks to be in her early thirties (Book 13, Ch1002 L31).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **Stern**: Jason greets her "G'day, Nanna... Sorry, Grandmother" and earns a glare (Book 4, Ch74 L40).
- **Deliberate**: she quietly takes in Jason's explanation, sipping tea, before responding (Book 5, Ch12 L84).
- **Scolding**: she scolds Jason "in a very matronly tone" (Book 13, Ch1002 L31).
- **Wary**: she wonders whether any of the boy she knew is still inside Jason (Book 12, Ch2 L102).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Flesh-shaping powers (Book 11, Ch36 L8).
- Forbids members going far outside the domain (Book 11, Ch36 L8-12).

### 5. Background

- Jason's paternal grandmother (Book 11, Ch68 L565).
- Book 12 also calls a woman named Noriko "matriarch of the Asano clan" (Book 12, Ch63 L19); the two descriptions are not reconciled (open question).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 4**: raises her eyebrows at Jason (Book 4, Ch74 L43).
- **Book 5**: hears Jason's warning (Book 5, Ch12 L84); chats with Dawn (Book 5, Ch39 L125).
- **Book 6**: pushes Jason to formalise the clan (Book 6, Ch47 L58); raps Jason on the arm (Book 6, Ch25 L55).
- **Book 11-13**: zeppelin over Nitra (Book 11, Ch36 L9); contribution points (Book 11, Ch68 L934); Jason confides his fear of a god (Book 13, Ch1020 L19); sits as matriarch beside General Mills (Book 13, Ch1002 L23).

### 7. Relationships

- **Jason**: grandson (Book 4, Ch74 L40).
- **Erika**: shares contribution-point plans (Book 11, Ch68 L934).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Jason says "That's a god, Grandmother" about what awaits him (Book 13, Ch1020 L19).

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Authoritative, affectionate and unimpressed by his status. Cue: a glare at "Nanna."

## Zara Rimaros (Zara Nareen)

### 1. Summary

Zara is a celestine princess of the Storm Kingdom, the "Hurricane Princess". Jason meets her in a tent during the contest for the Scythe of the Reaper, when she is nineteen and he is iron-rank. Years later the scandal of her false engagement claim, her loss of the succession, and her adoption into her mother's house bring her to Team Biscuit and, in 2038, into a romance with Jason.

### 2. Appearance

Celestine with caramel skin, sapphire eyes and waterfall-blue hair (Book 2, Ch69 L16). After her adoption into her mother's House Nareen she has milky teal hair and eyes (Book 9, Ch40 L7-13); by Book 12 she is still "turning your hair and eyes copper" (Book 12, Ch12 L10).

### 3. Personality and voice

At first she is regal ("royal highness", Book 2, Ch65 L47) and wary: in Book 2 Jason teleports into her tent and offers gem-berry and milk-nut squares (Book 2, Ch65 L55). She invents a fiancé (Book 9, Ch40 L55) and tells Korinne "I'm looking for a place to belong" (Book 9, Ch40 L32). In Book 13 she tells Jason he is a terrible leader but "a good lord" and advises him to keep a consistent persona (Book 13, Ch969 L56-63).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- **Powers**: wind and water, big storms (Book 12, Ch0 L14 says she has "been blowing things up with big storms"); recovery, speed, astral and holy affinity (notes, Book 2).
- **Rank**: gold by Book 12: she stays in a suite fit for gold-rank adventurers (Book 12, Ch12 L3) and calls up a storm of gold-rank force (Book 13, Ch965 L86); her rank when she first meets Jason is not stated in the chapters read.

### 5. Background

Firstborn daughter of the Storm King, called the Hurricane Princess (Book 7, Ch5 L68-69); her brother Emiliano becomes Storm King, and the notes for Book 13 call him her "adopted cousin-brother", an adopted baby shielded from the parents' treason; Zara herself is adopted into her mother's House Nareen (Book 12, Ch12 L17-20). Vesper Rimaros is Zara's aunt (Book 2, Ch69 L18); Vesper says she is sixty-seven and calls Pelli "Aunt Pelli", who remembers her as a wilful girl on the island (Book 7, Ch15 L110-113), so the notes' "descendant of Pelli" is corrected to niece (or at least a younger relative); she hopes to reach gold during the surge (Book 7, Ch15 L114-115), which places her below gold, and she is silver rank ("Vesper's silver-rank vision", Book 7, Ch15 L74; "Vesper was only silver rank to Liara's gold", Book 7, Ch21 L32); Liara Rimaros is a gold-ranker of the royal house, and Zareen Rimaros, Zara's lady in waiting and cousin, is Liara's daughter (Book 8, Ch62 L32-36).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 2**: meets Jason in a tent at the Scythe contest; the Hurricane Princess at the farewell feast.
- **Book 7**: Zara had been matched with a member of House Irios, a political marriage the royals wanted for stability before the surge (Book 7, Ch18 L66-72).
- **Book 9**: she is a former princess of the Storm Kingdom by Book 9 (Book 9, Ch40 L21); she says "I'm Zara Nareen now" (Book 9, Ch40 L18) and that she adopted into her mother's house, whose colouration she wears (Book 9, Ch40 L13), to signal her withdrawal from the contest for the crown (Book 9, Ch40 L72).
- **Book 12**: meets Jason again after fifteen years (Book 12, Ch12 L20); has joined Team Biscuit (Book 12, Ch0 L14; Book 12, Ch49 L7).
- **Book 13**: she is left with Emi and Erika for an hour, and Jason's father and brother-in-law join them (Book 13, Ch956 L40); Jason tells Ken how they met twenty years ago (Book 13, Ch956 L41); she walks the promenade deck hand in hand with Jason (Book 13, Ch956 L3) and kisses him later in a scene about Allayeth and Rufus (Book 13, Ch1004 L44-52).

### 7. Relationships

Jason, Vesper and Liara Rimaros, Emiliano, Team Biscuit, Zareen Rimaros.

### 8. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Courtly, with a threat in the smile. Cue: "Might I introduce my aunt, Vesper Rimaros?" (Book 2, Ch69 L17). See `../10_Roleplay_Support/Tone_and_Voice.md`.

Courtly with a streak of mischief; storms for emphasis.

## Zareen Rimaros

### 1. Summary

Zareen Rimaros is Liara and Baseph's middle child: a three-star adventurer and political enthusiast with the royal family's sapphire hair and eyes. She serves as the royal family's liaison to Jason in Rimaros, is proposed as a political match, and in Book 13 is a lady in waiting to Princess Zara on the embassy to Earth. Her sister Dara and brother Joseph are covered in Baseph_and_the_Rimaros_Children.md.

### 2. Facts

- **Family**: "Dara was the eldest and, like the middle child, Zareen, had followed their mother into adventuring"; the youngest, Joseph, is an administrator (Book 8, Ch62 L32).
- **Appearance**: "physically smaller" than her sister, not inheriting her mother's height, but with "the iconic sapphire hair and eyes of the royal family" (Book 8, Ch62 L36).
- **Politics, not combat**: she is "much more interested in politics than her mother" (Book 8, Ch62 L36), and was close to Vesper, "picking up her relative's taste for the politics that Liara disdained but could never seem to escape" (Book 9, Ch11 L53).
- **Interest in Jason**: "I'm more interested in the man himself... Is it true that his aura is as strong as a gold-ranker's?" and Liara scolds her "Don't even think about it" (Book 8, Ch62 L54-59). Jason later says he is "not looking for the entanglements a political marriage would bring" (Book 8, Ch63 L106).
- **A political match**: Zara notes whether Jason chooses "Zareen, myself, someone else or no one at all" is up to him (Book 9, Ch12 L108); Dara and Baseph exchange looks about Zareen's absence from dinner (Book 9, Ch11 L51). Rufus guesses she would be the royal choice, since her sister is "pure adventurer" without political sensibilities (Book 9, Ch12 L89).
- **Liaison**: she is the royal family liaison to Jason's team (Book 9, Ch13 L45). Liara scolds her for making "a bold move instead of talking to your mother about it because you knew she would be against it" (Book 9, Ch14 L61).
- **At the duel and ball**: she sits with Jason and Liara at the confrontation with Hector de Varco (Book 9, Ch16 L3), asks whether he is "remotely torturing a group of gold-rankers" (Book 9, Ch18 L15), and asks "Did you plan for the king to step in?" (Book 9, Ch15 L103).
- **Intelligence on the duel**: she explains that most of a rival guild fought the city attack on Livaros, with its special members on monster watch on Provo (Book 9, Ch15 L16).
- **Book 12**: she is assigned to the Rimaros diplomatic delegation to Earth (Book 12, Ch56 L117).
- **Book 13**: "technically a princess, but far enough down the hierarchy that she was formally referred to as 'lady'"; she is something like a lady in waiting to Princess Zara and "had a history with Jason... mostly a social connection, through her mother" (Book 13, Ch953 L50-51). She teases Zara by swooning at her pacing (Book 13, Ch953 L56).

### 3. Roleplay notes

Sharp, strategic and amused: she sizes people up for leverage, enjoys politics and teases her cousins. She says what she wants and tests how far the answer will bend.

## Zato

### 1. Summary

Zato is the silver-rank leader of the Builder cult's local forces in Book 3, a metal-bodied shapeshifter who recruits Thadwick, drives the cult's survivors to the Vane Estate and is the final opponent of Jason's team. He is competent, unfazed and sure of victory.

### 2. Appearance

- A silvery metal body that flows "like quicksilver", reshaping itself to produce combat abilities (Book 3, Ch67 L69).

### 3. Personality and voice

- **On top of things**: Jason says "He does seem pretty on top of things... I actually kind of like him" and invites him to join team "Hopelessly Outmatched" (Book 3, Ch57 L119).
- **Convinced of victory**: "Zato knew that his victory was imminent. He knew that the adventurers were no match for his power" (Book 3, Ch68 L60).
- **Quiet in command**: he stands with his back to the door, eyes lingering on Timos's neck marks, saying nothing (Book 3, Ch41 L73).
- **Recruiter**: "I see your true potential" (Book 3, Ch46 L60).

### 4. Powers and skills as world facts

- Silver rank, with a metal body of shifting abilities (Book 3, Ch67 L69).
- Immovable in the final fight: no damage seems to impair him, even Humphrey's strikes (Book 3, Ch68 L46).
- Trump card: after baiting out Sophie's absorb power, his body explodes into a mass of shrapnel (Book 3, Ch67 L100).

### 5. Background

- "The last silver-ranker left in the Builder cult's local forces"; tasked with leading the evacuation when the island stronghold was invaded, he escaped with a good number of people, though none of the other silver-rankers survived (Book 3, Ch7 L88-89).

### 6. Timeline of involvement

- **Book 3**: leads the evacuation (Book 3, Ch7 L88-89); stands before the inert archway (Book 3, Ch41 L73); recruits Thadwick (Book 3, Ch46 L60); asks what to do with bronze-rankers the cult cannot convert with clockwork cores (Book 3, Ch60 L37); falls before Jason and Sophie flee to the gate (Book 3, Ch66 L45); the climax with Humphrey and Sophie (Book 3, Ch67 L69-100; Book 3, Ch68 L46-61).

### 7. Relationships

- **Thadwick Mercer**: his recruit (Book 3, Ch46 L60).
- **Humphrey and Sophie**: opponents in the climax (Book 3, Ch68 L58-60).
- **Timos**: his follower, whose neck he notices (Book 3, Ch41 L73).

### 8. Secrets and spoiler notes

Nothing hidden in the lines read.

### 9. Roleplay notes

**Voice (condensed)**: Measured, zealous and confident until the very end. Cue: "I see your true potential."

## Colin

### 1. Summary

Jason's first familiar: a swarm of apocalypse leeches that lives in his blood, sprays out over enemies to bite and drain them, and can take the shape of a red-eyed blood clone of Jason. Colin begins as a hungry, wriggling swarm and grows into a being who talks back, waves from his bowl of leeches and calls Jason "smarmy".

### 2. Facts

- **Named**: Jason says, "I've decided to call him Colin. And his friends. Team Colin" (Book 1, Ch30 L85), and calls the swarm "Leechy" in the same fight (Book 1, Ch29 L23).
- **Lives in Jason's blood**: Jason pricks his finger and the leeches crawl into his hand and vanish into his blood (Book 1, Ch72 L32). His rapid regeneration only works while the familiar is in his bloodstream (Book 1, Ch72 L32).
- **Method**: Jason sprays him out over a target like a fire hose and Colin crawls over armour to find flesh (Book 3, Ch8 L76; Book 7, Ch26 L22). Colin wiggles happily when pleased (Book 3, Ch21 L132).
- **Where he comes from**: a summoned familiar is created through different means from the sanguine horror, but Clive observes it is what Jason summoned (Book 1, Ch75 L12), and if Jason reached diamond his familiar would reach the full strength of a sanguine horror (Book 1, Ch75 L14).

### 3. Later developments, Books 5 to 9

- **Silver vessel**: he needs a silver-rank vessel with simple requirements, such as a wheelbarrow-load of silver-rank blood quintessence (Book 5, Ch27 L57).
- **Blood clone**: Colin takes a form like a blood clone of Jason (Book 6, Ch29 L10), and Clive can switch-teleport him (Book 8, Ch10 L30).
- **Origin**: he comes from the border between the realms of the All-Devouring Eye and Legion, where life and annihilation are neighbours (Book 8, Ch55 L92).
- **Refined**: Jason refines his physical vessel with the astral throne and his connections with the astral gate (Book 9, Ch64 L90). A window offers him the chance to awaken as a Voice of the Will after extended hibernation in the astral kingdom (Book 9, Ch69 L55).

### 4. Later developments, Books 10 to 13 (spoilers)

- **Voice of the Will**: "Your familiar and bonded avatar [Colin] has become your [Voice of the Will]" (Book 10, Ch34 L24). He spends time in a cocoon while Jason is busy (Book 10, Ch5 L24).
- **He speaks**: "Justice?" (Book 10, Ch34 L72); "Smarmy?" he calls back at Jason (Book 11, Ch68 L2513); Jason thanks him quietly (Book 12, Ch34 L6).
- **Hunger**: Shade names Colin an avatar of hunger (Book 13, Ch981 L37). Colin says that going over his usual limit burns through the magic he feeds on and he must keep feeding on the vine to keep it up (Book 13, Ch1015 L26). He devours a creature's remains and brings back a sample (Book 13, Ch958 L80), and a bloody hand grows out of his bowl of leeches and meat to wave at Jason (Book 13, Ch981 L52).
- **Shaped by Jason**: Shade says Jason has shaped Colin and Gordon "like a parent" (Book 13, Ch981 L51).

### 5. Using this in a story

Colin is a mascot who happens to be a nightmare. He is happiest eating, enjoys his role in a fight and has become a person with opinions, so play him as cheerfully ravenous rather than menacing. His regeneration is a reason Jason does not use him lightly in crowds of friends, and his hunger limits what he can do for long.
