## Gordon

### 1. Summary

Jason's third familiar: an Avatar of Doom, a floating cloak holding a nebula in the shape of an eye, circled by blue and orange eye-orbs that fire beams. He cannot speak, but he answers questions with his orbs and has a distinct personality, and he is the key to the intrinsic-mandate magic Jason uses to work with authority.

### 2. Facts

- **Summoned**: the doom essence ability Avatar of Doom summons a familiar (Book 2, Ch64 L12). At first it is unnamed, an iron-rank incorporeal familiar whose orbs make sustained beams, one of disruptive force and one of resonating force, and whose damage leaves Vulnerable (Book 2, Ch72 L140-144).
- **Named**: asked if it wants a name, it flashes its blue orb, and Jason says, "I'm going to call you... Gordon" (Book 2, Ch72 L148-155). Orange is no and blue is yes: Gordon's orange orb flashes brightly as his signal for no (Book 3, Ch46 L96). Shade relays him: "Gordon says that I should be last" (Book 3, Ch46 L95).
- **Appearance**: a disembodied cloak with a nebula-like cloud of blue and orange in the shape of an eye, and eyeball-patterned orbs drifting around it that fire unrelenting beams (Book 3, Ch4 L28).
- **In a fight**: his beams inflict Vulnerable on a lizard (Book 3, Ch8 L76); his energy dash is fast but his reflexes are sluggish, and a blow can dissipate his vessel entirely (Book 3, Ch13 L38).

### 3. Later developments, Books 5 to 9

- **Subsumed**: while he is subsumed into Jason at silver rank, Jason can call up one of each orb to use for himself (Book 5, Ch49 L43).
- **Shields**: his orbs make shields that protect Jason (Book 6, Ch38 L35; Book 7, Ch26 L29).
- **Reputation**: the Magic Society has only iron- and bronze-rank information on the "floating death orbs" and finds it terrifying (Book 8, Ch25 L48).
- **Origin**: he comes from the realm of the All-Devouring Eye (Book 8, Ch55 L92).
- **The orrery**: in Book 9 he draws a glowing orrery that looks like a solar system made of fireworks, a work he completes by floating down next to Jason (Book 9, Ch94 L92).

### 4. Later developments, Books 10 to 13 (spoilers)

- **The library**: he spends months with some of Jason's avatars in the soul-realm library (Book 10, Ch5 L24).
- **Intrinsic-mandate magic**: Jason can reach it through Gordon, who executes the actual magic while Jason guides the authority with will (Book 11, Ch33 L152-153).
- **Personality**: he answers Colin with more flashing lights (Book 11, Ch1 L87), sits next to Jason on the couch and sends an orb to absorb a portion of the juice (Book 13, Ch981 L26), watches the film with his orbs (Book 13, Ch981 L52) and fights a flying dogfight with an enemy (Book 13, Ch976 L49). He detonates orbs to clear space for Jason (Book 13, Ch1012 L26).
- **Nature**: Shade calls him a herald of annihilation (Book 13, Ch981 L37).

### 5. Using this in a story

Gordon is the silent member of the household, and the humour comes from how much he communicates without words. He is not shown speaking in the lines checked, so give him lights, orb movement and a taste for whatever Jason is eating. His orbs are the best shield and ranged support Jason has, and his dependence on his vessel is his weakness. Note that a different Gordon, a human, is called "Other Gordon" in Books 4 and 5 (Book 4, Ch38 L26: "Hanging Rock?" Other Gordon asked).

---

## Onslow

### 1. Summary

Clive Standish's familiar: a rune tortoise whose shell carries runes that throw elemental attacks, and whose shell the whole team rides in, shelters in and runs the battlefield from. Onslow is gentle and a little stubborn, and Clive talks to him as "little buddy".

### 2. Facts

- **First sight**: Onslow is at the front of Clive's airboat with his head jutting forward "like a dog with its head out a car window" (Book 1, Ch68 L106). Clive sits on his shell with Jason beside him (Book 1, Ch69 L56).
- **Powers**: he fires elemental attacks from the magic runes on his shell, which Clive recharges with his own mana (Book 3, Ch4 L29; Book 3, Ch38 L54). A rune dims when he takes a hit (Book 1, Ch56 L24).
- **A seat for the team**: Clive picks up Stash and climbs on Onslow's shell with Neil, and the tortoise floats off the rooftop on a cushion of air (Book 3, Ch66 L46-47). Clive drops down off him when the tower is threatened (Book 3, Ch69 L97).

### 3. Later developments, Books 7 to 9

- **Precaution**: when a familiar tears open the side of a ship, Clive sends Onslow out as a precaution (Book 7, Ch6 L52).
- **Power in a fight**: he pours elemental magic into the enemy from his rune shell, throwing hailstones and lightning bolts (Book 8, Ch10 L29).
- **Open-sided craft**: he expands his shell into an open-sided flying craft, and the unshelled tortoise takes the form of a small green humanoid wearing a child's clothes from Clive, "an adorable team mascot" (Book 9, Ch81 L23).
- **Under fire**: his shell draws constant barrage from the monsters, which Clive answers with ritual-enhanced wind barriers (Book 9, Ch87 L24). Humphrey tells Belinda to keep anyone from focusing on Onslow (Book 9, Ch84 L23).
- **"Little buddy"**: Clive asks, "What do you say, little buddy? Can you get us down any faster?" (Book 9, Ch97 L49).

### 4. Later developments, Books 10 to 13 (spoilers)

- **Bunker and command post**: the shell serves as a bunker where Neil, Clive and Belinda work and where freed silver-rankers recover (Book 10, Ch61 L30), and as the safest location of the expedition because it absorbs elemental attacks (Book 10, Ch70 L20).
- **Carrier**: it holds adventurers and brighthearts in an empty tunnel (Book 10, Ch79 L3), and the team crosses overland in it with the sides open (Book 11, Ch53 L12).
- **House-sized**: in Book 13 the shell has expanded to the size of a house, serving as a combination command centre, rest area and triage tent (Book 13, Ch966 L3). Those who cannot fly ride in Onslow's expanded shell (Book 12, Ch53 L90).
- **Plodding**: when a child demands he go faster he plods over the grass on thick legs, to the child's complaint (Book 11, Ch20 L19).
- **Friendly**: he returns Neil's fist bump with a three-fingered fist (Book 13, Ch1007 L77).

### 5. Using this in a story

Onslow is the team's place of safety. A party that has him can retreat, heal and regroup in the middle of a battle, and a story that removes him removes that base. Play him as slow, kind and immovable, a mascot who also happens to be a fortress.

---

## Shade

### 1. Summary

Jason's shadow familiar, a formal, dry astral being who is one of the Reaper's shadows. He first appears as the keeper of the Reaper trials, becomes Jason's closest and most constant companion, and acts as his butler, driver, spy and sounding board. He says himself that he is a shepherd of death, and that he has changed more than the others of his kind.

### 2. Facts

- **The invigilator**: he appears as the shadowy figure who runs the trials of the City of Fallen Echoes and offers to explain their practical dangers or their origins (Book 2, Ch44 L65). He hands out vials and medallions with his shadowy hands, which are cold to the touch (Book 2, Ch44 L119).
- **A familiar before**: he tells the competitors that the grandmaster who built the place was an outworlder with the dark essence like Jason, "I was his summoned familiar once" (Book 2, Ch44 L93).
- **Summoned by Jason**: when Jason chooses to summon a familiar after the trials, he greets Shade with "I was hoping it would be you" (Book 2, Ch72 L28).
- **Bodies**: he appears as three bodies that become horses for a ride (Book 3, Ch5 L80) or large lizards for rough terrain (Book 3, Ch60 L8), and his bodies move among monsters as elusive shadowy figures (Book 3, Ch49 L45).
- **The Reaper's child**: the Reaper says "Of all my children, Shade has ever followed his own path" (Book 3, Ch69 L306).

### 3. Later developments, Books 4 to 9

- **Manner**: formal, dry and discreet. He objects to "a decidedly indiscreet practice in the middle of the day" (Book 4, Ch9 L21), is told by Jason to "please show our guests out" (Book 4, Ch45 L81), and is described by Jason as "very nice" and "a good friend, even if he does occasionally keep things from me" (Book 4, Ch32 L21).
- **The Reaper's view**: he tells Jason, "You have a habit of not staying dead. This is not something the Reaper likes. You have its gratitude, however" (Book 4, Ch3 L28).
- **Vehicles**: he drives as a sports car and then a sleek four-door sedan (Book 4, Ch5 L33), and drives a motorhome onto the water (Book 4, Ch24 L33). Jason calls him "the single greatest thing on this planet" when he arrives as the car (Book 4, Ch3 L83).
- **A voice**: his voice can come from Jason's shadow, as when he speaks for Jason in a meeting (Book 4, Ch46 L78), and Jason can channel his sight and voice through him (Book 4, Ch18 L40). Jason compares talking through him to a better phone (Book 4, Ch50 L76).
- **Silver rank**: his bodies can teleport between each other (Book 5, Ch16 L103-108).
- **Brother**: Umber trapped him in an astral space for centuries (Book 8, Ch55 L85-86); see `../Umber.md`.

### 4. Later developments, Books 10 to 13 (spoilers)

- **Nature**: Shade tells Jason that astral beings are things of spirit with defined natures, and that Colin was born an avatar of hunger, Gordon a herald of annihilation and he himself a shepherd of death (Book 13, Ch981 L37).
- **Familiars develop personalities**: he says astral beings are uniform until physical reality gives them idiosyncrasies, "that is the gift that mortals give us", and that Jason has shaped Colin and Gordon "like a parent" (Book 13, Ch981 L51).
- **A falling out**: his previous summoner severed their bond and bound him to the place where he and Jason met, with Umber's interference (Book 13, Ch981 L33-35). Shade explains that Umber fixed on the idea that changing from the original state means falling from grace (Book 13, Ch981 L62).
- **Sanctioning himself**: Shade spends authority accumulated over tens of thousands of years, becomes a Shadow of the Hegemon, and accepts avatar status, which makes the familiar contract permanent (Book 11, Ch68 L2205-2218). The Reaper warns "Sanctioning can so easily go wrong" (Book 11, Ch68 L2220).
- **Vehicles in the astral kingdom**: his black skimmer is free of colour, and letting Colin and Gordon influence it would add defensive properties (Book 12, Ch9 L7).
- **Size**: Jason's gold-rank sheet lists Shadow of the Hegemon as three bodies at iron, seven at bronze, thirty-one at silver and two hundred and eleven at gold (Book 12, Ch67 L229-232).

### 5. Using this in a story

Shade is the straight man to Jason's jokes and the one who says the sensible thing in the plainest words. He is loyal but not transparent; he keeps secrets for reasons he considers good, and he is not afraid to let Jason be wrong. His speech is formal and unhurried. He can carry Jason, his luggage, his voice and his mana-draining attacks, so a story that removes him leaves Jason without a driver, a go-between and an informant at once.

---

## Shimmer

### 1. Summary

Belinda Callahan's astral lantern: a small living lantern that orbits her, projects shields, fires force bolts and feeds mana to her team. It is the quietest of the team's familiars, but it is on the field in almost every battle.

### 2. Facts

- **Summoned**: the final ability of Belinda's power set is a summoned familiar, an astral lantern (Book 2, Ch71 L50). Belinda names it: "How about Shimmer?" (Book 2, Ch72 L62).
- **In a fight**: it projects shields to protect the team (Book 3, Ch4 L32) and, with Gordon, beams the enemy to split their attention (Book 3, Ch11 L68). The force bolts of a lantern familiar prove more dangerous to its own side against Hendren's defences (Book 3, Ch58 L60).

### 3. Later developments, Books 7 to 9

- **Mana supply**: against constructs its attacks do little, so it mostly replenishes mana (Book 7, Ch4 L78). At the battle of Yaresh it fires force bolts at worms and pumps out mana to the team (Book 9, Ch59 L67; Book 9, Ch82 L36).
- **Pairing**: Belinda's other familiar replicates Humphrey, swinging a huge sword (Book 7, Ch4 L78).

### 4. Later developments, Books 10 to 12 (spoilers)

- **Rapid-fire bolts**: its force bolts are as effective as Gordon's beams against flaming and gaseous elementals (Book 10, Ch61 L28).
- **Echo spirit**: Belinda's two summoned familiars are the astral lantern, which orbits her droopily, and an echo spirit that looks like a blurry version of her (Book 12, Ch27 L23).

### 5. Using this in a story

Shimmer is the supply line: shields, bolts and mana. It has little personality in the text beyond its droopy orbit when Belinda is tired, so play it as a quiet companion rather than a speaker.

---

## Stash

### 1. Summary

Humphrey Geller's bonded familiar: a baby mirage dragon whose full name is Velitraxistaasch, who prefers "Stash". He changes shape constantly, starts as a barking lizard, a bird or a puppy and ends up large enough to crush a company of messengers, and he talks, mostly in cheerful, blunt remarks.

### 2. Facts

- **Name**: "It's short for Velitraxistaasch. He likes 'Stash,' though." (Book 1, Ch38 L58). Jason works out what he is at once and Humphrey is startled (Book 1, Ch38 L59-61).
- **Bond**: "Our mothers arranged him becoming my familiar. Or me becoming his person, depending on how you look at it" (Book 1, Ch38 L64). A bonded familiar is an actual magical creature that can die, unlike a summoned familiar (Book 2, Ch42 L70).
- **Shapes**: a canary on Humphrey's head and a puppy (Book 1, Ch38 L62), a bird that swoops from the sky and turns into a puppy in his arms (Book 2, Ch20 L29), a barking lizard (Book 1, Ch78 L84), and a bark lurker or a darting bird in a fight (Book 3, Ch4 L31).
- **Biscuits**: Jason feeds him a biscuit and he turns into a puppy to snuffle it from Jason's hand, then yaps his agreement (Book 1, Ch78 L85-88; Book 2, Ch70 L11).
- **Speech**: "Stash chase worm! Stash chase worm!" (Book 1, Ch87 L180).
- **Scouting**: he leads Humphrey's party by barking in the right direction to the margolls (Book 2, Ch20 L31).
- **Special attack**: Humphrey's racial ability evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon (Book 2, Ch61 L147).

### 3. Later developments, Books 6 to 9

- **Mother**: his mother is Carlivexistrix, a vast dragon with scales of changing rainbow colours who asks to be called Carli (Book 6, Ch47 L736-738, L804). Humphrey apologises for not doing the best job of helping her little boy grow up (Book 6, Ch47 L737).
- **Language**: "Porky pies!" and "Stick it up your bum, lady" at a Magic Society official, and "Telling people to bugger off is kind of my thing" (Book 6, Ch47 L761-763).
- **With Sophie**: he is sprawled in Sophie's lap in puppy form (Book 7, Ch57 L34), and she keeps biscuits for him (Book 7, Ch6 L87).
- **Forms in battle**: a marsh hydra (Book 8, Ch10 L29), a copy of Belinda and then of Jason (Book 8, Ch42 L35), and a hopping insect that pulls Neil out of a messenger's path (Book 9, Ch98 L93).
- **Given a task**: Jason tells him to stick to the messengers and keep them safe (Book 9, Ch81 L35).

### 4. Later developments, Books 10 to 13 (spoilers)

- **Team Biscuit**: asked whether a familiar picked the team name, someone answers "Actually, yes, they did" (Book 10, Ch47 L78).
- **Size and strength**: he is a giant who smashes Dustin and Rick together, impaling messengers (Book 10, Ch70 L38). In Book 11 the text calls him "boy Stash", who demands "Faster!" (Book 11, Ch20 L19).
- **Bird-lizard**: he leaps from Humphrey's clothes as something between a bird and a lizard (Book 12, Ch47 L61).

### 5. Using this in a story

Stash is the team's most affectionate and least filtered voice. He is a dragon child, so give him a child's appetite for biscuits, praise and bad language, and a child's sudden courage. Keep him changing shape. His mother is a major dragon, which is a hook if the story needs dragon allies.

## Family Trees

### 1. Summary

This file gathers who is related to whom in the six family lines roleplay needs most: the Asano family (with the Evans line through Erika), the Remores, the Gellers, the Mercers and their circle, and the Rimaros royal house. It adds nothing that the character files do not already cite; its job is to put the links in one place. The file is level 3 throughout because it names deaths and Book 13 outcomes.

### 2. How to read the trees

- A line like "A → B" means A is a parent of B as the cited chapter says.
- "Spouse" and "partner" are given only where the text says so.
- Where the text is silent or two sources disagree, the item is listed under "Open points" at the end of that section.

### 3. The Asano family (Jason's line)

#### Grandparents and parents

- **Yumi Asano**, Jason's paternal grandmother, whose flesh-warping powers restored her youth; she looks no older than her mid-twenties (Book 4, Ch74 L40; Book 11, Ch68 L565). In Book 13 she sits as matriarch of the clan (Book 13, Ch1002 L23).
- Jason's **other grandmother**, his mother's mother, is seen "chugging a beer" beside Yumi (Book 4, Ch74 L43) and had a miraculous recovery that sets his mother's thoughts racing (Book 4, Ch35 L52).
- **Ken Asano**, Jason's father, was born in Japan and raised in Australia from a very young age (Book 1, Ch1 L88). His brothers are the elder **Shiro**, "the favourite", and **Hiro**, "the disappointment"; Ken "laid low in the middle" (Book 4, Ch7 L10).
- **Cheryl Asano**, Jason's mother, comes from a farming and mining family and was the one fascinated with Japan (Book 1, Ch1 L88). Her brother is **Robert** (Book 4, Ch31 L3).

#### Jason and his siblings

- **Kaito** is Jason's older brother by a year (Book 2, Ch11 L65); **Erika** is the older sister (Book 5, Ch56 L7). Jason is the youngest of the three.
- Kaito married **Amy**, the girl next door, who is Jason's childhood best friend (Book 4, Ch26 L47; Book 4, Ch3 L133). Their daughters are **Hana** (twenty-three in 2038) and **Jace** (nineteen) (Book 13, Ch950 L29). Kaito dies in Book 5 (Book 5, Ch52 L20).
- Erika married **Ian Evans**, a doctor (Book 4, Ch3 L123); their daughter is **Emi** (Book 4, Ch3 L132), twelve in Book 4 (Book 4, Ch25 L60).

#### The extended line

- Emi's cousins are Hana and Jace, and her great-grandmother Yumi is "Nana Yumi" to her (Book 4, Ch56 L46; Book 11, Ch68 L836-837).
- **Nik**, the rabbit Jason brought into being when his soul realm became a transformation zone, calls Jason "Dad" (Book 11, Ch61 L16; Book 12, Ch39 L15).
- Families brought into the clan through Jason's circle include those of Greg and Asya (Book 11, Ch68 L632) and Chloe Baudrillard's (Book 11, Ch68 L633).

#### The old Japanese clan

- The Japanese Asano clan is a separate line. Its patriarch is a silver-rank man named Shiro, father of **Akari**; Jason's own eldest paternal uncle is also named Shiro, a different man (Book 5, Ch34 L70). Its strongest member is **Noriko**, the patriarch's mother (Book 5, Ch36 L3). Jason tells her "My Asano family and your Asano clan henceforth have no connections" (Book 5, Ch37 L92).
- Akari married **Itsuki Tiwari** of the Tiwari clan (Book 13, Ch1004 L4-5); his father is Koya, youngest of three elders (Book 5, Ch39 L3).

#### Open points

- How the Japanese patriarch's line connects to Ken and Hiro's family is not stated in the lines read.
- Book 12 calls Noriko "matriarch of the Asano clan" while Yumi is also called matriarch (Book 12, Ch63 L19); the two descriptions are not reconciled.

### 4. The Remore family

- **Roland Remore**, diamond-rank sword master and archchancellor, is Gabriel's father ("It's Dad", Book 12, Ch45 L56) and Rufus's grandfather (Book 3, Ch20 L25).
- **Gabriel** and **Arabelle** are husband and wife (Book 3, Ch1 L73); Roland is Arabelle's father-in-law (Book 10, Ch14 L50).
- Their sons are **Gwydion**, the older, a priest of Hero (Book 11, Ch67 L20), and **Rufus** (Book 2, Ch33 L6). Arabelle once said "I think it's time for another child, husband. A daughter, this time" (Book 3, Ch1 L73).

### 5. The Geller family

- **Danielle Geller** and **Keith Geller** are husband and wife; their children are **Henrietta**, the older sister, and **Humphrey** (Book 2, Ch62 L24).
- **Rick** and **Phoebe** are brother and sister of a distant branch; Phoebe is a distant cousin of Humphrey (Book 1, Ch66 L3-4; Book 1, Ch110 L51).
- **Jonah Geller** was Rick's cousin, whom he failed to save (Book 2, Ch17 L10). **Henry Geller** is also named on Rick's team (Book 1, Ch110 L51).
- **Dustin Kettering** replaced Jonah on Rick's team (Book 12, Ch16 L83) and is cousin to **Hudson Kettering** (Book 2, Ch15 L44).
- Rick married **Hannah Adeah** (Book 12, Ch15 L6).

### 6. The Mercers and their circle

- **Beaufort Mercer** is the Duke of Greenstone's brother and **Thalia Mercer** is his wife, a silver-rank adventurer (Book 1, Ch77 L47; Book 2, Ch59 L4).
- Their children are **Cassandra** and **Thadwick**; Cassandra is the older (Book 2, Ch27 L43). Thalia "looked more like her daughter's sister than her parent" (Book 1, Ch65 L120).
- **Neil Davone** grew up in the Mercer orbit because the Davone and Kettering families had close ties to the Mercers (Book 2, Ch27 L41).

### 7. The Rimaros royal house

- **Soramir Rimaros** is the founder; even the Storm King defers to him (Book 9, Ch14 L4).
- The **Storm King**'s firstborn daughter is **Zara**, the Hurricane Princess (Book 7, Ch5 L68-69). Her brother **Emiliano** becomes Storm King (Book 12, Ch12 L17-20); the notes for Book 13 call him her adopted cousin-brother (notes, Book 13). Zara later adopts into her mother's House Nareen (Book 9, Ch40 L18).
- **Vesper Rimaros** is Zara's aunt (Book 2, Ch69 L18) and is sixty-seven (Book 7, Ch15 L110-113).
- **Liara Rimaros** comes from "one of the more remote branches of the royal family" (Book 7, Ch17 L14). She married **Baseph**, born into House Amouz (Book 7, Ch17 L19-20; Book 9, Ch5 L3). Their children are **Dara**, **Zareen** and **Joseph** (Book 8, Ch62 L28-39).
- Liara calls **Cassin Amouz** "Uncle Cassin" when angry (Book 8, Ch20 L21).
- **Pelli** is "Aunt Pelli" to Vesper (Book 7, Ch15 L67); the text does not say she is a blood relative.

## Knowledge States: Who Knows What, and When

### 1. Summary

This file tracks four things a roleplayer needs to keep straight for the core characters: whether the character knows that Jason is an outworlder from Earth, how much they know about the party interface and the later System, what they know about the Earth-Pallimustus link and Earth's magic, and what they know of Knowledge's plan. For each, it names the earliest scene where the text shows the character knowing, and the band of books that scene falls in. It is the character-by-character companion to the secrets table in Spoiler_Management.md.

### 2. Method and limits

- **First evidence, not full proof.** An entry says "Book N" when a cited line shows the character with the knowledge. The character may have known earlier in a scene the compendium has not read; a blank means no scene was found.
- **Bands.** A = Books 1-3; B = Books 4-6; C = Books 7-9; D = Books 10-13. A character shown as knowing in band A is assumed to know in every later band unless the text says otherwise.
- **Belief versus fact.** The table records what the character is shown to know or be told, not whether it is true.
- **Level 3.** The file is level 3 throughout because it names Book 13 reveals.

### 3. Topic 1: Jason is an outworlder from Earth

| Character | First evidence | Band |
|---|---|---|
| Rufus Remore | Rufus explains outworlders to Jason's circle, and Gabriel asks to be told about "this outworlder of yours" (Book 1, Ch15 L21; Book 1, Ch49 L42) | A |
| Farrah Hurin | "He's from another world, so there's no telling" (Book 1, Ch21 L82) | A |
| Gary | "And he's an outworlder... He didn't absorb his essences the same way we did" (Book 1, Ch21 L87) | A |
| Humphrey Geller | "Jason is from another world... You should get used to explaining things to him" (Book 1, Ch80 L7) | A |
| Clive Standish | Jason tells him: "Clive, I'm an outworlder" (Book 1, Ch68 L81) | A |
| Emir Bahadir | "This is why I like outworlders" (Book 1, Ch108 L6) | A |
| Danielle Geller | Investigates Jason at Gabriel's request, and Rufus is told "You know he's an outworlder" (Book 1, Ch48 L101-105) | A |
| Sophie Wexler | An outworlder-made stone is explained to her as being "like Jason's" (Book 2, Ch63 L27); no first-telling scene found | A (indirect) |
| Belinda Callahan | Shows she knows what an outworlder is while the group discusses Jason (Book 7, Ch37 L6); no first-telling scene found | C |
| Neil Davone | Asks "do all the outworlders get the drinking-baby-blood combination?" (Book 8, Ch45 L61); no first-telling scene found | C |
| Taika | An Earth native who deals with Jason in Sydney from Book 4 (Book 4, Ch33 L82) | B |

### 4. Topic 2: The party interface and the System

The party interface is an outworlder ability Jason evolves in Book 1 (Book 1, Ch87 L157-163); it gives party members chat and voice chat (Book 1, Ch89 L76). No first-use scene was found for Rufus, Farrah, Gary or Taika. The later, world-wide System is a separate matter and is covered below the table.

| Character | First evidence of using the party interface | Band |
|---|---|---|
| Sophie Wexler | Can see Jason's map when he does (Book 2, Ch43 L94) | A |
| Clive Standish | Combines the interface with his identification ability (Book 2, Ch51 L83) | A |
| Neil Davone | "Full [Party Interface] functionality has been restored to party member [Neil Davone]" (Book 2, Ch50 L8) | A |
| Humphrey Geller | Speaks to Jason over party chat (Book 2, Ch65 L89) | A |
| Belinda Callahan | Tries to shape-shift into Jason to replicate the interface and keeps getting the wrong power (Book 3, Ch1 L21) | A |

The System:

- **Appearance in the world.** At the end of Book 11, the System message "Welcome to the System" is shown (Book 11, Ch68 L2540). By Book 12, the world's people know the interface calling itself the System appeared and the Adventure Society linked it to Jason (Book 12, Ch1 L44-54).
- **Who knew Jason held it.** Anna Tilden suspects the System might be some cosmic force rather than Jason (Book 12, Ch42 L99); Jason is shown receiving the System administrator gift (Book 12, Ch10 L14-17).
- **Hazy memories.** The Book 12 characters say things were hazy when the System first appeared (Book 12, Ch2 L110).

### 5. Topic 3: The Earth link and Earth's magic

| Character | First evidence | Band |
|---|---|---|
| Arabelle Remore and others in Jason's hearing | Jason says his world "didn't have magic" and uses magician stage tricks to explain (Book 3, Ch29 L73-76) | A |
| Farrah Hurin | Travels between worlds with Jason; comments that "Earth is only just coming into real magic" and that Earth's grid and rift knowledge are limited (Book 7, Ch14 L29; Book 7, Ch55 L20); Jason credits her with working the Network to prevent complete disaster (Book 13, Ch1017 L40) | B |
| Clive Standish | Jason tells him about the door and the bridge in his soul and the astral instincts they give him (Book 8, Ch4 L92-104) | C |
| Humphrey Geller | Hears "Back on Earth as well, now it has magic too" (Book 9, Ch29 L60) | C |
| Travis Noble (and Earth natives) | Is himself from Earth, "the magical ordnance specialist from Earth" (Book 9, Ch81 L10), and plans relays inspired by Earth's detection grid (Book 9, Ch37 L24-28) | B |
| Rufus Remore and Taika | Travel to Earth with Boris in Book 11 (Book 11, Ch68 L305, L470-473) | D |
| Sophie, Belinda, Neil, Gary | No scene found of Jason explaining the Earth link to them individually; in Book 9 Neil says "no more people from Earth, or this will turn into a disaster" (Book 9, Ch21 L12) | C |

### 6. Topic 4: Knowledge's plan

| Character | First evidence | Band |
|---|---|---|
| Farrah Hurin | Jason tells her the Builder-and-outworlder story: a god makes a deal with the new Builder and "recruits an outworlder, originally from Earth" (Book 8, Ch57 L56); Knowledge herself is not named in the lines read | C |
| Everyone in the Book 13 lecture hall (Danielle Geller, Michael Mills and other leaders) | Jason lays out Knowledge's half-millennium plan, her deal with Purity and Disguise and the founder's mission (Book 13, Ch1017 L13-47); Danielle interjects "A lot" when Jason says Knowledge knew a lot (Book 13, Ch1017 L33) | D |
| Gabrielle Pellin | A cube leaves her chest into Knowledge's hand and she seizes (Book 13, Ch1023 L139); she is not shown as knowing the plan | D |
| Travis Noble | His negotiations with the Church of Knowledge over Earth magitech are part of the plan (Book 9, Ch13 L85); he is not shown as knowing | D |
| Humphrey, Sophie, Belinda, Clive, Neil, Gary, Rufus, Taika, Emir | No scene found in the lines read before Book 13 where Jason or anyone explains the plan to them; Jason tells the lecture hall in Book 13 (Book 13, Ch1017 L3-50) | D |

How others saw Knowledge before Book 13: as a charming, omniscient goddess who knows what everyone in her world knows (Book 1, Ch46 L22-50; Book 1, Ch77 L10).

### 7. Using the table

- **Rule of thumb.** Until a scene shows a character being told, do not let them speak with the knowledge. Use the band column as the earliest safe point.
- **Jason's own state.** Jason's own understanding of the plan sharpens across Books 8-13: by Book 8 he can summarise the Builder and outworlder story (Book 8, Ch57 L53-59), and by Book 13 he names Knowledge's role (Book 13, Ch1017 L31-32).
- **Open points.** First-telling scenes for Sophie, Belinda, Neil, Gary and the team's grasp of the Earth link are not found in the lines read. Add them here if a later pass finds them.

## Romances and Rivalries

### 1. Summary

This file lists romantic ties and standing rivalries between named characters, in the order a reader meets them. Romances are given as pairs with the book they begin, change or end; rivalries are given with what each side wants. It is level 3 because it includes outcomes up to Book 13.

### 2. Romances and marriages

#### Jason

- **Amy**: the girl next door and his best friend; she "had a crush on Kaito from an early age" and later returned Jason's feelings, but the fallout when she and Kaito got together ended it (Book 4, Ch26 L47-50). In Book 13 the history "hung in the air like London fog" (Book 13, Ch950 L30).
- **Cassandra Mercer**: they kiss in Book 1 (Book 1, Ch98 L35). Her family ends it because they decided he "wasn't going to amount to anything" (Book 11, Ch68 L1104). In Book 12 she finds him "different, yet the same", his features "sharper and less boyish" (Book 12, Ch46 L20).
- **Asya Karadeniz**: she enters his spirit vault "as her relationship with Jason deepened" (Book 5, Ch44 L45); she dies in Book 5 (Book 5, Ch51 L40).
- **Zara Rimaros**: the two are walking the promenade deck hand in hand in Book 13 (Book 13, Ch956 L3) and she kisses him later (Book 13, Ch1004 L44-52).

#### Others

- **Kaito and Amy**: married, with two daughters; Kaito dies in Book 5 (Book 4, Ch3 L133; Book 13, Ch950 L29).
- **Erika and Ian Evans**: married, with a daughter, Emi (Book 4, Ch3 L132).
- **Gabriel and Arabelle Remore**: married, with two sons (Book 3, Ch1 L73).
- **Danielle and Keith Geller**: married, with two children (Book 2, Ch62 L24).
- **Thalia and Beaufort Mercer**: married (Book 1, Ch77 L47).
- **Liara Rimaros and Baseph Amouz**: married for political reasons in youth, living largely separate lives but staying friends (Book 7, Ch17 L19-20).
- **Humphrey and Gabrielle Pellin**: they were a couple; he ended it (Book 2, Ch28 L25-30). Their break-up is partly blamed on her friction with Jason (Book 10, Ch8 L10). Gabrielle later marries **Travis Noble** (Book 13, Ch1016 L74).
- **Rick Geller and Hannah Adeah**: girlfriend, fiancée, then wife (Book 10, Ch1 L77-80; Book 12, Ch15 L6).
- **Valdis Volaire and Sigrid Freyn**: husband and wife (Book 12, Ch15 L8).
- **Emir Bahadir and Constance**: employer and chief of staff for years, then married (Book 6, Ch47 L494, L539-542; Book 12, Ch51 L49).
- **Belinda Callahan and Estella Warnock**: married by Book 13 (Book 13, Ch1011 L23).
- **Akari Asano and Itsuki Tiwari**: married; he leaves her in Book 13 so she can focus on the sword, saying "Your life doesn't have room for me anymore" (Book 13, Ch1004 L5-23).
- **Emi Evans-Asano and Vincent Baudrillard**: lovers in 2038; Jason recognises her as a grown woman who does not need his protection (Book 13, Ch971 L49).
- **Rufus Remore and Hassan Dukhtar**: Rufus introduces him as someone he is dating (Book 13, Ch1016 L23-27).
- **Lorelei Grantham and Clive Standish**: partners in Book 13 (Book 13, Ch992 L122-124).

### 3. Rivalries and standing hostilities

- **Jason and Thadwick Mercer**: Thadwick "was always fixated on me" (Book 9, Ch26 L59), partly after Jason dated Thadwick's sister (Book 4, Ch68 L177).
- **Jason's team and Team Shining Scabbard**: a friendly rivalry through the mock battles; the team is built around Sigrid with Valdis as its political core (Book 3, Ch3 L76-81).
- **Padma's team leader and Valdis**: both sword specialists with almost identical essence combinations but very different swordsmen (Book 3, Ch1 L89).
- **Rick's team and Beth's team**: they fight in the Fallen Echoes contest, where Beth is struck down by the thorn fountain (Book 2, Ch29 L74; Book 2, Ch30 L80).
- **Cole Silva and Clarissa Ventress**: Clarissa uses Sophie to provoke the rash Silva (Book 1, Ch50 L92-96).
- **Elspeth Arella and Jason**: wary opposites from Book 1, easing into polite acquaintance by Book 12 (Book 1, Ch106 L82; Book 12, Ch29 L32).
- **Kalif and Jason**: Kalif provokes Jason on first meeting and comes to work with him (Book 9, Ch24 L50-52).
- **Allayeth and Charist**: partners with different approaches to Jason (Book 10, Ch6 L17; Book 10, Ch23 L7).
- **Gilbert Bertinelli and his brothers**: he is loath to refer Jason to one of them (Book 1, Ch76 L3-5).
- **Gabrielle and Jason**: mutual friction (Book 10, Ch8 L10).

### 4. Not in the text

- No romantic tie is stated between Jason and Farrah in the lines read.
- The wiki's dating dates for Belinda and Estella (Book 12) are wiki-only (wiki).

## Teams by Era

### 1. Summary

This file lists the named adventuring teams and who was on them, by era. Roster changes (deaths, departures) are noted where the text gives them. It is level 3 because rosters run to Book 13.

### 2. Early years (Books 1-3, Greenstone and the Reaper contest)

#### Jason's team (Team Biscuit)

- The name was picked by a familiar; Marcus Xenoria wonders aloud whether it was (Book 10, Ch47 L78).
- Core roster in Book 3: Jason, Humphrey, Sophie, Belinda, Clive and Neil, planning against Valdis's team (Book 3, Ch3 L70-82).
- Gary and Farrah are Rufus's old team, as Gabriel puts it (Book 10, Ch57 L92). Farrah dies in Book 2: Rufus remembers it during the island raid (Book 2, Ch76 L8).
- Zara joins in Book 9 and is named Team Biscuit by Book 12 (Book 12, Ch0 L14; Book 12, Ch49 L7).
- By Book 11 all of Team Biscuit are Burning Violet members except Jason and Taika (Book 11, Ch68 L1067); the team withdraws in Book 12 (Book 12, Ch45 L95).

#### Other teams

- **Rick's team**: Rick, Phoebe, the Adeah twins Hannah and Claire, Jonah (until his death), Henry, and later Dustin Kettering (Book 1, Ch110 L51; Book 2, Ch29 L8; Book 9, Ch104 L54).
- **Beth's team**: Beth Cavendish, Hudson Kettering, Niko, Emily and her cousin Mose (Book 1, Ch89 L53-85).
- **Team Shining Scabbard**: built around Sigrid Freyn with Prince Valdis as its political core (Book 3, Ch3 L76-81).
- **Padma's team**: Rufus's juniors from Remore Academy (Book 3, Ch1 L87).
- **Emir's old team**: Emir, Gabriel and Arabelle Remore and Callum Morse (Book 2, Ch76 L3; Book 3, Ch24 L35).

### 3. Middle years (Books 4-9, Earth and Rimaros)

- **The Network defectors' combat team**: Asya, Greg and Kaito form the core, with Itsuki and Taika added (Book 5, Ch44 L17). Asya, Greg and Kaito die in Berlin (Book 5, Ch51 L40).
- **Storm Shredder**: led by Korinne Pescos with Orin, Kalif and Rosa, six members in all (Book 9, Ch24 L49-52; Book 9, Ch39 L80); Zara joins their vehicle (Book 9, Ch41 L119). Their name is given by Kalif (Book 9, Ch26 L69).
- **The surge expedition**: guild elites with independents and two princesses under Jeni Kavaloa (Book 7, Ch47 L33-60).

### 4. Late years (Books 10-13)

- **Moon's Edge**: six gold-rank women raised by Allayeth, led by Miriam Vance (Book 10, Ch51 L43; Book 10, Ch59 L4, L17).
- **Emir's old team reformed**: Emir, Gabriel and Arabelle with Constance replacing Callum Morse, who was not trusted for the mission (Book 10, Ch59 L4).
- **Cardinas expedition gold-rankers**: Amos Pensinata, Carlos Quilido and Hana Shavar join the teams above (Book 10, Ch59 L5).
- **Storm Shredder after the zone**: loses two members; Orin, Rosa and Korinne survive (Book 11, Ch32 L73-74; Book 11, Ch68 L378).
- **Nigel Thornton's unit**: a nine-person mercenary unit that began as a Network tactical team, now gold and silver-rank core users (Book 12, Ch3 L3-5).
- **Team Shining Scabbard in 2038**: led by Sigrid Freyn, with Valdis her husband and the Mirror King's backing (Book 12, Ch15 L8-10).
- **Neil's training**: Neil trains with Sigrid and faces her in a healer match (Book 12, Ch20 L9).

### 5. Open points

- The text does not give a full roster for Moon's Edge beyond Miriam Vance.
- Where Gary and Farrah stand in the Team Biscuit roster in Books 6-9 is covered in their character files.

## Master Timeline

### 1. How to read this timeline

- **Month counts** are months since Jason's arrival on Pallimustus ("M0"). Where the book text gives a cue it overrides the old wiki figures (see section 4); any count without a chapter-line citation is approximate. Discrepancies are listed in section 7.
- **Citation format**: every fact taken from the books carries "(Book N, ChX LY)" against `Source_Text/`. This replaces the old "[book]" marker; the register rows are in `Appendices/Source_Register.md` and the anchors in `Appendices/Source_Map.md` section 6.
- **Earth and Pallimustus run at the same rate.** The two universes are linked and their time-space is synchronised (Book 11, Ch63 L80).
- **Calendar anchors.** Taken together, the following give a calendar for the whole series:
  - Jason left Earth in **late November** and returned in **early June, a year and a half later** (Book 4, Ch3 L112).
  - His birthday is **1 April** ("April Fool's Day"); he has just turned **26** in Book 5 (Book 5, Ch20 L24-26).
  - He was **23** at arrival (Book 1, Ch25 L43; Book 13, Ch950 L29), **29** in Book 10 (Book 10, Ch33 L76), and was **born forty-four years before** the Book 12 Earth scenes (Book 12, Ch67 L113).
  - Book 13 is set in **2038** (Book 13, Ch951 L50), and mentions transformation-zone events "like those in 2020" (Book 13, Ch964 L41).
  - These fit one calendar: born 1 April 1994; arrival late November 2017 (age 23); return June 2019 (age 25); the age-26 birthday in April 2020, which is the year of the first transformation zones. The year numbers are inferred from the book statements, not stated in Book 1.
  - Further consequences: the departure from Earth (end of Book 6) falls in the autumn of 2021, the Earthlings vanish from Earth then, and Book 13 in 2038 is about sixteen and a half years later, which the characters round to "sixteen" or "seventeen". Jason's twenty-ninth birthday (1 April 2023, about M65) means Book 10, in which he says he is twenty-nine, begins at about M65 or later.
  - A Book 12 speaker says the priests Jason freed were released "around twenty years ago now" (Book 12, Ch7 L78) and another says "it's been almost twenty years" (Book 12, Ch13 L36), which fits Book 2 at about M5 (April 2018) and the Pallimustus part of Book 12 in late 2037 or early 2038.
- **Jason's age** summary: 23 at arrival; 25 on returning to Earth (derived); turns 26 on 1 April in Book 5; 29 in Book 10; 44 in Books 12-13.
- **Ranks**: iron within the first days (notes), bronze around M15 (wiki; Book 5 says he had been bronze "for a year" when he had been back nine months, Book 5, Ch3 L170, and that iron to bronze took "about a year and a quarter", Book 5, Ch3 L212), silver in Book 5 (about M28-29), gold by Book 12 ("how you got to gold rank", notes, Book 12).
- Events are grouped by book. Items marked **(Level N)** are spoiler-sensitive.

### 2. Before the series (background)

1. **Distant past**: the original Builder crafts the twin universes of Earth and Pallimustus; Pallimustus is magic-rich, Earth magic-poor. The great astral beings sanction him and a mortal messenger (Zithis Carrow Vayel, a sixteen-year-old diamond-ranker when recruited, Book 10, Ch26 L55) takes his place. **(Level 3)** The wiki's "billions of years" is unchecked.
2. **Long ago**: the great astral beings sunder the Cosmic Throne to escape regulation, replacing it with pacts. **(Level 3)**
3. **Roughly 500 years ago**: "some five centuries ago, a new kind of magic appeared" on Earth (Book 4, Ch11 L4); it is collected into secret societies, and the Network's founder, an Earth-born outworlder, sets in motion schemes that continue into the present; his familiar, Mr North, a rune spider, is betrayed with Boris's help to the early societies that become the Network (Book 13, Ch1017 L14-26). In Pallimustus, Purity is likely about to sanction himself; Knowledge interferes, Disguise takes Purity's place, and the Order of the Reaper is destroyed by the churches (Book 13, Ch1017 L16-24). **(Level 3)** The notes for Book 13 add that the founder returned to Earth with magic bargained from messengers, built the secret societies and the Grid as a pressure-release valve, and was betrayed by his familiar to US secret societies at about the time of the American Revolution (notes, Book 13; the first part is confirmed at Book 13, Ch1017 L19-28).
4. **Five years before Book 7**: the monster surge, normally due about every ten years (Book 1, Ch31 L71), is "some five years overdue" when Book 7 begins (Book 7, Ch1 L56). (An earlier version of this document said fifteen years; that figure applies instead to the Church of Knowledge building up fighting forces "over the last fifteen years or so", Book 7, Ch56 L62.) **(Level 2)**
5. **Earlier on Earth**: in 1948 local Network operatives discovered the anomalous incursion space near Saint-Étienne, and that sector of the grid has been offline for about seventy years (Book 4, Ch51 L30, L37). The Engineers of Ascension take Perth about two years before Book 4's scene, Melbourne a year later, and are pushing into Sydney (Book 4, Ch9 L76; Book 4, Ch5 L113). Network partnerships with governments and militaries have been in place "over the last few years" before the monster waves of Book 5 (Book 5, Ch13 L37). The claim that the Network reveals itself to governments "about three years before Book 4" is unchecked. **(Level 2)**

### 7. Known conflicts and open points

- **Resolved - Earthlings' arrival**: "fifteen years ago" (Book 12 characters on Pallimustus) and "seventeen years ago" (Lenora Coleman on Earth, 2038) are rounded statements about the same autumn-2021 event.
- **Resolved - Book 3's winter**: Greenstone is in the southern hemisphere, so a Book 3 opening in winter does not conflict with the Book 2 contest at about M5.
- **Resolved - surge delay**: "some five years overdue" (Book 7, Ch1 L56), not fifteen.
- **Resolved - time away**: "fifteen" in Book 12 and "sixteen" in Book 13 are roundings of the roughly sixteen and a half years between autumn 2021 and 2038.
- **Resolved - Book 5 opening**: nine months after the June 2019 return (Book 5, Ch3 L170), about March 2020.
- **Resolved - Book 3 death and Book 5 Kaito**: see section 4.
- **Open - Emi's age against the sword line**: Emi is "fifteen years old" when Rufus and Taika arrive (Book 11, Ch68 L782); she was thirteen in spring 2020, so fifteen fits late 2022 to early 2023. But "six years since you first gave it to me" (Book 11, Ch68 L115) and Jason's age of 29 (Book 10, Ch33 L76) place the departure in late 2023 or later, and Emi is "nineteen" later (Book 11, Ch68 L918). Not resolved here.
- **Narrowed - Book 12 present**: the Pallimustus chapters fit late 2037 to early 2038 by their roundings, and the Earth arrival is best placed in 2038 because Lenora counts seventeen years from the Earthlings' vanishing (Book 12, Ch67 L65) and Jota gives Jason's age as forty-four (Book 12, Ch67 L113). Book 13 is dated 2038 (Book 13, Ch951 L50). The book never states a year or the gap between the tour and the arrival.
- **Narrowed - vampire war length**: Book 13 gives "decades" (Book 13, Ch1002 L69) and "a decade" for the initiative and the team's monster fighting (Book 13, Ch1001 L6; Ch1003 L91). The renewed war is placed "two years" in at Book 13, Ch995 L69 (see `Book_13_Timeline.md`).
- **Resolved - clan hiding period**: the figures are snapshots at different dates, not a conflict. The clan "had not been heard from in two years" at the end of Book 11 (Book 11, Ch68 L2260), "half a decade" at the opening of Book 12 (Book 12, Ch1 L93), and the city of Nitra shows "more than a decade of abandonment" by the Book 12 arrival (Book 12, Ch59 L5).
- **Open - public reveal of magic**: "Less than fifteen years ago, no one knew magic existed" (Book 12, Ch2 L107) against "twenty years ago" (Book 12, Ch22 L27); likely different counting points.
- **Open - Part II of Book 11**: the intervals (a year for Lenora, almost a year for Gary, two years of team work, two years of empty road) are told on separate clocks, so no total is asserted.
- **Jason's death count** is settled by Books 5-10: apartment (first), the Builder's tower (second, Book 3), the Dinosaur King at Makassar (third, Book 5), Shako (fourth, Book 6), shown by the Church of Death's certificate in Book 7 (Book 7, Ch17 L104).

| Constance | Gold | Trained with Callum to reach gold (Book 9, Ch50 L51) |
| Nik | Gold | Gold rank at Nik's celebration (Book 13, Ch997 L11) |

### 10. The Book 11 Part II clock

Part II mixes several threads, each told on its own clock (see Book_11_Timeline.md section 7): a year for Lenora in the monitoring room (Book 11, Ch68 L412), almost a year for Gary (L703), two years of team work (L1034), two years more on Earth (L1341) and two years on the empty road (L2244). The text does not add these into one total.

**Working convention for the compendium** (an editorial choice, not a book statement):

1. Treat Jason's void departure as late 2023, following Jason's age of twenty-nine (Book 10, Ch33 L76) and the "six years since you first gave it to me" line (Book 11, Ch68 L115).
2. Start the Earth-side threads from Rufus and Taika's arrival, shortly after that date, and run them forward: Lenora's year and Gary's almost-year overlap at the start, the team's two years and the further two years follow, so the Earth-side threads end several years after the departure and well before 2038.
3. Treat Emi's "fifteen years old" at Rufus's arrival (Book 11, Ch68 L782) as the single outlier. It fits late 2022 to early 2023 and conflicts with convention point 1 (see Open_Questions).
4. Treat the void threads (the empty road, the nested soul) as running on Jason's own clock, which the text does not tie to Earth's, and add nothing to the Earth total.

This convention produces no contradiction with Book 12's "almost twenty years" since arrival (Book 12, Ch13 L36), which counts from late 2017 to late 2037 or early 2038.

### 11. Corrections already recorded

The month-count corrections are in section 4 and the resolved and open points in section 7. Further corrections made in later passes: Cressida Vane is killed in Book 1 (Book 1, Ch97 L122); Akari Asano is married to Itsuki Tiwari (Book 13, Ch1004 L5); Clarissa Ventress is reported dead by Book 3 (Book 3, Ch16 L7); Vitesse's magic density is narrowed to a rank band (Book 1, Ch30 L43-44).

## The Boko Evacuation (Book 12)

### 1. Summary

Boko is destroyed on the day an assassin spears Jason's avatar there. Jason uses his aura to lift the city's people out and drop them in the desert, holds his draining power while the containment ritual is built, and dies in the blast. A messenger army then descends on the survivors until Jason's ghost-fire phoenix form rises from the crater. The survivors are sheltered in his astral kingdom.

### 2. Before

- **Li Li Mei** has lived in Boko for years; someone zeroing in on her sends her fleeing to a storehouse, where she meets Jason (Book 12, Ch30 L71-81). Boko is the origin of the anti-intellectual movement (Book 12, Ch29 L65).
- **Jason's arrival**: Jason reached Greenstone quietly days before the official arrival (Book 12, Ch27 L12). In Boko he meets Li Mei with Estella and Belinda (Book 12, Ch31 L3-12).

### 3. The attack

- **The assassin**: a man in black and red armour appears behind Jason; a slab of black-red metal is run through his body (Book 12, Ch32 L13). The blade is [Lesser Celestial Gorger (broken)], gold rank (Book 12, Ch34 L35).
- **The alert**: a System Alert announces a magical incident; occupants will be evacuated immediately; clergy are told to evacuate holy ground (Book 12, Ch32 L15-17). A regional alert tells silver-rank-and-below adventurers not to approach, and gold-rankers not to approach until after the blast (Book 12, Ch32 L24-26).
- **Jason's message**: "Got attacked. Going to blow up and take some or all of Boko with me. Getting people out, need wide-area containment ritual" (Book 12, Ch32 L29).
- **Shade's report**: the weapon drains Jason's power, which is infinite, until either the weapon or the avatar cannot contain it (Book 12, Ch32 L42-43).

### 4. The evacuation

- **Jason's aura**: aura floods out; the whole population floats up and is moved away from him and his attacker (Book 12, Ch32 L19-21). He drops the residents in the desert, as far from the city walls as he could (Book 12, Ch32 L66).
- **The ritual**: Clive and Farrah lead an improvised wide-area containment ritual with Belinda, Farrah and Humphrey's readings, built in the sky from Onslow's shell (Book 12, Ch32 L37-54). Danielle, Gabriel and Arabelle organise order and healing (Book 12, Ch32 L46-47).
- **The toll**: the aura becomes a spiritual wildfire; many normal-rank evacuees, mostly the very old and very young, die of haemorrhages and heart attacks (Book 12, Ch33 L5-6). Most of Boko's ninety thousand people are evacuated (Book 12, Ch33 L4).

### 5. The blast and the invasion

- **The blast**: when the containment gives out the outer regions are rubble and the space within is a hole (Book 12, Ch33 L3). A System alert reads "[System Administrator] assassinated. The Hegemon has arisen. Beware his wrath" (Book 12, Ch33 L9-10).
- **The messenger army**: four Voices of the Will watch an assassin kill Jason and say "It is time ... for an example to be made" (Book 12, Ch32 L49-53). Massive portals open and disgorge messengers by the thousand (Book 12, Ch33 L4, L7).
- **The phoenix**: a vast dark bird, speckled with lights like a starry night and limned in silver flames, rises from the crater and batters the messengers into disorder (Book 12, Ch33 L11-12). The ghost fire phoenix arcs through the host (Book 12, Ch33 L16).

### 6. Aftermath

- **Shelter**: only Jason's astral kingdom has the space and resources to shelter a city's worth of people (Book 12, Ch36 L3). He builds an oasis city for them, later named New Water (Book 12, Ch36 L4; Book 12, Ch39 L61).
- **The crater**: the coastal side collapses and becomes a harbour with floating temples as islands (Book 12, Ch39 L37).
- **Diplomacy**: Jamis Fran Muskar apologises for the deaths in Boko; Jason refuses a proposal to blunt his fury by giving up areas, and refuses to slaughter a quarter of a million messengers to restore his ghost phoenix form (Book 12, Ch35 L6-8, L66, L84, L88).
- **Later**: portals again open over the crater and messengers pour out, never close to the survivors (Book 12, Ch36 L6).

### 7. Open questions

- The exact number of dead; the text gives only that many of the very old and very young died (Book 12, Ch33 L6).

## The Messenger War (Books 7-13)

### 1. Summary

The messenger war is the long conflict between the winged servants of the astral kings and the people of Pallimustus, with Jason caught between them as a would-be astral king. It begins with the invasion of the south in Book 9, includes the Battle of Yaresh and the Cardinas expedition, and ends with the reprisal at Boko and an uneasy peace in Books 12-13. This file sets out the sequence; the Battle of Yaresh and the Cardinas expedition have their own era guides.

### 2. Before the war

- **How messengers move**: Clive explains that messengers create dimensional channels (Book 7, Ch36 L47). Messenger architecture is obsessed with circles (Book 9, Ch55 L3).
- **Preparation**: the noble houses expect the conflict with the messengers "to start" and grab what they can while they can (Book 9, Ch13 L52). The vast majority of astral kings are messengers, and a war against them is in the offing (Book 9, Ch23 L44).

### 3. The campaign

- **Yaresh (Book 9)**: Marek Nior Vargas leads the breach force over the entertainment district (Book 9, Ch86 L16); Jes Fin Kaal, the Voice of the Will, directs from a circular tower (Book 9, Ch66 L3). The battle is covered in ../Era_Guides/Battle_of_Yaresh.md.
- **Why the southern front matters**: the messengers are fighting on multiple fronts (Book 9, Ch52 L74) and use apocalypse beasts as weapons (Book 9, Ch62 L26).
- **After the battle (Books 9-10)**: Marek, Tera and others become Jason's captives; Jason tells Marek his story about the war guilt clause in the peace treaty after the Great War (Book 10, Ch4 L31). Marek works on plans for an uprising among the captives (Book 10, Ch42 L4).
- **Cardinas (Books 10-11)**: the messengers' device and soul forge attempt, covered in ../Era_Guides/Cardinas_Expedition_and_Zone.md; Boris says Vesta Carmis Zell would never accept an Unorthodoxy member (Book 11, Ch24 L85).
- **A withdrawal**: by Book 11 the messengers are done in the region, their numbers and resources too low to defend (Book 11, Ch68 L361).

### 4. The reprisal (Book 12)

- **Boko**: four Voices of the Will watch the assassination and say "It is time ... for an example to be made" (Book 12, Ch32 L49-53). Massive portals open over the ruins and disgorge an army (Book 12, Ch33 L4). See Boko_Evacuation.md.
- **The Council of Kings**: Jamis Fran Muskar is told "We are all astral kings" and that the Council may guide but does not rule (Book 12, Ch33 L55). He apologises for the deaths in Boko; Jason refuses to blunt his fury by giving up areas or to slaughter a quarter of a million messengers (Book 12, Ch35 L6, L66, L88).
- **Later portals**: more messengers pour out over the crater but never reach the survivors (Book 12, Ch36 L6).

### 5. Aftermath (Book 13)

- **Rehabilitation**: someone is wanted to rehabilitate the messengers whom Jamis Fran Muskar surrendered to Jason (Book 13, Ch973 L24). Jali Corrik Fen is the caretaker of the messengers living with the Asano clan (Book 13, Ch973 L85).
- **Jamis on McKean**: Farrah says Muskar might not think McKean is dangerous (Book 13, Ch1003 L25).

### 6. Who is where

- **Messengers**: Kaal, Marek, Hess Jor Nasala, Fal Vin Garath, Tera Jun Casta, Jali Corrik Fen; the astral kings Vesta Carmis Zell and Jamis Fran Muskar.
- **Jason's side**: Jason, his team, Yaresh's gold-rankers, the Church of the Healer and the Adventure Society.

### 7. Open questions

- The full list of astral kings on the Council and their stakes.
- How the war ended for the messengers' other fronts.

## The One Day War (War of Four Cities)

### 1. Summary

During the Rimaros monster surge, the Builder cult sends mobile cities against the Storm Kingdom: a ground city that walks south, an underwater city and a flying fortress-city that appears over Livaros. The adventurers answer with six diamond-rankers, gods' miracles and a single true bomb carried into the flying city. The war is later called the War of Four Cities or the One Day War (Book 7, Ch66 L27).

### 2. Warning signs

- **Rumours and reports**: Rick Geller reports a "ground city" that moves on thousands of thick legs, which started moving south several weeks earlier (Book 7, Ch59 L124). It passed through the arid lands and the Arkivahl Desert; two cities have already fallen, with news several days old (Book 7, Ch59 L127-129).
- **The assessment**: at least four diamond-rankers are needed to attack it, five or more would be better (Book 7, Ch59 L130).
- **A second city**: an underwater city is already in the kingdom and on the move; the two converge on the northern reaches (Book 7, Ch59 L131).
- **The Builder's invasion platforms** appear worldwide (Book 7, Ch8 L36). Soramir and Jason look to Dawn, who answers "No" (Book 7, Ch59 L133-134).

### 3. Preparation

- **Rallying**: the royal family, the Irios house and the royal guard are reassured by the gods' help (Book 7, Ch65 L18); Archbishop Rimmon says each of the gods will do what they can, with the Archbishops of War and Ocean empowering defences and the sea (Book 7, Ch65 L17-19).
- **Soramir's warning**: "many of us will fall today" (Book 7, Ch65 L20).
- **The weapon**: many teams, Jason's team among them, are handed devices; only one is the true bomb, so the cult will have to guess (Book 7, Ch65 L21). Jason's team is given a dummy; Keel's crystal turns red to confirm it (Book 7, Ch65 L70-75). Liara holds the true device (Book 7, Ch65 L77).
- **The magic defences**: Farrah is a formation magic expert, wanted to breach the Builder city's defences (Book 7, Ch65 L27).
- **Travis's weapon**: Jason brought Travis into the fold to produce the weapon that destroyed the flying city (Book 7, Ch66 L44).

### 4. The battle

- **The kraken city**: the floating city is "actually a city-sized kraken construct", with ten panels opening into tentacles each a diamond-rank construct, swatting airships from the sky (Book 7, Ch64 L10-12).
- **The diamond-rankers**: the adventurers have six, with Soramir conspicuously absent (Book 7, Ch64 L14). Each faces a Builder cult diamond-ranker, and the clashes spell doom for lower-rankers nearby.
- **The lower ranks**: their objective is to invade the city, fight to its core mechanisms and destroy them, while the cult aims to bleed them (Book 7, Ch64 L15-16). The adventurers' quality tells over time (Book 7, Ch64 L17).
- **Barrier**: a diamond-ranker slays the lamprey and turns to breach the defence screen, with gold-rankers pounding it (Book 7, Ch64 L18).
- **The flying city**: a rainbow light above Rimaros disgorges a city in the sky, a stone disc with a ritual circle on its underside that fires a beam at Livaros; the gods' intervention shields Livaros (Book 7, Ch65 L28-30; Book 7, Ch66 L34). Jason notes "That is a Builder fortress-city, appearing over Livaros" (Book 7, Ch64 L72).
- **The raid on Arnote**: while forces are mobilised, pirates raid Arnote, and Pelli fights the pirate captain outside the town of Kasilaro (Book 7, Ch64 L20-25). The raiders who enter the town are struck down by black, withering death (Book 7, Ch64 L28-29).
- **The bomb**: Liara, with the siblings Ledev and Jana, carry the true device through the underground industrial depths; they join a mixed group including Vesper and Jeni Kavaloa (Book 7, Ch65 L77-80). Vesper tells her "We're close now," and the group draws attention so Liara can sneak the rest of the way (Book 7, Ch65 L83-87). Liara feels Vesper's aura wink out (Book 7, Ch65 L88). Ledev stays behind (Book 7, Ch65 L90).

### 5. Aftermath

- **A month later** the Storm Kingdom and the Adventure Society are still adjusting (Book 7, Ch66 L27).
- **Dead**: Ledev and Vesper both died saving the city, and Jeni Kavaloa died fighting alongside Vesper (Book 7, Ch66 L36).
- **Effect on adventuring**: quotas are raised and safety standards lowered; bronze-rankers were kept out of the war and are combined into larger groups sent on silver-rank missions (Book 7, Ch66 L29).
- **The other cities**: the kraken city sank to the sea floor; the flying city fell and Livaros was shielded; only minor coastal flooding hit Provo and Arnote (Book 7, Ch66 L34).
- **Jason's part**: he is at the periphery of the events; Arabelle reminds him that his intervention persuaded Dawn to move and that Travis's weapon destroyed the flying city (Book 7, Ch66 L37-44).

### 6. Open questions

- The exact casualty numbers and which diamond-rankers fought.
- The fate of the ground city beyond "burned into desolation" (Book 7, Ch66 L33).

## The Vampire War (Books 5-13)

### 1. Summary

The Earth vampire war runs in two phases: a first war that "ended without conclusion" when both sides were exhausted and the vampires got nuclear weapons, then a renewed war that was in full swing again by the Book 13 symposium and ends at McKean's castle. This file collects the duration statements. For the events, see ../Era_Guides/Earth_Vampire_War.md.

### 2. Duration statements

- **The first war**: it "ended without conclusion" when both sides were exhausted and the vampires got nuclear weapons (Book 13, Ch987 L63).
- **The renewed war**: it was "back in full swing" (Book 13, Ch988 L26), and Anna says military forces operate out of Asano territory again (Book 13, Ch993 L81).
- **The symposium**: a character places it "two years into the renewed vampire war" (Book 13, Ch995 L69).
- **Decades**: Simon McKean says the conflict has been fought "off and on for decades" (Book 13, Ch1002 L69).
- **The end**: Jason says the operation will bring it to a final conclusion (Book 13, Ch1002 L64), and it ended in the months before the farewell (Book 13, Ch1023 L12).
- **Not known**: the first war's length (Open_Questions item 19).

### 3. The start (Books 5-6)

- The old vampires are woken by blood imbued with reality-core power, and sleep again once it runs out (Book 5, Ch55 L92; Book 5, Ch51 L127). Russia and Europe suffer massive vampiric occupation (Book 5, Ch66 L8).
- In Book 6 the vampires of the Saint-Étienne zone are partly allied with Jason; they later abandon France (Book 6, Ch47 L5).

### 4. The détente and the purge

- Under Elizabeth the vampires establish a détente: every major city hides vampires, and bombings in Europe are answered by assassinations in four world capitals (Book 11, Ch68 L1489).
- Humanity tries to kill Elizabeth with a modified nuclear missile that floods a region with magical sunlight (Book 11, Ch68 L1490).
- Jason's purge of reality-core remnants in Book 12 (Book 12, Ch5 L70).

### 5. The final offensive

- Belgrade and Multan (Book 13, Ch1007 L3-16); McKean's castle and the blood vine (Book 13, Ch1008 L20-27; Book 13, Ch1011 L18-44); the last vampire lord (Book 13, Ch1013 L34).

## Era Guide: The Battle of Yaresh (Book 9)

### 1. Summary

After a four-month journey south from Rimaros, Jason's convoy reaches the rainforest elf city of Yaresh as messengers besiege it. The Church of Knowledge gathers an army in the background, the messengers use apocalypse beasts and world-taker worms as weapons, and the battle ends with a breach the messengers' commander Marek has to concede. Jason's identity as an astral king comes out, and Marek and Tera become his captives.

### 2. The world at the start

- **The journey**: the trip will take "about four months" (Book 9, Ch26 L26); the convoy stays at Rajoras for a few days (Book 9, Ch29 L13) and clears Cartise's ruins on the way (Book 9, Ch31 L11).
- **Orders from Knowledge**: a priest of the Church of Knowledge tells Humphrey's team to follow the Adventure Society's orders for a couple of weeks, after which the church will requisition them for the main conflict (Book 9, Ch42 L57). Clive says Knowledge's forces are mobilising (Book 9, Ch42 L80).
- **Yaresh**: the walls are a line of massive trees with glossy black stone between (Book 9, Ch43 L33). Jason says "See you in two weeks" (Book 9, Ch43 L72) and returns to the city's defence. Hana Shavar runs the refugee camp (Book 9, Ch74 L43).
- **The messengers**: the messenger architecture is obsessed with circles (Book 9, Ch55 L3); Jes Fin Kaal, the Voice of the Will, leads them (Book 9, Ch66 L3).

### 3. Key events

- **Messenger agents in the city**: Benella presents Jason to Kaal as a threat (Book 9, Ch56 L4-20); Fal Vin Garath calls Shade "Reaper spawn" (Book 9, Ch52 L32).
- **Apocalypse beasts and worms**: Carlos suspects a heat-consuming parasite with a swarm hive mind (Book 9, Ch57 L16); "[Inexorable Doom] on [World-Taker Worm]" (Book 9, Ch58 L45); the messengers know the apocalypse beasts and use them as weapons (Book 9, Ch62).
- **Defence plans**: the two cloud palaces are reconfigured into defence bunkers (Book 9, Ch76 L88); Hana directs the clergy away from Jason's bunker (Book 9, Ch80 L7).
- **The trigger**: an Adventure Society functionary hides his anger behind an aura mask (Book 9, Ch77 L13); a naga egg is triggered in the city (see ../../06_Places/Yaresh.md).
- **The breach**: Marek Nior Vargas leads the breach force over the entertainment district (Book 9, Ch86 L16); the breach is a trap (Book 9, Ch96 L14). Eilaf Hayel commands the defence of the entertainment district (Book 9, Ch94 L3).
- **Intervention**: Raythe tells Schaat "Leave Asano be. Turn around and leave this city" (Book 9, Ch97 L74); Schaat is found dead (Book 9, Ch98 L4-5).
- **The duel**: Tera Jun Casta challenges Jason; Jason's last word stops her dead (Book 9, Ch101 L18).
- **The end**: the command council advises withdrawal (Book 9, Ch102 L9); Marek orders his people in (Book 9, Ch103 L64) and later asks Jason to wait (Book 9, Ch104 L5). In the weeks following the battle, countless tons of rubble are repurposed to rebuild the city (Book 9, Ch103 L85).

### 4. Who is where

- **Jason's team**: the convoy, Taika and Zara among them (Book 9, Ch41 L119); Rufus, Sophie and Jason as mobile responders (Book 9, Ch79 L21).
- **Allies**: Charist and Allayeth, Hana Shavar, Marcus Xenoria later, the gold-rankers of Yaresh.
- **Messengers**: Kaal, Marek, Hess Jor Nasala, Fal Vin Garath, Tera; their astral king is Vesta Carmis Zell (Book 9, Ch78 L82).
- **The wider world**: Knowledge's army gathering (Book 9, Ch42 L80); Dawn's recording supplies the real list of auxiliaries (Book 9, Ch6 L41).

### 5. Known and unknown

- **Known by the end**: a healer realises Jason is a silver-rank astral king (Book 9, Ch62 L30-34).
- **Unknown**: the messengers' real aim, which is the soul forge beneath Yaresh (revealed in Book 10; spoiler level 3).

### 6. Dangers and hooks

Besieging messengers, apocalypse beasts, world-taker worms, infiltrators in the Adventure Society. Hooks belong in ../../10_Roleplay_Support/Plot_Hooks.md.

## Era Guide: The Builder Cult in Greenstone (Books 2-3)

### 1. Summary

For about a year after the Reaper trials, a hidden cult of the Builder works inside Greenstone's aristocracy and through the church of Purity. It implants star seeds, suborns Thadwick Mercer and others, and prepares to claim an astral space. Jason's team learns of it in Book 2 and breaks it in Book 3, ending in the astral space the cult built and the death of Jason.

### 2. The world at the start (Book 2, about M3 to M5)

- **Where things stand**: Jason is an iron-ranker in Greenstone; Farrah has just died covering civilians (Book 1, Ch113 L41); the Adventure Society campus holds "a continual series of memorial services" (Book 2, Ch6 L3).
- **The first sign**: Cassandra says her brother Thadwick "woke up on the way back" and is "different" (Book 2, Ch4 L24); Henry Geller is among the missing faces (Book 2, Ch4 L7). A Continental Council inquiry team arrives (Book 2, Ch10 L51).
- **Rumours in the upper crust** about Jonah, Thadwick and the others disrupt Greenstone's aristocracy (Book 2, Ch16 L75).

### 3. Key events

#### Book 2

- **The star seed**: Danielle, Emir, Thalia, Arella and the archbishop of Purity witness Jonah Geller's death; the archbishop says a star seed was implanted in the boy and that star seeds are creations of entities that exist only in the deep astral (Book 2, Ch21 L19-28). Clive says he has simulated the enemy's goal: to reinforce an astral space and sever it from the world (Book 2, Ch21 L123).
- **The enemy's shape**: clockwork kings are creatures native to the world the Builder created, which make clockwork cores for constructs (Book 2, Ch25 L35-41).
- **Aristocrats in the cult**: Thalia reports that three star-seed survivors are awake with limited recollection (Book 2, Ch36 L36); a hooded cultist posing as the foreman follows a woman, and the archbishop rebukes the cult's failures (Book 2, Ch37 L24, L31, L33). Guards have stood at Thadwick's door for weeks (Book 2, Ch41 L67).
- **While the iron-rankers are away**: in Greenstone, Thalia is uneasy because most iron-rankers left a few days earlier; in the Mercers' underground black parlour, Timos berates Thadwick, whose use as an infiltrator is at an end (Book 2, Ch59 L3-22).
- **The strike**: a small force of three gold-rankers, six silvers and a dozen bronzes, including Gabriel and Arabelle Remore, hits the cult's island; Timos runs for the nearest portal device (Book 2, Ch76 L3, L58).

#### Book 3

- **Evacuation**: Zato, the last silver-ranker in the cult's local forces, leads the survivors off the island (Book 3, Ch7 L88-89).
- **Jason's capture**: Cole Silva and Lucian Lamprey orchestrate Jason's kidnapping and star seed implantation (Book 9, Ch2 L84); he is held in a stone box, emaciated and bloodied (Book 3, Ch17 L3; Book 3, Ch20 L9).
- **The war council**: Jason's team and allies meet as a war council for the anti-Builder effort (Book 3, Ch31 L56).
- **Into the astral space**: the team arrives on one of twelve portal towers ringing the city (Book 3, Ch35 L4; Book 3, Ch36 L36); a legendary-set site is a subterranean forge (Book 3, Ch42 L6). The church of Purity arrives at the Vane estate through a portal, fifty-eight in all (Book 3, Ch54 L19). Hendren dissolves under transcendent light (Book 3, Ch59 L126).
- **The truth of the place**: Clive says the astral space is artificial, "a giant boarding vessel" (Book 3, Ch65 L79).
- **The ending**: the Builder grabs Jason by the face (Book 3, Ch67 L39); Zato is defeated (Book 3, Ch69 L42); the Builder, the World-Phoenix and the Reaper negotiate (Book 3, Ch69 L279). Jason's soul is vouchsafed on his death (Book 3, Ch69 L378).

### 4. Who is where

- **Jason**: iron in Book 2, bronze by Book 3 (Book 3, Ch45 L90); dies at the climax (Book 3, Ch69).
- **Humphrey, Clive, Sophie, Belinda, Neil**: the team that enters the astral space with him (Book 3, Ch34 L16-28).
- **The cult**: Zato, Timos, Thadwick, Dougall and the abandoned vessel the Builder takes up (Book 3, Ch51 L85-93).
- **Purity**: the archbishop Nicolas Hendren and the priestess Anisa Lasalle, with fifty-eight others at the Vane estate (Book 3, Ch54 L19).
- **Greenstone's powers**: Thalia Mercer and Danielle Geller; Elspeth Arella; the Duke; Adris Dorgan as the effective mayor of Old City (Book 3, Ch26 L76).

### 5. Known and unknown

- **Known to Jason's team**: the cult exists, star seeds, and the aim to seal an astral space (Book 2, Ch21 L123).
- **Unknown to them until later**: that Purity is largely run by Disguise and that Knowledge arranged much of it (spoiler level 3; see ../../10_Roleplay_Support/Spoiler_Management.md).
- **Open**: how Thadwick was recruited in detail; the cult's full numbers.

### 6. Dangers and hooks

Clockwork constructs and cores; cult members hiding in plain sight among aristocrats; star seeds that can make a person into a vessel; a siege of the Vane estate. Plot hooks for this era belong in ../../10_Roleplay_Support/Plot_Hooks.md.

---

## Era Guide: The Cardinas Expedition and Zone (Books 10-11)

### 1. Summary

A descending expedition goes beneath Yaresh to stop the messengers' device from turning the city's natural array into a soul forge. In Book 10 the allies reach the brightheart city of Cardinas, face the Church of Undeath and Hero's divine power; in Book 11 the failed forge becomes a transformation zone that Jason must claim territory by territory. It ends with Jason holding the astral throne, gate and soul forge, and with Rufus and Taika leaving for Earth.

### 2. The world at the start

- **After the battle**: Yaresh is rebuilding, the messengers are Jason's captives, and the Adventure Society is deciding whether to revoke his membership (Book 10, Ch2 L65; Book 10, Ch30 L63).
- **The device**: the messengers give Jason a device that is meant to turn the natural array into a soul forge (Book 10, Ch57 L3, L53); Clive says the messengers want this and cannot do it alone because the place corrupts them (Book 10, Ch72 L65).
- **Allies**: Musin Heath presides at the meetings (Book 10, Ch9 L38); Marcus Xenoria names Jason operations commander (Book 10, Ch60 L14); the gold-rank participants include Amos, Carlos and Hana Shavar (Book 10, Ch59 L5).

### 3. Key events

#### Book 10: the descent

- **The descent**: Jason and Kaal go over the operation to descend the access shaft (Book 10, Ch17 L39). Brightheart stone-shapers guide thousands into switchback queues for the portal (Book 10, Ch76 L45).
- **Cardinas**: ruled from the Citadel of Pillars (Book 10, Ch65 L3); Beaufort heads the Builder cult's forces as an uneasy ally (Book 10, Ch65 L30). Lorenn says the citadel chamber is the site of the echo array (Book 10, Ch72 L58).
- **Undeath**: Garth Larosse, a priest of Undeath about nine feet tall (Book 10, Ch80 L42). Death appears as a stocky, middle-aged woman in a colourful dress (Book 10, Ch82 L62) and names the pact "Death Pact: The Sanctity of Death" (Book 10, Ch83 L61).
- **Hero**: Gary greets "Lord Hero" (Book 10, Ch86 L19); a divine forge golem stands over twice Gary's height (Book 10, Ch87 L50). Gary and the avatar stare at each other like kaiju (Book 10, Ch91 L46).
- **The tree**: the birthing tree is the result of a failed attempt to create a soul forge (Book 10, Ch80 L29). Clive and Farrah overlook the ring of ritual circles round the tree (Book 10, Ch92 L14).

#### Book 11: the zone

- **A third zone**: Jason's third transformation zone, unified by claiming all non-central territories (Book 11, Ch1 L15, L39). A replica of Casselton Beach occupies one (Book 11, Ch5 L8).
- **Battles**: the Undeath priests fall quickly (Book 11, Ch4 L21); Garth throws off his robes (Book 11, Ch24-26); Jason fights him in a warped castle (Book 11, Ch30-31).
- **Factions**: each faction has Builder cultists, Undeath priests or brighthearts leading messengers (Book 11, Ch9 L108). Lorus Durrum tries to reconcile the Builder cult and the brighthearts (Book 11, Ch10 L12). Territory holding follows Lorenn's rules (Book 11, Ch17 L27).
- **Nik**: a four-foot humanoid rabbit Jason brings into being when his soul realm becomes a zone (Book 11, Ch61 L16); he is "six months old" in the zone (Book 11, Ch50 L15) and calls the structure a weather machine, not a satellite weapon (Book 11, Ch50 L11).
- **Boris**: reveals himself as Unorthodoxy and tells the astral-king story (Book 11, Ch24 L85; Book 11, Ch25 L51); he says the process to become an astral king takes years (Book 11, Ch43 L131).
- **Gary**: drank from the Cup of Heroes; Jason offers to replace the divine power (Book 11, Ch48 L22; Book 11, Ch48 L30).
- **Reintegration**: Jason separates the natural array, the soul forge and the tree and claims the forge (Book 11, Ch60 L43-46; Book 11, Ch61 L19-21). The forest city has a soul of its own, like Nik (Book 11, Ch61 L16). Lorenn gathers her people in the new brightheart home (Book 11, Ch62 L89).
- **The Cosmic Throne**: Velius says the throne must be left empty as a neutral arbiter (Book 11, Ch65 L8).
- **Departure**: Boris can take two people to Earth, Taika among them (Book 11, Ch66 L89).

### 4. Who is where

- **Jason** in the zone, leaving his body in a cloud chair during soul battles (Book 11, Ch35 L39).
- **The team**: Humphrey, Sophie, Clive, Belinda, Neil, Gary, Rufus, Taika and Farrah; Zara, Dustin, Korinne and Moon's Edge (Book 11, Ch21 L9; Book 11, Ch32 L75).
- **Local forces**: Lorenn and the brighthearts; Miriam Vance as co-commander (Book 11, Ch19 L56).
- **Enemies**: the Church of Undeath, Builder cultists, messengers.
- **Earth**: the clan holds two domains, Saint-Étienne and near Nitra (Book 11, Ch36 L3).

### 5. Known and unknown

- **Known**: the soul forge is the third part of an astral kingdom (Book 8, Ch65 L94); Boris is Unorthodoxy (Book 11, Ch24 L85).
- **Unknown**: how long the zone lasted (see Open_Questions on the timing, Book 11 Part II), and what Gary's ultimate bargain with Hero is.

### 6. Dangers and hooks

Territories that must be claimed while enemies are present, a corrupted tree, gods acting through avatars, and a city of survivors that needs a home. Hooks belong in ../../10_Roleplay_Support/Plot_Hooks.md.
